articles.title: 2019–20 FC Nitra season
articles.text:
2019–20 FC Nitra season

The 2019–20 season was FC Nitra's third consecutive season in the top division of Slovak football. The club finished 11th in the regular season and subsequently competed in the relegation group, where it finished bottom of the table in 12th place, one point behind the team above them. FC Nitra therefore faced second-tier champions FK Dubnica in a relegation play-off to retain their place in the top flight. Nitra won the tie and secured their top-flight status. The top-flight season was suspended in March 2020 following the completion of the regular season due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The clubs voted on whether the competition should resume, with the majority ultimately favouring its continuation in a shortened format. However, stadiums were only permitted to operate at 50% of their capacity.
The club experienced financial difficulties during the season, which were expected to be resolved through the involvement of Ukrainian investors. However, their investment proved unsuccessful, and they subsequently withdrew from the club. Their involvement ultimately worsened the club's financial situation.
The club went through as many as five different head coaches during the season, with each change prompted by unsatisfactory results.
In the Slovak Cup, the club reached the quarter-finals, where they were eliminated by ViOn Zlaté Moravce on penalties.

articles.title: 1933–34 Newark Bears season
articles.text:
1933–34 Newark Bears season

The 1933–34 Newark Bears season was arguably seen as the first professional basketball season played by the Newark Bears (who sometimes were referred to as the Newark Joe Fays) franchise in Newark, New Jersey, as well as their first and only full (professional) season played under that particular name. When the American Basketball League was revived in 1933 by Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer John J. O'Brien after he previously was managing the revived version of the Metropolitan Basketball League, O'Brien had the Newark Bears become the only independent team get invited into the revived version of the ABL after he previously invited the revived Eastern Basketball League's two best teams from the previous season in the EBL champion Trenton Moose and runner-up Philadelphia Sphas (the latter of whom previously competed in the original ABL as the Philadelphia Quakers / Warriors) to join up with five teams that were playing in the revived version of the Metropolitan Basketball League in the MBL champion Brooklyn Jewels, the Brooklyn Visitations (who previously participated in the original version of the ABL), the Bronx Americans (who previously played under multiple names the previous season), the Hoboken Thourots (formerly the Hoboken Lisas, though they later became the Camden Brewers and then the New Britain Palaces), and the Union City Reds to create the new eight team ABL that would essentially be the same version of the original ABL from the late 1920s and early 1930s, but with a few differences in terms of rules and scope in mind for this iteration of the ABL. During their first season as a professional team in the ABL, the Bears would end up performing rather poorly throughout the season, with the first half of the season resulting in them getting a below-average 9–17 record for a 7th place finish ahead of only the aforementioned Hoboken Thourots turned Camden Brewers turned New Britain Palaces. While the second half of the season would see them perform a little bit better, they'd still end up having a below-average record (albeit with a 4–5 finish this time around instead) that resulted in them being ahead of only the Union City Reds, the Bronx Americans, and the Brooklyn Visitations for a fifth place finish. As a result of their poor overall record, Newark would fail to qualify for the ABL's championship series for this season.

articles.title: 2018 WPT Andorra Open
articles.text:
2018 WPT Andorra Open

The 2018 Andorra Open (officially 2018 World Padel Tour Vallbanc Andorra La Vella Open) was the ninth tournament of the sixth season organized by World Padel Tour, the most prestigious padel circuit at the time.
In the women's category, Mapi and Majo Sánchez reached their seventh consecutive final (out of eight possible), where they faced the world's number three pair, Alejandra Salazar and Marta Marrero, for the second time in 2018. In the title match, the world number ones defeated Marrero and Salazar, with twins Majo and Mapi Sánchez claiming their fourth title of the season and successfully defending the title they had won in Andorra the previous year.
In the men's category, Cristian Gutiérrez and Franco Stupaczuk reached their first final of the season, where they faced the top seeds. In the title match, Maxi Sánchez and Sanyo Gutiérrez, playing their seventh final of the season out of nine possible, defeated Gutiérrez and Stupaczuk to claim their fifth title of the year and further narrow the gap to world number one Pablo Lima. With this victory, Maxi and Sanyo claimed their first title as a pair in Andorra, while Sanyo successfully defended the title he had won the previous year.


== Relevant Data ==


=== Belasteguin loses the world N.1 ranking for the first time in 16 years ===
Fernando Belasteguín's absence due to an injury sustained in the previous tournament, combined with Pablo Lima's participation in Andorra alongside Marcello Jardim, has made the Brazilian the new world number one, leading by just 180 points. This marked a historic moment in padel, as it is the first time in 16 years (a total of 200 months) that Belasteguin has lost the top spot in the world rankings.
Lima, who was eliminated in the quarterfinals of the Andorra tournament, now held 13,440 points following the ranking update, with Sanyo Gutiérrez in second place, trailing by 165 points.

articles.title: Ajatushautomo Kompassi
articles.text:
Ajatushautomo Kompassi

Ajatushautomo Kompassi (English: "Compass Think Tank") is a Finnish think tank focusing on the research and promotion of Christian democracy. Founded in 2016, it operates close to the Christian Democrats, a political party.


== Activities ==
The purpose of Ajatushautomo Kompassi is to promote social research, discussion and decision-making that develops Finnish society based on Christian democratic values. The association strives to promote human dignity and the overall well-being of people in its activities.
The think tank arranges seminars and has published a number of books. In 2018, Kompassi called for reforming Finland's social security system.
Kompassi is a member of Sallux, the official European political foundation for the European Christian Political Party (ECPP). The think tank is also a partner of the Wilfried Martens Centre for European Studies, the official European political foundation for the European People's Party. Additionally, Kompassi works with other think tanks, both European and international.
The think tank's executive director is Tommi Terä, and the association's board chair is Annika Lyytikäinen.


== Funding ==
In late 2023, the Konrad Adenauer Foundation gave Kompassi a €15,000 grant. In 2024, the think tank had a surplus of €84,0865. Kompassi, like many other think tanks in Finland, received funding from the Ministry of Education and Culture, receiving a €14,000 grant in 2018. The Ministry of Education and Culture's funding was discontinued on 1 January 2025.

articles.title: 2026 Multan train derailment
articles.text:
2026 Multan train derailment

On 13 October 2026, the Rehman Baba Express passenger train derailed in Multan, Punjab, Pakistan, killing seven people and injuring over 50 others. 


== Background ==
The Rehman Baba Express is a passenger train operated daily by Pakistan Railways between Karachi and Peshawar. The train was inaugurated on 23 December 2018 by former Minister for Railways Sheikh Rasheed Ahmad at Peshawar Cantonment railway station. The train similarly derailed near Hyderabad on 13 May 2022 while bound for Karachi from Peshawar. All of the bogies derailed along with the engine, however, no casualties were reported.


== Accident ==

The derailment happened at around 5:15 a.m. while the train was passing through the Sher Shah Junction railway station in Multan. The train driver said while travelling at 100 kilometres per hour (62 mph), he suddenly felt a push and applied the brakes. After stopping, some 14 coaches derailed near the Sher Shah Bridge. Search and rescue teams immediately launched an evacuation operation.


== Aftermath ==
Railway traffic on the affected section were suspended, while an additional train was dispatched to transport the stranded passengers to Peshawar.


== Victims ==
Seven people were killed, including a one-year-old, and more than 50 others were injured. The injured victims were transported to the nearby Nishtar Hospital for treatment, including some in critical condition. 21 people were still receiving treatment a day after the accident.


== Investigation ==
According to an initial investigation report, the derailment was likely caused by a fault in a passenger coach. The train driver said the train was in working order, while a passenger said that workers had repaired the nuts and bolts of coach number nine near Rohri. Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi appointed the federal government inspector of railways (FGIR) as the inquiry officer.

articles.title: 2026 Azerbaijani protests
articles.text:
2026 Azerbaijani protests

The 2026 Azerbaijani protests are series of protests from 21 September in various cities and towns in Azerbaijan. They erupted in response to the ban on wearing hijab in schools by Azerbaijani government and have been described  as one of the largest anti-government protests in Azerbaijan in recent years.
Azerbaijan, although a Muslim-majority country, is a secular state, which has previously debated balancing religious freedom and secular education. The similar protests happened in 2010-2012 over restrictions on wearing headscarves in educational institutions. The Azerbaijani pro-government media defended the hijab ban by presenting it as a way to protect Azerbaijan's secular education system, while portraying the protesters as "Iranian provocateurs", linking conservative Islam to Tehran amid strained Azerbaijan–Iran relations. Public demonstrations are rare in Azerbaijan, with demonstrations unsanctioned by the government facing serious restrictions. The event strained relations with Azerbaijan's long-standing ally, Turkey, as Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke against the hijab ban in unspecified country in his UN General Assembly speech immediately after the adoption of new rules in Azerbaijan, while Oktay Saral, a chief adviser to Erdoğan, and several MPs from Turkey's ruling Justice and Development Party were more explicit in their criticism of new Azerbaijani regulations. In response, the Azerbaijan's ruling New Azerbaijan Party issued a statement telling Turkey to stay out of Azerbaijan's internal affairs. The event added further tension between Azerbaijan and Turkey, with the New Azerbaijan Party linking the Turkish reaction to previous Turkish criticism of Azerbaijan's ties with Israel.


== History ==
On 21 September 2026, the Azerbaijani Cabinet of Ministers amended the rules on uniforms in public schools, prohibiting "clothing items that violate the uniform dress code or are considered inconsistent with the secular principle of general education". Although the ban did not explicitly mention hijab, although the reports suggested those girls wearing hijab were turned away from schools. In September 2026, a video circulated online alleging that the hijab had been banned in Azerbaijani schools. The video shows girls wearing the hijab being prevented from entering middle school.

articles.title: 150 Micklegate
articles.text:
150 Micklegate

150 Micklegate is a Grade II listed building on the corner of Micklegate and Bar Lane in the city of York, England. Its Bar Lane elevation faces the city walls and the site lies close to Micklegate Bar. Originally built for commercial use, it was modernised in the 20th century and was included within the Central Historic Core conservation area in 1968. Since 2019 it has been occupied by Micklegate Social, a bar and café that also occupies neighbouring No. 148.


== History ==
The mid‑19th‑century commercial building on Micklegate stands on the corner with Bar Lane, where its Bar Lane frontage faces the York city walls across the road, and it lies close to Micklegate Bar. It was later modernised in the 20th century, including new shopfronts.
Trade directories record a sequence of occupants under different address numbers, reflecting changes to the building's shop units and the renumbering of Micklegate carried out by York Corporation in 1910. In 1851 the directory of Kingston-upon-Hull and York lists Anthony Brown at No. 54, and by 1885 The York Furnishing Company appears at Nos. 54 and 55. The 1913 Kelly's Directory of the North and East Ridings of Yorkshire records the glass and china dealer Walter Ward at No. 148, with no separate entry for No. 150.
In 1968 the site was included within the newly established Central Historic Core conservation area, and on 14 March 1997, No. 150 was designated a Grade II listed building. It stands next to Nos. 144–148, which are listed at Grade II*.

In 2013 the combined café and bicycle workshop, York Bike Shed, opened in the building. In 2019 it reopened as Micklegate Social, a bar and café that also occupies neighbouring No. 148.


== Architecture ==
The ground floor is finished in dressed sandstone with textured panels, and the upper storey is built of orange‑red brick with cream‑brick pilasters and window surrounds. Stone and moulded brick are used for the main decorative details, and the slate roof has brick chimney stacks, one with a cornice.
The building stands on a corner plot and has two storeys, with two uneven bays facing Micklegate and four uneven bays facing Bar Lane, and a canted half‑bay at the corner. The shopfronts continue along both elevations, marked by pilaster piers on plain bases with moulded bands and a dentilled cornice. articles.title: 1997 New York City Comptroller election
articles.text:
1997 New York City Comptroller election

The 1997 New York City Comptroller election took place on November 4, 1997, to elect the comptroller of New York City. The election was held concurrently with the races for mayor and public advocate.
The incumbent comptroller, Alan Hevesi, a Democrat first elected in 1993, won re-election with 76% of the vote.


== Background ==
Hevesi was favored to win re-election. His main opponent was Annemarie McAvoy, a Republican who entered the race too late to join the city's campaign finance program; the other candidates were Independence nominee Genevieve Torres, Right to Life nominee Donald Young, Fusion nominee Donal Yarbrough and Socialist Workers nominee Wendy Lyons.
Hevesi raised $1,959,275 for the campaign and spent $2,053,787. He received $247,054 in public matching funds, but announced at a Campaign Finance Board debate on October 27 that he would return some of the money because McAvoy had not launched a "$3-million attack." He ultimately returned $172,600.
Two general election debates were held. The first, on September 29, included Hevesi, Torres and Lyons, the candidates participating in the campaign finance program. McAvoy and Hevesi, the only candidates to qualify as "leading contenders," met in a second debate on October 27.


== Democratic primary ==
Hevesi was the only Democratic candidate for comptroller, and no Democratic primary for the office was held. The Campaign Finance Board's list of 1997 primary results includes no comptroller race.


== General election ==
Hevesi won with 76.30% of the vote.


== Aftermath ==
Hevesi was sworn in for a second term on January 1, 1998. He was term-limited in 2001 and ran unsuccessfully for mayor that year, finishing fourth in the Democratic primary. He was elected New York State Comptroller in 2002. Bill Thompson won the open city comptroller seat in 2001.

articles.text:
Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS)

Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences
The Center for Earth and Natural Resource Sciences (CENRS) is a research organization based in Mukamira, Nyabihu District, Rwanda, with a community service branch in Nyabugogo, Kigali. The Rwanda Development Board registered it on 3 September 2025 under Law No. 007/2021 of 5 February 2021.It conducts research in environmental systems, Earth processes, natural hazards, natural resources, and pollution control and remediation, and does not offer teaching programmes.
History
Its founders, Jean Claude Ndayishimiye and Pascaline Nyirabuhoro, were doctoral researchers at the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Institute of Urban Environment, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in Xiamen. On 15 September 2016, Super Typhoon Meranti struck Xiamen with two-minute sustained winds of 173 km/h. Ndayishimiye later studied the effects of typhoon-driven disturbances on drinking-water reservoirs and testate amoeba communities. Both founders later held postdoctoral positions at Shenzhen MSU-BIT University, from February 2021 (Ndayishimiye) and September 2021 (Nyirabuhoro). On 3 August 2025, they finalized plans for a research institution, and CENRS was registered on 3 September 2025.
Research and services
CENRS states that it applies its research to services for local communities,Its research covers four areas

Environmental systems and Earth processes
Natural hazards (risk assessment, early warning, mitigation)
Natural resource science
Pollution control and remediation (water, soil, air, solid waste)
Collaborations
According to the Nature Index, its main research collaborators include Shenzhen MSU-BIT University, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Beijing Institute of Technology, Henan Normal University, and Saint Petersburg State University.
Research output
In the Nature Index 2025–2026 window (June 2025 to May 2026), CENRS ranked 8,715th globally and 14th in Rwanda by overall output, and 1,881st globally and 2nd in Rwanda in Earth and Environmental Sciences.

articles.title: Hawaii Ishizuchi Jinja
articles.text:
Hawaii Ishizuchi Jinja

Hawaii Ishizuchi Jinja (ハワイ石鎚神社) was a Shinto shrine in Honolulu, Hawaii, United States. It was established on February 17, 1913, by Shina Miyake, and became a branch of Ishizuchi Jinja in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. Following the closure of its organization in November 2023, its kami were transferred to Izumo Taisha Hawaii.
The shrine's observances included hatsumōde, the customary first shrine visit of the New Year. Its centennial celebration in 2013 brought together priests and members of the parent shrine in Japan for a religious ceremony, followed by a dinner and entertainment.


== History ==


=== Foundation and early organization ===
The shrine originated in the religious activities of Shina Miyake, an immigrant from Hiroshima Prefecture who had grown up in a household affiliated with Jōdo-shū Buddhism. According to a later account of the shrine's foundation, on February 17, 1913, she reported possession by a deity she called Takayama no Takagami. An immigrant from Saijō identified this deity with the god of Mount Ishizuchi, and Miyake adopted that identification. Miyake subsequently traveled to Japan for religious training and returned with a divided spirit of the deity from Ishizuchi Jinja. Early devotees sought healing through her mediumship.
Worship initially took place at an altar in Miyake's home. The congregation received recognition as a nonprofit religious organization from the territorial government on October 22, 1917, and moved to its South King Street location on November 24 that year.
Miyake returned to Japan on June 13, 1927. Tomiji Kimura, who had trained at Ishizuchi Jinja and Taga Shrine in Matsuyama, succeeded her as the second chief priest. Under Kimura, purification rites and festivals became the principal activities, replacing the earlier emphasis on Miyake's mediumship. The shrine also joined the Honolulu Shinto Federation.


=== Wartime disruption and postwar recovery ===
Following the attack on Pearl Harbor, Kimura was arrested in December 1941 and held at Sand Island. In February 1942, he was transferred to the continental United States, where he was incarcerated at several camps, including Fort Missoula and the Santa Fe camp. He returned to Hawaii in November 1945 aboard the Yarmouth.
The shrine had been taken over by government authorities, and Kimura was unable to resume public religious activities after his return. On June 1, 1949, the Office of Alien Property issued Vesting Order 13323 under the T

articles.title: Anders Ekegren
articles.text:
Anders Ekegren

Anders Ekegren (born 27 February 1957) is a Swedish lawyer and politician from the Liberals. Ekegren has been a member of the Riksdag for the Liberals since 2025, representing the Stockholm Municipality constituency. He is the party's tax and senior policy spokesperson.


== Biography ==


=== Background ===
Ekegren was born and raised in Gothenburg. He was an economics high school student. He became involved in the then Folkpartiet in 1976, party leader Per Ahlmark convinced him that "the two legs of liberalism – market economy and social responsibility were the right thing". He moved to Solna in 1983 and took a law degree from Stockholm University in the mid-1980s. Ekegren has worked as a negotiator and advisor in Akavia's negotiation department. He also represents Akavia in the Akademikeralliansen.


=== Political career ===
Ekegren was a municipal councilor in Solna from 1989–1994 and 2003–2014, chairman of the urban planning committee and first vice chairman of the municipal executive board.
Ekegren became the acting chairman of the municipal board in 2006 after the death of Anders Gustâv (M). Lars-Erik Salminen (M) succeeded him as chairman. He was again appointed acting chairman in 2011 after Salminen was indicted for bribery. Salminen then became chairman again after his acquittal in the district court and the court of appeal.
He served on the Stockholm County Council at the end of the 2011–2014 term. Between 2007–2014 he was chairman of the board of Film Capital Stockholm. From 2018–2022 he was chairman of the board of the municipal Film City Culture Foundation.
In February 2025, Ekegren became a member of the Riksdag for the Stockholm Municipality constituency. He succeeded party colleague Anna Starbrink who left to become Director General of the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency. He was a deputy minister to Minister of Climate and Environment Romina Pourmokhtari and a member of the Committee on Taxation. Following the 2026 Swedish general election, he took the seat from Karin Karlsbro in Stockholm County.

articles.title: Samuel Lunden
articles.text:
Samuel Lunden

Samuel Eugene Lunden (July 14, 1897 – June 10, 1995) was an American architect who designed many buildings in Los Angeles, California, particularly on the campus of University of Southern California.


== Early life ==
Samuel Eugene Lunden was born in Illinois on July 14, 1897. He graduated from Pasadena High School, then received his Bachelors of Science from California Institute of Technology in 1918 and Masters of Arts from Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1921.


== Career ==
Lunden worked as a draftsman for Reginald D. Johnson in Los Angeles County from 1915 to 1918, then worked part-time for Cram and Ferguson Architects, beginning while he was a student at Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1919 and continuing until 1927. He also was a member of American Students' Reconstruction Unit in France in 1921. In 1927, Lunden worked as a designer for Gordon B. Kaufman, and in 1928 he worked as Field Supervisor and Manager of Schultz and Weaver's Los Angeles office.
Lunden worked as a principal architect in his own practice from 1928 to 1950 and 1957 to 1960. He was a partner at Lunden, Hayward, and O'Connor from 1950 to 1957 and with Joseph Leupp Johnson starting in 1960. Lunden sold his practice in 1985 and continued as a consultant afterward.
Lunden joined the American Institute of Architects in 1932 and served as the organization's Vice President from 1945 to 1946.  He received the Edward C. Kemper Award for his contributions to the Institute and profession in 1963.


=== Style ===
Lunden was best known for his Art Deco and Classic styles.

articles.title: Louro (footballer)
articles.text:
Louro (footballer)

Francisco das Chagas Veras (26 December 1946 – 12 December 2005), more commonly known as Louro or "Magro de Aço" is a Brazilian retired footballer. He played as a right-back for various different clubs throughout the 1970s, commonly playing for Fortaleza, winning many editions of the Campeonato Cearense. 


== Club career ==
Louro began his career within the U–20 sector of Fortaleza in 1964, distinguishing himself for his great speed. He was later promoted to the senior squad in 1968 though he caught the attention of Corinthians who signed him for the remainder of the 1968 season where he made his debut in a 2–1 victory over Palmeiras on 10 March 1968. After an additional season, he wouldn't make the Starting XI for the club and soon returned to Ceará to play for Ferroviário–CE in 1970. However, he then played for Fortaleza again mid-season and remained there for a sizable portion of his career. He was briefly loaned to Santa Cruz in 1972 before returning to Fortaleza for an additional two seasons. His greatest achievement came during the 1974 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A as he was later elected to be part of the XI roster of the annual Bola de Prata by Placar magazine, considered one of the best defenders of the season. He later played for Sport Recife in Pernambuco throughout the next 2 seasons before returning to Ceará once more in the 1977 season before retiring soon after.


== Later life ==
Louro was briefly involved in youth football as he managed the youth sectors of his former club Fortaleza and Bacabal. However, in 2005, during a violent robbery, he was violently assaulted and was hospitalized at Maranguape where he lived his final days before dying on 12 December 2005 from cardiac arrest.

articles.title: Elizabeth McKellar
articles.text:
Elizabeth McKellar

Elizabeth McKellar FRHistS is a British architectural and design historian and academic. She is Professor Emerita in Architectural and Design History, at The Open University and served as President of the Society of Architectural Historians of Great Britain from 2021 to 2026.


== Early life and education ==
McKellar studied modern history at St Hugh's College, Oxford, graduating in 1984. She received an MSc in the History of Modern Architecture from the Bartlett School of Architecture and Planning at University College London in 1985.
She completed a PhD in the History of Design through the joint Royal College of Art and Victoria and Albert Museum programme in 1992. Her thesis was titled Architectural Practice for Speculative Building in Late Seventeenth-Century London. 


== Career ==
McKellar worked as a historical adviser and researcher for the Hackney Society from 1985 to 1990. She subsequently taught at Kingston Polytechnic and Canterbury College of Art and was a lecturer and senior lecturer at the University of North London from 1988 to 1993. From 1993 to 1996, she was Head of Higher Education at the Victoria and Albert Museum.
In 1996, McKellar joined Birkbeck College, University of London, as a senior lecturer in the history of art and architecture. She remained at Birkbeck until 2005, when she joined The Open University as a senior lecturer and staff tutor.
McKellar became Professor and Chair in Architectural and Design History at The Open University in 2013, serving until 2020. She has since been Professor Emerita in Architectural and Design History. 
She has been a member of the Editorial Boards of The London Journal, the Georgian Group Journal, The London Record Society and Lund Humphries publishers.  She has been an adviser to the Royal Commission on the Historic Monuments of England, English Heritage, the Museums, Libraries and Archives Council and was a member of Historic England’s London Advisory Committee (2012-2018).  


== Research ==
McKellar's research focuses on the architectural and urban history of London, particularly its development from the seventeenth to nineteenth centuries, urbanism, housing and vernacular architecture. She has also written widely on Georgian and Neo-Georgian British architecture from the seventeenth to the mid-twentieth century the and the history of architectural historiography.

articles.title: David William Carstens
articles.text:
David William Carstens

David William Carstens (born July 14, 1964) is an American attorney, entrepreneur, venture capitalist, and legal educator. He is the founder of Carstens, Allen & Gourley, LLP (formerly Carstens & Cahoon, LLP), as well as a co-founder of T Bank, N.A., PreMark Health Science, and 5IR Funds. He has also served as an adjunct professor at the Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law.


== Early life and education ==
Carstens earned a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from Texas A&M University in 1986 before attending Southern Methodist University, where he received his Juris Doctor in 1989. Carstens later completed a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering at the University of Texas at Dallas in 1994. In 2004, he earned a Master of Business Administration from Southern Methodist University. Carstens also completed the General Management Program at Wharton Business School at University of Pennsylvania in 2022.


== Career ==
Following his admission to the legal profession, Carstens focused on intellectual property law, particularly patent prosecution, patent litigation, technology licensing, and intellectual property transactions. He co-founded the intellectual property law firm Carstens & Cahoon, LLP, which later became Carstens, Allen & Gourley, LLP. The firm specializes in patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and intellectual property litigation. Throughout his legal career, Carstens has represented clients in patent and trademark litigation before the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit and federal district courts.
In addition to his legal practice, Carstens has been involved in banking and entrepreneurship. He co-founded T Bank, N.A., a nationally chartered community bank serving businesses, professionals, and individual customers.
Alongside his legal and entrepreneurial activities, Carstens has served for many years as an adjunct professor at the Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law. In this role, he has taught courses relating to international intellectual property law, legal protection of computer software, and copyright law.

articles.title: Key of Saint Servatius
articles.text:
Key of Saint Servatius

9
The Key of Saint Servatius is an object of Carolingian metalwork preserved in the treasury of the Basilica of Saint Servatius in Maastricht, the Netherlands. Made of silver and originally gilded, the object is attributed to a workshop operating in the vicinity of the Palace of Aachen. It may have been brought to Maastricht by Einhard.
The key is an attribute of Saint Servatius and belongs to a group of objects known as the Servatiana, which are traditionally associated with the saint's life. The association between the key and the saint derives from medieval tradition, while art-historical analysis dates the surviving object to the Carolingian period.


== History ==
The Key of Saint Servatius has been part of the treasury of Saint Servatius' Church in Maastricht for centuries. It was first mentioned by Jocundus in the 11th century and was first depicted in the 12th century on a relief panel in the church's westwork. How the key came to Maastricht is not known with certainty.

In 1985, the Dutch art historian A. M. Koldeweij proposed that the key was most likely made in the workshops associated with the Palace of Aachen in the early 9th century. Einhard may have played a role in its arrival in Maastricht. Also known as Eginhardus, Einhard was a scholar, poet and chronicler at the court of Charlemagne and his successor, Louis the Pious, in Aachen. He was also a lay abbot of several imperial monasteries, including the collegiate church of Saint Servatius in Maastricht. Through Einhard, the relics of the holy martyrs Peter and Marcellinus came into the possession of Saint Servatius' Church. The so-called Einhard Arch, a silver base in the form of a Roman triumphal arch that once supported an altar cross with relics of the True Cross, is also associated with him. The cross has long been considered lost. The base disappeared at the end of the 18th century, along with the reliquary shrine of Peter and Marcellinus, although the relics themselves survived. According to Maastricht art historian and archaeologist Titus Panhuysen, there are grounds for believing that these valuable and sacred gifts—the key, the base and the relics—formed part of a significant donation to the collegiate church of Saint Servatius. The presence of this royal treasure at the tomb of Saint Servatius may point to the close ties between the church and the Carolingian dynasty, and may also help explain the interest in Maastricht shown by the dukes of Lower Lorraine.

articles.title: Claire Le Flécher
articles.text:
Claire Le Flécher

Claire Le Flécher is a French diplomat and senior civil servant. She was ambassador of France to Kuwait from 2021 to 2024. A graduate of Sciences Po and the École nationale d'administration (ENA), she worked as a parliamentary assistant, ministerial adviser, regional councillor and deputy mayor before joining the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs in 2014. In September 2026 she was reported to be taking over as director general of the political party La France Humaniste.


== Education ==
Claire Le Flécher studied hypokhâgne and khâgne at the Lycée La Bruyère from 1992 to 1995, then took a licence (bachelor) in history and a maîtrise (masters) in political science at Paris Nanterre University (1995–1997). She studied Arabic and Russian at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (INALCO) from 1995 to 2000, and attended the public service section of Sciences Po from 1997 to 1999.
In October 2008 she was admitted to the preparatory cycle for the ENA internal competition, and she was a student at ENA in 2011–2012 (the "Marie Curie" class).


== Early career ==


=== Political activism ===
Claire Le Flécher became politically active at the age of 19 during the 1995 strikes. She chaired the Sciences Po section of the Young Socialist Movement and later sat on its national bureau. She sat on the Regional Council of Île-de-France from 2004 to 2008, one of three elected councillors of the Nouveau Parti socialiste tendency of the Socialist Party, of whose National Council she was a member.


=== Ministries and local government ===
From 2000 to April 2001 she was parliamentary assistant at the Senate to the Socialist senator Bernard Angels. From April 2001 to May 2002 she was parliamentary adviser to the Secretary of State for the Budget, Florence Parly. A Journal officiel notice of 1 March 2002 appointed her technical adviser in a secretary of state's cabinet from 4 March 2002.
From September 2002 to June 2007 she headed the Cycle des hautes études pour le développement économique at the Ministry of the Economy and Finance in Vincennes, and from June 2007 to December 2010 she was a researcher in public management at the same ministry. From March 2008 to January 2011 she was deputy mayor of Soissons and vice-president of its communauté d'agglomération.

articles.title: Benjamín G. Rosado
articles.text:
Benjamín G. Rosado

Benjamín García Rosado Bordallo (born 1985), known professionally as Benjamín G. Rosado, is a Spanish cultural journalist, writer, classical music critic, and cultural manager. In 2025, he won the Premio Biblioteca Breve for his debut novel, El vuelo del hombre, and received a Beca Leonardo grant from the BBVA Foundation in the Music and Opera category.


== Education and academia ==
Born in Ávila in 1985, Rosado graduated with a degree in Audiovisual Communication from the Complutense University of Madrid and studied journalism at Charles III University of Madrid. He later pursued postgraduate studies in film studies at Wesleyan University in Connecticut, United States.
In higher education, he has worked as a lecturer in communication techniques at the Alfonso X El Sabio University.


== Career ==


=== Cultural journalism and criticism ===
Rosado has developed a career spanning more than fifteen years in journalism and cultural criticism, focusing on classical music, performing arts, and contemporary thought.
He was a staff writer in the music section of El Cultural from 2008 to 2013, and in 2021 joined the cultural supplement La Lectura published by the daily newspaper El Mundo. He serves as a regular classical music critic for the specialized magazine Scherzo, and has contributed articles and columns to general-interest newspapers and magazines including El País, Esquire, Vanity Fair, Harper's Bazaar, and Gentleman.


=== Cultural management and musical drama ===
As a music programmer and manager, he founded and directed the concert series The London Music N1ghts, held at Madrid's Café Comercial as an experimental platform for classical music listening formats. He has also authored musicological essays and program notes for institutions such as the Teatro Real in Madrid, the Gran Teatre del Liceu in Barcelona, and Carnegie Hall in New York City.
In 2025, he was awarded the Beca Leonardo fellowship by the BBVA Foundation in the Music and Opera category to develop MIEDO, a contemporary chamber opera based on the novella Fear by Stefan Zweig, featuring music by composer Mario Carro and a libretto by Rosado.


=== Literary work ===
In February 2025, he was awarded the Premio Biblioteca Breve by publishing house Seix Barral for his debut novel, El vuelo del hombre. articles.title: Greg Moser
articles.text:
Greg Moser

Gregory Andrew Moser (born May 5, 1960) is an American former professional football wide receiver who played in the United States Football League (USFL) with the Los Angeles Express, Houston Gamblers, and Memphis Showboats. He played college football and baseball for the Oregon Ducks.


== Early life ==
Gregory Andrew Moser was born on May 5, 1960, in Fort Collins, Colorado. He attended Hood River Valley High School in Hood River, Oregon.


== College career ==
Moser enrolled at the University of Oregon to play college football for the Ducks. He was a four-year letterman from 1979 to 1982. He played in all 33 games from 1979 to 1981 but only four games in 1982 due to a broken foot. Moser caught three passes for 34 yards in 1979, 32 passes for 611 yards and two touchdowns in 1980, 39 passes for 605 yards and two touchdowns in 1981, and ten passes for 156 yards and one touchdown in 1982. He also threw a 25-yard touchdown in 1981.
Moser played college baseball for the Ducks as well. After the spring 1981 season, the school dropped baseball. However, Moser continued on with the University of Oregon's club baseball team.


== Professional career ==
After going undrafted in the 1983 NFL draft, Moser signed with the Los Angeles Express of the United States Football League (USFL) on May 14, 1983, midway through the 1983 USFL season. He played in seven games for the Express as a reserve wide receiver, recording four receptions for 47 yards, two kick returns for 20 yards, two punt returns for five yards, and one fumble recovery.
On September 6, 1983, Moser was selected by the Houston Gamblers in an expansion draft. He played in all 18 games, starting 17, for the Gamblers during the 1984 season, catching 36 passes for 685 yards and four touchdowns. Houston finished the year with a 13–5 record. He was released on February 7, 1985, a few weeks before the start of the 1985 regular season.
Moser then signed with the Memphis Showboats. He led the team in receiving yards in 1985, totaling 57 catches for 1,145 yards and six touchdowns as Memphis went 11–7. The USFL folded after the 1985 season.

articles.title: Jason Seagraves
articles.text:
Jason Seagraves

Jason Seagraves is an American film and television producer and former studio executive. He was vice president of production and development at Cross Creek Pictures, where he was a co-producer on American Made (2017) and on the Academy Award-winning Hacksaw Ridge (2016), and later senior vice president of development at Cavalry Media. He is an executive producer of the Prime Video series Motorheads (2025).


== Early life and education ==
Seagraves is from Georgetown, Texas. He attended Baylor University, entering as a theater major before switching to the university’s film department, and graduated in 2007. As a student he performed with and later managed the Guerrilla Comedy Troupe, Baylor’s improvisational comedy group, an experience he has credited with pointing him toward producing. During his senior year he took part in Baylor’s satellite programs, interning in Los Angeles and then in New York, where he interned for producer Scott Rudin and was hired to work for him after graduating. He has said that the Los Angeles internship gave him his foundation and connections in the industry: “Going into the Baylor in LA program, I had an idea about what elements go in to making a movie, but it wasn’t until I got there that the light bulb went off.”


== Career ==


=== Cross Creek Pictures ===
After working for Rudin, Seagraves joined Cross Creek Pictures as assistant to the company’s president, Brian Oliver. He was promoted to creative executive within a year and to vice president of production and development roughly a year and a half later. The first projects he led at the company were American Made and Hacksaw Ridge. He was Cross Creek’s lead executive on Black Mass (2015) and Roman J. Israel, Esq. (2017), structured financing and sales strategies for independently funded films, and procured several million dollars in financing for development projects. In 2016 he was announced as a producer, with Oliver and Maurice Fadida, of Cross Creek’s historical epic The Great Game, about the Nobel family and the Baku oil rush, to be directed by Gary Shore; the film was never completed. He produced the Gerard Butler thriller Keepers, later released as The Vanishing (2018). He was an executive producer of the David Ayer film The Tax Collector (2020), a Cross Creek production filmed shortly before he left the company.


=== Cavalry Media ===
In September 2018, Seagraves joined Cavalry Media, the finance and production company founded by Dana Brunetti

articles.title: The Joshua Tree Singles Vinyl Collection: 1987 & 2017
articles.text:
The Joshua Tree Singles Vinyl Collection: 1987 & 2017

The Joshua Tree Singles Vinyl Collection: 1987 & 2017 is a limited-edition compilation by Irish rock band U2, released in 2017 exclusively to subscribers of the band's official website, U2.com. The collection consists of four 10-inch vinyl records, each pairing a remastered studio recording of a single from the band's fifth studio album, The Joshua Tree (1987), with a live performance of the same song recorded during The Joshua Tree Tour 2017.
The collection features eight tracks, comprising the original studio versions and 2017 live recordings of "With or Without You", "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For", "Where the Streets Have No Name" and "In God's Country". It was announced on 3 May 2017 to commemorate the 30th anniversary of The Joshua Tree. The tracks became available as digital downloads on 5 October 2017, while the first physical vinyl sets began arriving to subscribers in December.


== Background and release ==
On 3 May 2017, U2 announced The Joshua Tree Singles Vinyl Collection: 1987 & 2017 as the exclusive gift for subscribers to U2.com during 2017. The release formed part of the band's celebration of the 30th anniversary of The Joshua Tree, which had originally been released on 9 March 1987. The anniversary was also marked by a reissue of the album and a stadium tour during which U2 performed the album in its entirety.
The collection brought together the four singles released from The Joshua Tree in North America during 1987. Each record features a remastered version of the original studio recording on its A-side, paired with a newly recorded live performance from The Joshua Tree Tour 2017 on its B-side. The live recordings were selected from four concerts performed in the United States during June 2017.
The set was produced exclusively for U2.com subscribers and was not made available for general retail sale. At the time of its announcement, the band expected the physical collection to begin shipping in September 2017, with digital downloads made available separately.
On 5 October 2017, all eight tracks were made available to qualifying subscribers as a digital download. The files were distributed in MP3 format at 320 kbit/s, with artwork corresponding to the individual records. The first physical copies began arriving on 8 December 2017. Subsequent manufacturing delays interrupted distribution, with further shipments continuing into 2018.

articles.title: Another Time, Another Place: Live at the Marquee London 1980
articles.text:
Another Time, Another Place: Live at the Marquee London 1980

Another Time, Another Place: Live at the Marquee London 1980 is a live album by Irish rock band U2, released in July 2015 exclusively to paid subscribers of the band's official website, U2.com. Recorded on 29 September 1980 at the Marquee Club in London, the album contains ten live performances from the band's early career, along with a spoken-word recording by lead singer Bono recalling the band's performances at the venue.
The album was issued as a limited-edition double 10-inch vinyl set, with the ten live tracks also made available as digital downloads. It was the first U2.com subscriber audio gift to be released on vinyl rather than compact disc.


== Background and release ==
The album was first announced on 25 November 2014 as the exclusive gift for U2.com's 2014–2015 subscription programme. At the time of the announcement, the title, artwork and track listing had not yet been revealed. The band described the forthcoming release as a recording from an early period of their career when they were performing in small venues across Ireland and the United Kingdom.
The release was intended as a companion to North Side Story, a publication previously distributed to U2.com subscribers documenting the band's early years in Dublin. The vinyl album was initially expected to be delivered during spring 2015, with selected tracks available for digital download in advance.
On 8 February 2015, the album's title and cover artwork were revealed. The track listing followed in April, when the expected shipping date was moved to July 2015. The first physical copies began arriving with subscribers on 29 July 2015, with distribution continuing throughout August.
The album was manufactured by GZ Vinyl in the Czech Republic and issued under the catalogue number U2COMV10. The two records were housed in a gatefold sleeve. The live performances occupy the first three sides of the release, while the fourth contains a spoken-word recollection by Bono.
On 24 August 2015, U2 officially promoted the completed release and made all ten live performances available for download to qualifying subscribers.


== Recording ==
The album was recorded on 29 September 1980 at the Marquee Club on Wardour Street in London. The performance was the fourth of four consecutive Monday-night concerts U2 played at the venue during September 1980, shortly before the release of their debut studio album, Boy.

articles.title: Swami Prajnanananda (musicologist)
articles.text:
Swami Prajnanananda (musicologist)

Swami Prajnanananda (31 August 1907 – 8 October 1998) was an Indian Hindu monk, musician and musicologist. A disciple of Swami Abhedananda, a direct disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa, he was associated with the Ramakrishna Vedanta Math in Calcutta (now Kolkata), and served as its President from 1984 until his death in 1998. He was associated with the Faculties of Music of the Calcutta University, Rabindra Bharati University and Visva-Bharati University.
He authored or edited over fifty books in Bengali and English, including multi-volume studies of Indian classical music, Vedanta and Indian philosophy. In 1963, he was awarded the  Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship , the highest award of the Akademi, for his contributions to musicology.


== Early life and education ==
Born as Pashupati Banerjee on 14.5.1314 (according to the Bengali calendar), 1907, in Prosadpur, in the Hooghly district of present-day West Bengal. His father was Nakurchandra Banerjee and elder brother, Panchakari Banerjee. He graduated (B.A.) from the City College, Kolkata University of Calcutta.


== Career ==
He received his monkhood initiation (Sannyas diksha) from Swami Abhedananda, a direct disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa and a contemporary of Swami Vivekananda.
Prajnanananda later served as president of the Ramakrishna Vedanta Math in Calcutta and of its associated Vedanta ashramas in Darjeeling, Kurseong and Siliguri. He edited the eleven volumes of Complete Works of Swami Abhedananda.
As a scholar of history and philosophy of Indian classical music, his notable books include, Sangeet O Samsktiti (1956) and Historical Development of Indian Music (1960). The latter won him the Rabindra Puraskar, highest honorary literary award given in the State of West Bengal, in 1961.In 1970, he received D.Litt. degree from Rabindra Bharati University. He died on 8 October 1998 at age 91.

articles.title: Pratap Pal
articles.text:
Pratap Pal

Pratap Pal was Maharaja of Karauli from 1837 until his death in 1848.


== Early life and family ==
Pratap Pal was born to Ameer Pal. His grandfather, Jawahar Pal, was a son of Tursam Pal, the Maharaja of Karauli, and was adopted into the Hadoti family. He married, amongst others, a daughter of Fateh Singh, the Raja of Jaoli, under Alwar, and Takhat Kumari, a daughter of Abhey Singh, the Raja of Khandela (Senior), and his wife, Udawatji. He had issue: a daughter, Jadaunji, who married Shatru Sal II, the Maharao Raja of Kotah.


== Reign ==
Upon the death of Harbaksh Pal in 1837, the throne of Karauli became vacant, as he had left behind no male issue who could have succeeded him on it. Pratap was therefore selected and was raised to the throne. The East India Company at first did not recognise his succession to the throne, for two reasons: first, because the state owed them a large debt, and second, because a widow of Harbaksh Pal claimed she was pregnant and later announced the birth of a son to her. Pratap called that child fraudulent and illegitimate. This led the East India Company to intervene, and it appointed a commission to investigate the legitimacy of that child, and that commission concluded that the widow's claim was false and the child was a fraud. Based on the findings of the commission and upon payment of all debts, George Eden, the then Governor-General of India, issued his ruling at the close of 1839 in favour of Pratap and recognised him as the legitimate ruler of Karauli. He built the Pratap Saroman temple. He was an authoritarian ruler who repeatedly abused his authority to extract wealth from his subjects in an attempt to replenish the depleted state treasury. His imposition of heavy taxes impoverished his subjects and fuelled civic unrest in the state. The resulting unrest became so serious that British officers were sent to Karauli on four separate occasions to address public grievances, mediate between the ruler and his subjects, and restore order.


== Death ==
He died in 1848. As he had left behind no male issue to inherit his dignities and power, his family adopted Nar Singh Pal as his successor.

articles.title: Betty Blackman
articles.text:
Betty Blackman

Betty Joan Blackman (October 7, 1931 – October 4, 2022) was an American librarian whose passion for empowering library workers led her to significant leadership positions at academic library systems. She was the first African-American dean of libraries in the California State University System, and a life-long supporter of library workers. She was inducted into the California Library Hall of Fame in 2018, and is memorialized in the California Library Leader History Project through the California State Library. 


== Education and career ==
Betty Blackman received her Bachelor's degree from Ohio State University and her Master of Arts in Library Science from Western Michigan University. She was a member of the Zeta Phi Beta Sorority.
Her first library position was at the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base library. In 1965, she moved to California and worked at the Long Beach library with the California State University (CSU) until 1979, when she became the library director of the Loyola Marymount University Library. She left the position in 1986 to take up the position of Dean of Libraries at California State University, Dominguez Hills, where she remained until retiring in 1999. Throughout all of these positions, Blackman was active in many professional organizations, including the Black Caucus of the American Library Association and the California Librarians Black Caucus, Southern Section. Within the California Library Association, she served as a council member and the chair of the Academic Research Libraries chapter. Within the American Library Association council, she was the CLA's representative and advocate, as well as a participant and leader in many other committees.
Blackman received the BCALA's Leadership Award in 1994, and certifications of merit from the California Librarians Black Caucus, Southern Section.
Blackman held her positions during important times of change, both on the national scale during the US civil rights era and on the scale of her individual universities, as Loyola Marymount University became more co-ed, secular, and adjusted to an expanded scope of identity as a religious university. 
In 2014, Blackman was interviewed for the California Library Leader History Project, and described her experiences and career. The California Library Leader History Project was an oral history project run by the California State Library.
In 2018, Blackman was indicted into the California Library Hall of Fame for her accomplishments

articles.title: Evan Prosofsky
articles.text:
Evan Prosofsky

Evan Prosofsky is a Canadian cinematographer.


== Career ==
Prosofsky began his career in the early 2010s working on music videos, frequently collaborating with director Emily Kai Bock. Notable credits include Grimes’ “Oblivion” (2012), Arcade Fire’s “Afterlife” (2013), Lana Del Rey’s “West Coast” (2014), Lorde’s “Yellow Flicker Beat” (2014), and Paul McCartney’s “Early Days” (2014). He later worked on videos for Florence + the Machine, Mitski, Steve Lacy and M.I.A.
Prosofsky directorial debut was the short documentary Water Park (2013), presented by NOWNESS. As cinematographer, he later worked on the short films A Funeral for Lightning (2016), Möbius (2017), Baton (2018), and Lay Me by the Shore (2022), directed by David Findlay and shot on 35 mm and 65 mm film. In 2025, he served as director of photography on Isaiah Saxon’s fantasy film The Legend of Ochi, produced by A24. He is a member of the Canadian Society of Cinematographers (CSC).
Prosofsky is best known for his early adoption and advocacy for shooting on celluloid. His projects often feature sequences shot on large format 65 mm. His upcoming feature-length debut, the documentary Grand Prairie, is being filmed on 65 mm film.


== Personal life ==
Prosofsky is married to cinematographer and director Emily Kai Bock.

articles.title: Wilmington Township, Kansas
articles.text:
Wilmington Township, Kansas

Wilmington Township is a township in Wabaunsee County, Kansas, United States. As of the 2020 census, its population was 583.


== History ==
Wabaunsee County was organized on March 25, 1859. The first townships were organized the same day, among them, Wilmington Township. In October 1872, Rock Creek Township was created from the western part of Wilmington Township, and in June 1887, Plumb Township was created from the eastern part.
 The first settler in what would become Wilmington Township was Henry Harvey, who settled in 1854. The first school in what would become Wilmington Township was built in 1858. Part of the ghost town of Bradford lies within the township.


== Geography ==
Wilmington Township covers an area of 58.202 square miles (150.74 km2), 0.32% of it water. Elm Creek, Locust Creek, Chicken Creek, and Dragoon Creek flow through it.


=== Communities ===
Eskridge

== Demographics ==
As of the 2020 census, the township had a population of 583, giving a population density of 10.0 people per square mile (3.9 people/km2). The racial makeup of the township was 94.7% White, 0.5% Asian, 0.2% Native American, 0.3% from some other race, and 4.3% from two or more races. Hispanics or Latinos of any race were 2.1% of the population.
The 2020–2024 American Community Survey estimated that the township contained 196 households and 234 housing units.

articles.title: The Stewart/Perry Company
articles.text:
The Stewart/Perry Company

The Stewart/Perry Company is an American commercial general contractor headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, United States. The company was founded in 1984 and it operates mainly in the Southeastern United States with select projects nationwide for some core clients providing services for retail, light-industrial, adaptive reuse, mixed-use, multifamily and historic renovation projects.


== History and operations ==
The Stewart/Perry Company was established in 1984 by Merill Stewart and Charles Perry. The company is licensed by the Alabama Licensing Board for General Contractors and provides commercial construction, design and build and civil management services. 
In 2008, the company opened its headquarters located on a 16-acre wooded campus at 4855 Overton Road in Birmingham, Alabama. The headquarters was designed by the Birmingham based architecture firm HKW and it achieved the LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) certification from the US Green Building Council.
Stewart/Perry's commercial client portfolio includes national retailers and commercial developments such as the Target Corporation, Buc-ee's, TJX companies such as HomeGoods and Marshalls, PetSmart, Five Below, Ulta Beauty, Ross Stores, Academy Sports + Outdoors, Onelife Fitness and Dick's Sporting Goods.
The company has completed various adaptive reuse and historic renovation projects in Downtown Birmingham including the restoration of the Lyric Theatre, the residential conversion of the Thomas Jefferson Hotel as well as the redevelopment of the former Edwards Chevrolet Building into Nextec, a 65,000-square foot technology hub and workspace for startup businesses.

articles.title: Don Puskarich
articles.text:
Don Puskarich

Don Puskarich (born February 26, 1939) is an American former professional stock car racing driver. He competed in the NASCAR Winston Cup Series and NASCAR Winston West Series between 1974 and 1984. He won Rookie of the Year in the Winston West Series in 1975.


== Racing career ==
Puskarich began competing in the NASCAR Winston West Series in 1974, finishing fifth in his debut at Altamont Speedway; he finished tenth and fourth in his other starts at Clovis Speedway and Ascot Park respectively. He competed full-time in 1975, where in eighteen races, he scored a pole and seven top-tens with a best finish of second at Santa Maria Speedway. He finished fourth in the standings and was awarded Rookie of the Year. The West Series schedule included three combination races, Puskarich's first NASCAR Winston Cup Series starts, where he scored a best finish of twelfth in his debut at Riverside International Raceway.
Puskarich ran eight of thirteen Winston West races in 1976, with his lone top-ten being a fifth place finish at Evergreen Speedway. He finished 27th and 21st in the Riverside combination race and fifteenth in the combination race at Ontario Motor Speedway.
Puskarich attempted twelve of twenty Winston West races in 1977, scoring five top-ten finishes with a best finish of seventh at Ascot Park and Craig Road Speedway. He finished 30th and 28th in the Riverside combination races and failed to qualify for the Ontario combination race. Puskarich also made his USAC Stock Car Series debut at Ontario, finishing 22nd due to overheating issues.
In 1978, Puskarich attempted four races, failing to qualify at Mesa Marin Raceway and Ontario and finishing 31st at Riverside and sixteenth at Sears Point International Raceway; the Riverside and Ontario races were combination races with the Winston Cup Series. He made his second and final USAC Stock Car start at Ontario, finishing last in the 28 car field due to an oil leak after four laps.
Puskarich's lone NASCAR start of 1979 came in the Winston Cup and Winston West season opener at Riverside, where he finished 28th. He would run his second and final full-time Winston West season in 1980, where he scored one top-ten, a tenth place finish in a standalone race at Ontario, in eleven races. He finished seventh in the standings. Puskarich finished nineteenth and seventeenth in the Riverside combination races and last in 42nd due to engine issues after two laps in the Ontario combination race.

articles.title: Second Masisi cabinet
articles.text:
Second Masisi cabinet

The second Masisi cabinet was the sixteenth government of Botswana headed by President Mokgweetsi Masisi after the Botswana Democratic Party (BDP) formed a majority government following its victory at the general election held on 23 October 2019. 
Masisi began his elected presidential term on 1 November and appointed a new ministry on 6 November, comprising 18 ministers and eight assistant ministers. Slumber Tsogwane was retained as Vice-President. The administration ended with the accession of Duma Boko to the presidency on 1 November 2024, after the BDP lost power for the first time since independence at the 2024 Botswana general election.
During its five years in office, the cabinet oversaw Botswana's response to the COVID-19 pandemic, an economic recovery programme, changes to public administration and negotiations with De Beers over the country's principal diamond-mining partnership. Its membership changed through appointments and transfers in 2020 and 2021, the replacement of ministers in early 2022, and a major reorganisation of ministerial responsibilities in April 2022. Further changes in 2024 followed the departure of environment minister Philda Kereng, the death of her successor Dumezweni Mthimkhulu and the dismissal of health minister Edwin Dikoloti.
The cabinet was the last BDP administration in an uninterrupted period of government extending from Botswana's independence in 1966. The party's defeat was attributed to a combination of economic difficulties, dissatisfaction with governance and divisions arising from candidate selection within the BDP.


== Background and formation ==


=== From the Khama presidency to the 2019 election ===
Masisi succeeded Ian Khama as president after Khama reached his term limit and the first Masisi cabinet was formed on 1 April 2018. The transition preceded what would be a public rift between Masisi and Khama; Khama subsequently supported the breakaway Botswana Patriotic Front (BPF). The two leaders' conflict was an important element of the political setting of the 2019 election. The personal and party rivalry subsequently complicated Masisi's constitutional-reform programme and the direction of the state.
Defying the odds against him, the BDP retained its majority, winning 38 of the 57 directly elected National Assembly seats at the general election on 23 October 2019. The Umbrella for Democratic Change (UDC) won 15 seats, the BPF three and the Alliance for Progressives one. Masisi's new

articles.title: Heather H. Lavallee
articles.text:
Heather H. Lavallee

Heather H. Lavallee is an American business executive and the president and CEO of Voya Financial. She has also served in executive roles at the company, including its Wealth Solutions chief executive officer and president of its Tax-Exempt Markets and Employee Benefits businesses.


== Education ==
Lavallee earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from Colby College and a Master of Business Administration from Pepperdine University's Graziadio Business School. She has also served on the board of the Council for Economic Education.


== Career ==
Lavallee began her financial career in 1992 as a sales representative at Sun Life Financial.
From 2005 to 2008, she served as regional vice president of the Group Insurance Division for the Western Region at Mutual of Omaha. 
In 2008, Lavallee joined Voyal Financial. In 2011, she was promoted to president of Employee Benefits Distribution. Her responsibilities included the company's group and voluntary insurance distribution teams and marketing efforts in the United States. In 2014, Voya Financial appointed her president of its Employee Benefits business, with responsibility for areas including strategy, product management, underwriting, actuarial operations and distribution. 
Three years later, Lavallee was named president of the company’s  Employee Benefits business, with responsibility for areas including strategy, product management, underwriting, actuarial operations and distribution.
In 2016, Lavallee became president of Voya's Tax-Exempt Markets business. Lavallee subsequently became chief executive officer of Voya's Wealth Solutions business. In July 2022, the company announced that she would succeed Rodney O. Martin Jr. as CEO of Voya Financial the following January. She also joined the company's board of directors in July 2022.


== Philanthropic efforts and awards ==
Lavallee was the first executive sponsor of Voya Cares, an initiative focused on people with disabilities and special needs and their caregivers. In 2023, she became CEO of Voya Financial while continuing to oversee the company's overall strategy and performance.
In 2022, Lavallee received the Hartford Business Journal's Top 25 Women in Business recognition. In 2023, she was included in Forbes' 50 Over 50 list, according to biographical profiles published by the Women's Business Collaborative and ABILITY Magazine.

articles.title: New Mooring Container Terminal
articles.text:
New Mooring Container Terminal

The New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT; also NMCT) is a container port facility at the Port of Chittagong in Bangladesh. It is the largest terminal in the country. It handled 44% of the port's container traffic in 2024.
The NCT is a brownfield riverine terminal with an 820-metre quay wall. It has five jetties. Four of them are dedicated to ocean-going vessels and the remaining one is for smaller ships on inland routes. The terminal was built with support from the China Harbour Engineering Group. The Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) signed the construction agreement in 2004. The initial construction began in 2004 and was completed in 2007. The adjacent overflow container yard (OCY) for additional storage was developed later in 2015.
Since 2007, Saif Powertec Ltd, a local firm, operated two of the jetties on an ad hoc basis. While the terminal was aimed to be the first port-centric foreign investment in the country, the international tendering process initiated under the Caretaker government of Fakhruddin Ahmed was canceled following Awami League's return to power in 2009. The four pre-qualified international operators under this tender, including Orient Steam Navigation Company (a subsidiary of Dubai-based DP World), were expected to submit their final tender on 25 February 2010. Later reports attributed the cancellation to interventions by Noor-e-Alam Chowdhury, the then chairman of Jatiya Sangsad's Standing Committee on Ministry of Shipping, and Shajahan Khan, the Minister of Shipping.
In June 2012, a fresh round of tender began for selecting a terminal operator. Five international and local firms submitted their bids on 30 August. On 2 September, a panel from the Central Procurement Technical Unit (CPTU) stopped the tender to review the allegation of irregularities in the bidding process by an international bidder. The CPTU later asked CPA to cancel the 2012 tender and begin a new tendering process. The orders issued by the review panel included that CPA retain the list of pre-qualified operators originally selected under the terms and conditions of the pre-qualification documents from 2008. This was reportedly done in light of changes and relaxation of terms CPA made to the original bidding documents under the Ministry's directions in the preceding two and a half years following the initial tender. articles.title: Norbert Pfaffenbichler
articles.text:
Norbert Pfaffenbichler

Norbert Pfaffenbichler (born 1967) is an Austrian experimental filmmaker, visual artist and curator. His work ranges from abstract and found-footage films to experimental horror features influenced by silent cinema. He is best known for his Notes on Film series, which reworks material from film history, and the dystopian 2551 trilogy (2021–2025).


== Life and career ==
Pfaffenbichler was born in Steyr, Upper Austria, in 1967. From 1992 to 1994, he studied theatre studies and journalism at the University of Vienna. He subsequently studied visual media design under Peter Weibel at the University of Applied Arts Vienna from 1994 to 2001. He has worked as an independent artist and curator in Vienna and was a founding member of the experimental media initiatives VIDOK and lanolin.
His early films include santora (1998), made with Jürgen Moritz, and 36 (2001), made with Lotte Schreiber. Both are abstract works concerned with editing, rhythm and the relationship between sound and image. In the early 2000s, Pfaffenbichler began making films almost entirely from existing footage.
He has also curated film programmes and exhibitions. His films have been screened at the Venice Film Festival, the Locarno Film Festival and the International Film Festival Rotterdam, among others.


== Film work ==


=== Early films and Notes on Film ===
Pfaffenbichler began his Notes on Film series in 2002. The films re-edit existing footage, often isolating particular gestures, movements or recurring visual motifs. Several works in the series use material from early cinema or concentrate on individual actors and their screen personas.
In Mosaik mécanique (2007), Pfaffenbichler rearranged Charlie Chaplin's short comedy A Film Johnnie (1914) into 98 simultaneously displayed, continuously looping images. Instead of watching Chaplin's film unfold from beginning to end, the viewer sees its individual shots arranged across the screen.
Conference (Notes on Film 05) (2011) consists of close-ups of actors portraying Adolf Hitler in films made over several decades. Their performances are edited together, bringing out similarities in their gestures, expressions and mannerisms.
Three subsequent feature-length works concentrate on individual actors. A Messenger from the Shadows (2013) uses performances by silent-film actor Lon Chaney, while A Masque of Madness (2013) is assembled from films featuring Boris Karloff. articles.title: Inauguration of Péter Magyar
articles.text:
Inauguration of Péter Magyar

The inauguration of Péter Magyar as Prime Minister of Hungary took place on Saturday, 9 May 2026, after Magyar was elected by the National Assembly.


== Background ==

Before the election, Magyar served as the leader of the opposition. Although it had remained uncertain for a long time, Magyar announced on 20 February 2026 that he would be the Tisza Party's candidate for Prime Minister. Following the party's landslide victory on 12 April 2026, Magyar ordered President Tamás Sulyok to convene the inaugural session of the National Assembly as soon as possible. The session was ultimately scheduled for 9 May 2026.


== Inaguration ==

After the members of the National Assembly elected the Speaker, appointed the parliamentary notaries, and established the parliamentary committees, President Sulyok nominated Magyar for Prime Minister. With 140 votes in favour, 54 against, and one abstention, the National Assembly elected Péter Magyar as the 60th Prime Minister of Hungary.
After taking the oath of office, Magyar delivered a speech in the chamber, during which he once again called on Sulyok to resign. At the conclusion of the inaugural session, a group of children performed the Romani anthem on the tambura, followed by the Hungarian folk song Tavaszi szél vizet áraszt. During the performance, all six members of the Our Homeland Movement walked out of the chamber, sparking considerable controversy. The session ended with performances of the European Union anthem, Ode to Joy, and the Székely anthem.


== Aftermath ==


=== National flag-raising ===

After all Tisza Party MPs had walked out onto Kossuth Square, Magyar followed them as the last person to leave the chamber, accompanied by his three sons. He was then received by Gábor Böröndi, Chief of the General Staff. The commander of the ceremonial unit reported to Magyar that the unit had assembled in formation to mark the establishment of the National Assembly. Magyar then inspected the square, after which the Hungarian flag was raised. He subsequently delivered another speech.


=== Celebrartion ===
Later that day, an event titled Rendszerbontó Népünnepély (lit. 'System-Breaking People's Celebration') was also held, attracting tens of thousands of attendees. The event took the form of a celebration that continued late into the night. When the barriers were removed, the crowd flooded into the square as Ibolya Oláh performed her song "Magyarország".

articles.title: Gustav Trinkler
articles.text:
Gustav Trinkler

Gustav Vasilyevich Trinkler (Russian: Густав Васильевич Тринклер; (24 April 1876 – 4 February 1957) was a Russian and Soviet engineer and inventor, best known for developing an early compressorless diesel engine, marketed in Germany as the "Trinkler engine". In Russia, the dual combustion cycle is named the Trinkler cycle after him.
Born into a prosperous merchant family of largely German descent, Trinkler is also of interest to historians as a pre-revolutionary "bourgeois specialist" who succeeded in maintaining a comfortable, upper-class way of life across the Russian Revolution, the Stalin era and his own imprisonment, largely through his technical expertise and a lifelong habit of petitioning the authorities.


== Early life and education ==
Trinkler was born in Saint Petersburg, the youngest of four surviving children. His father, Ioann-Wilhelm Trinkler, was a Baltic German born in Reval who traded between Saint Petersburg and Moscow, owned a factory, and held the status of first-guild merchant and "honorary citizen". His mother, Ekaterina-Adel, was the daughter of a German, Friedrich Adolf Gaspari, and a Frenchwoman, Theresa Mortier. In his memoir Trinkler described his family as strongly "international", listing Swiss, Italian, German, French and Polish ancestry on his mother's side and Estonian-German and Swedish ancestry on his father's, while insisting that by culture and education the family was entirely Russian.
His father died when he was eleven, and his mother oversaw the children's education. The children shared a nursery with a German nursemaid, heard fairy tales in Russian and German, and were taught by several French tutors; Trinkler later spoke German, French and English well. After a private progymnasium he attended the Larin Gymnasium, a classical school whose intake was restricted largely to the privileged classes, graduating in 1894. He then studied at the Saint Petersburg Technological Institute, graduating as an engineer in 1899 with his name engraved on the institute's marble board of distinction, and served a year as a volunteer in the Izmaylovsky Regiment.
His diploma named him Gustav Wilhelmovich, but by 1906 he had adopted the Russian patronymic Vasilyevich while keeping his German first name and surname. His siblings went further and Russified their first names, becoming Georgii, Elizaveta and Vasilii. Trinkler identified as Russian throughout his life.

articles.title: Carmen Messina
articles.text:
Carmen Messina

Carmen Messina (born September 8, 1988) is an American former football linebacker. He played college football for the New Mexico Lobos and led the Football Bowl Subdivision in tackles in 2009. He was on the Detroit Lions' practice squad in 2012.


== Early life ==
Carmen Messina was born on September 8, 1988. He played high school football at Addison Trail High School in Addison, Illinois.


== College career ==
Messina enrolled at the University of New Mexico to play college football for the Lobos. He redshirted the 2007 season and was a four-year letterman from 2008 to 2011. He played in all 48 games for the Lobos from 2008 to 2011, and was a three-year starter from 2009 to 2011. Messina led the Football Bowl Subdivision in tackles in 2009 with 162. He was named first-team All-Mountain West Conference in 2009 and 2011 and second-team All-Mountain West in 2010. Messina finished his college career with 217 solo tackles, 237 assisted tackles, nine sacks, two interceptions, seven forced fumbles, and five pass breakups. The Lobos were only 3–33 in his three seasons as a full-time starter.


== Professional career ==
After going undrafted in the 2012 NFL draft, Messina signed with the Detroit Lions on May 10, 2012. During the 2012 preseason, he recorded nine solo tackles, five assisted tackles, and one interception for eight yards. He was released on August 31 but signed to the practice squad the next day.
Messina signed a futures contract with the Lions on December 31, 2012. He played in one game during the 2013 preseason, posting two solo tackles. He was waived/injured on August 12, 2013, with a hamstring injury and reverted to injured reserve the next day. Messina was waived from injured reserve on August 16, 2013.
