articles.title: Camberwell Courthouse and Police Station
articles.text:
Camberwell Courthouse and Police Station

The Camberwell Courthouse and Police Station is a court house and police station complex, located at 311–317 Camberwell Road in Camberwell, in the City of Boroondara, in the inner eastern suburbs of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia.
Built between 1938 and 1939 on the traditional lands of the Wurundjeri people, the legal complex was added to the Victorian Heritage Register on 25 July 1996 in recognition of its architectural significance. 


== Description ==
The Camberwell Police Station and Court House complex was designed by the Victorian Public Works Department architect, Percy Edgar Everett; the complex was built by W. A. Medbury between 1938 and 1939. The complex is in the Inter-war Moderne style and is set on a diagonal axis. The buildings are constructed of red, brown and manganese bricks and contain Everett's trademark pattern detailing. The complex still retains a law enforcement function, as the court house was closed in 1989 and the building is now used for tribunal work.
The Camberwell complex is of architectural significance as an exceptionally fine and intact example of a building complex designed by Everett who was influential in the design and evolution of Moderne-style buildings in Victoria. The Camberwell complex was influential in the development of style in Victoria and later examples of Moderne-style buildings by Everett include the court houses in Shepparton and Sandringham, the William Angliss School, and government offices in Ballarat, all of which employ similar stylistic elements to those utilised by the Camberwell complex.

articles.title: Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption
articles.text:
Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption

The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC), commonly known as the Bribery Commission, is the principal anti-corruption agency of Sri Lanka. It is an independent commission responsible for investigating, prosecuting and preventing bribery and corruption in the public and private sectors, and for administering the declaration of assets and liabilities by public officials.
First established as a permanent body in 1994, the Commission operates under the Anti-Corruption Act, No. 9 of 2023, which widened its mandate and was passed partly to give effect to the United Nations Convention against Corruption.


== History ==


=== Background ===
Bribery was first made a statutory offence in Ceylon by the Penal Code Ordinance, No. 2 of 1883. Several commissions of inquiry examined bribery in the 1940s, among them the L. M. D. de Silva Commission (1941), the Keuneman Commission (1948), which recommended a separate department to investigate bribery, and the M. W. H. de Silva Commission (1949). A dedicated statute, the Bribery Act, No. 11 of 1954, followed, and the Bribery (Amendment) Act, No. 40 of 1958 created the office of the Bribery Commissioner and the Bribery Commissioner's Department, which took over bribery investigations and became the direct predecessor of CIABOC. Later amendments broadened the law: the Declaration of Assets and Liabilities Law, No. 1 of 1975 brought asset declarations within the Commissioner's remit, and the Bribery (Amendment) Act, No. 20 of 1994 introduced corruption as a separate offence and provided for the forfeiture of property on conviction.


=== Establishment ===
The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption Act, No. 19 of 1994 established CIABOC as a permanent, independent commission to succeed the Bribery Commissioner's Department. It was given powers to investigate complaints of bribery and corruption and to direct prosecutions, and the prosecution of Bribery Act cases was transferred to it. The Commission was later empowered to act on its own initiative (ex mero motu) under Article 156A of the Constitution.


=== Reform under the 2023 Act ===
Sri Lanka's anti-corruption laws were consolidated by the Anti-Corruption Act, No. 9 of 2023, which came into force on 15 September 2023. The Act repealed and replaced three earlier laws: the Bribery Act of 1954, the CIABOC Act, No. 19 of 1994, and the Declaration of Assets a

articles.title: Penstemon guadalupensis
articles.text:
Penstemon guadalupensis

Penstemon guadalupensis, the Guadalupe penstemon or Hill Country foxglove, is a species in the veronica family that only grows in the US state of Texas. There it is found on the eastern Edwards Plateau and areas to the northwest.


== Description ==
The Guadalupe penstemon is a herbaceous plant with flowering stems that grow straight upwards or leaning out from the base of the plant before growing upwards to a height of 20 to 50 centimeters (8–19.5 in). They are covered in retrorse hairs, stiff ones that point backwards. It forms small colonies and spreads by underground stems. It is relatively long-lived for a penstemon.
The plants have both basal leaves and ones attached to the stems. The basal leaves and the lowest ones on the stems measure 2.5 to 9.5 centimeters (1–3.5 in) long and just 1–6 millimeters wide. This usually gives them a narrow grass-like shape, only rarely lanceolate. They have a tapered base, a pointed tip, and smooth edges. The basal leaves will persist over the winter. Attached to the stems there are six to eleven leaf pairs, most of them are attached directly by the leaf base to the main stem, but the lowest ones can have short petioles, leaf stems. They are 2.2–9.5 cm long, but can be wider at 1–1.8 mm, though typically they are no more than 6.5 cm (2.5 in) and less than 10 mm in width. They can be fully lanceolate to linear, the widest part of the leaf in the lower third of the length. The base of the stem leaves can be tapered or clasp the main stem and the edges are smooth to very slightly serratedly toothed.
The flowers are white, slightly pink, or very pale purple, with purple floral guide lines along the bottom of the flower's throat. The petals are fused into a funnel shaped tube that opens to five lobes with a length of 1.3–2 centimeters (0.5–0.8 in).


== Taxonomy ==
The scientific description of Penstemon guadalupensis was published in 1895 Amos Arthur Heller. Specimens collected prior to Heller's description were identified as the similarly colored Penstemon albidus. He collected his type specimen on 19 April 1894 near the confluence of the Guadalupe River and Town Creek. It is classified in the Penstemon genus within the Plantaginaceae family. The species has no accepted subspecies or varieties, however two subspecies and one variety have been published that are considered heterotypic synonyms.


=== Names ===
The scientific name of the species, guadalupensis, is derived from the Guadalupe River.

articles.title: Holland's embedding theorem
articles.text:
Holland's embedding theorem

Holland's embedding theorem is a representation theorem in the theory of lattice-ordered groups. It states that every lattice-ordered group can be embedded, with its lattice operations preserved, in the lattice-ordered group of all order-preserving bijections of a totally ordered set. It is the lattice-ordered analogue of Cayley's theorem in group theory, and was proved by W. Charles Holland in 1963.
Holland's embedding theorem is the foundation of the study of the groups of order-preserving permutations of chains, known as ordered permutation groups, which have been investigated in their own right ever since.


== Notation ==
A lattice-ordered group (written ℓ-group, with a script ell; older sources use l-group) is a group G together with a lattice order ≤ that is preserved by multiplication: a ≤ b implies ca ≤ cb and ac ≤ bc for all a, b, c ∈ G. Throughout, Ω denotes a totally ordered set (a chain), Aut(Ω) denotes the group of all order-preserving bijections from Ω to Ω, and ≤ on Aut(Ω) is the pointwise order: f ≤ g when f(x) ≤ g(x) for every x ∈ Ω. The lattice operations on Aut(Ω) are the pointwise meet and join, written ∧ and ∨. Holland's 1963 paper writes L where the 2011 survey writes Ω; the two letters denote the same object.


== Statement ==
The group Aut(Ω), ordered pointwise, is itself an ℓ-group: the meet (f ∧ g)(x) = min{f(x), g(x)} and the join (f ∨ g)(x) = max{f(x), g(x)} are again order-preserving bijections.
Holland's embedding theorem states that for every ℓ-group G there is a totally ordered set Ω such that G admits an injective homomorphism of ℓ-groups into Aut(Ω). In other words, every lattice-ordered group can be realised as a group of order-preserving permutations of a chain, with its order and lattice operations computed pointwise.
The chain Ω cannot in general be taken to be the underlying lattice of G, since that lattice need not be totally ordered; a separate chain must be constructed.


== Construction ==
The proof builds the chain from the convex ℓ-subgroups of G. For g ≠ 1, Zorn's lemma gives a convex ℓ-subgroup C[g] maximal among those that do not contain g; the convex ℓ-subgroups containing it form a chain under inclusion, so the right cosets R(C[g]) are totally ordered by Cx ≤ Cy when cx ≤ y for some c ∈ C. Each element of G acts on these cosets by right multiplication, and the resulting map is an ℓ-group homomorphism onto a transitive ℓ-subgroup. Applied to every g ≠ 1, this embeds G as a subdi

articles.title: Jozef Deleu
articles.text:
Jozef Deleu

Jozef Hugo Maria Deleu (20 April 1937 – October 2026) was a Flemish poet, prose writer, essayist and anthologist. At twenty he founded Ons Erfdeel (now de lage landen), a Flemish-Dutch cultural magazine he ran until 2002 and expanded into a foundation publishing in Dutch, French and English. In retirement he started the poetry magazine Het liegend konijn, which he put together single-handedly from 2003 to 2025. In Flanders he was sometimes called the "culture pope".


== Early life ==
Deleu was born in Roeselare, West Flanders, the youngest of seven children in a farming family. His father, Louis, was born in Lille in 1897 and gave up French nationality to become Belgian. He trained as a primary school teacher at the teacher training college in Torhout and taught from 1956 to 1970, first in Mouscron and then in Menen.


== Ons Erfdeel ==

The idea came from the writer André Demedts, who approached the nineteen-year-old Deleu at a 1956 meeting of the Committee for French Flanders. A year later the first issue of Ons Erfdeel ("Our Heritage") was out. It ran to 250 copies and was meant for young readers in West, Zeelandic and French Flanders. That soon changed. Deleu widened its scope to the whole Dutch-language area and built up a network of contributors in Belgium and the Netherlands; by 1982 circulation stood at 10,000.
He gave up teaching in 1970. The magazine moved into the independent Ons Erfdeel Foundation, with Deleu as managing director, and from there he went after readers beyond the language border: Septentrion for French speakers in 1972, the bilingual yearbook De Franse Nederlanden / Les Pays-Bas Français for northern France in 1976, and, in 1993, The Low Countries for the English-speaking world. Its offices stood next to Deleu's home in Rekkem, on the Franco-Belgian border. Deleu stepped down as editor-in-chief and managing director on 30 April 2002 and was succeeded by Luc Devoldere.
Deleu was also on the editorial board of the magazine Neerlandia in 1960–1961, and between 1969 and 1975 helped set up the first Encyclopedie van de Vlaamse Beweging (Encyclopedia of the Flemish Movement).


== Writing ==
His debut was a novella, De ontmoeting (1962). His first poetry collection, Schaduwlopen, followed a year later. Transience runs through all of it, verse and prose alike. articles.title: Kārlis Reišulis
articles.text:
Kārlis Reišulis

Kārlis Alberts Reišulis (born 2 November 2005) is a Latvian professional Motocross racer. Reišulis has competed full-time in the Motocross World Championship since midway through the 2024 season.
Reišulis has represented his country at the Motocross des Nations on five occasions, most recently at the 2026 event. During the 2026 event, the Latvian team recorded its highest overall position to date of fourth place. At the 2024 Motocross des Nations, he was awarded the Ricky Carmichael Award for the best young rider at the event.
He is the older brother of Jānis Reišulis, who is also a world-championship level motocross racer and two-time European champion. The pair have spent several years as team mates whilst racing in the MXGP paddock.
From 2021 to 2026, Reišulis was part of Yamaha's official teams. This saw him transition through EMX125, EMX250 and into MX2 with the manufacturer.


== Career ==


=== Junior career ===
After starting in the sport at a young age, Reišulis progressed through the junior ranks in Latvia and around Europe. After becoming MX50 Latvian champion in 2013, he got his first taste of international competition in 2015 when he scored five points in the EMX65 class 2015 European Motocross Championship. In 2016, he was able to improve to sixth in the EMX65 championship and take home the silver medal in the 65 class of the FIM Motocross Junior World Championship, held in Russia. Reišulis competed for a final time in EMX65 in 2017 but dropped to twelfth in the overall standings. A week later he returned to the FIM Junior Worlds but after a strong qualifying performance, did not finish the first race and was not able to start the second.
After competing in the MX85 class domestically in 2017, Reišulis made his full-time move to an 85cc motorcycle in 2018. On his debut in the EMX85 class of the 2018 European Motocross Championship, he scored three points. Reišulis also represented his country at the Motocross of European Nations, where the Latvian team finised seventh overall. In his second and final year on an 85 in 2019, Reišulis finished fourth overall in the EMX85 class of the 2019 European Motocross Championship and then fifth overall in the FIM Junior World Championship. He again travelled to the Motocross of European Nations with the Latvian team where, after winning his qualifying race, he finished third and sixth in the two 85 races. articles.title: Nightmare (2022 film)
articles.text:
Nightmare (2022 film)

Nightmare (Norwegian: Marerittet) is a 2022 Norwegian supernatural horror film written and directed by Kjersti Helen Rasmussen in her feature directorial debut. It stars Eili Harboe, Herman Tømmeraas and Dennis Storhøi. The film follows a young woman whose nightmares and episodes of sleep paralysis become increasingly disturbing after she moves into an apartment with her boyfriend.
The film had its world premiere at Fantastic Fest on 25 September 2022 and was released in Norwegian cinemas on 17 February 2023. It became available on the horror streaming service Shudder on 29 September 2023.


== Plot ==
Mona and her boyfriend Robby move into a spacious but run-down apartment which they have bought at a low price. Robby has begun a demanding new job, leaving Mona to work on renovating their home. Although Robby is eager to start a family, Mona is unsure about having a child. Soon she begins experiencing violent nightmares, sleepwalking and episodes of sleep paralysis. In her dreams, she encounters a threatening figure who resembles Robby. After learning about a previous resident's death and witnessing increasingly disturbing events involving the neighbours, Mona consults Aksel, a doctor researching sleep disorders. Aksel introduces her to lucid dreaming and to the idea that a supernatural being known as the mare may be responsible for her experiences. Mona grows increasingly uncertain whether her visions are dreams or events in the waking world.


== Cast ==
Eili Harboe as Mona
Herman Tømmeraas as Robby
Dennis Storhøi as Aksel
Siri Black Ndiaye as Liv
Peter Førde as Martin
Gine Therese Grønner as Siren
Preben Hodneland as David


== Production and release ==
Nightmare marked Rasmussen's feature directorial debut; she also wrote the screenplay. The film was produced by John Einar Hagen and Einar Loftesnes for Nordisk Film Production and Handmade Films in Norwegian Woods. Oskar Dahlsbakken was the cinematographer, Sjur Aarthun and Brynjar Lien Aune edited the film, and Martin Smoge composed the music. Filming took place in studios and on location in Bergen during spring 2021.
The film's world premiere took place at Fantastic Fest on 25 September 2022. It subsequently screened in the official competition at the Sitges Film Festival and at the 2022 BFI London Film Festival. Nordisk Film Distribusjon released it theatrically in Norway on 17 February 2023. An advance screening was held at the IFC Center in New York City on 18 September 2023

articles.title: Rock Creek Township, Wabaunsee County, Kansas
articles.text:
Rock Creek Township, Wabaunsee County, Kansas

Rock Creek Township is a township in Wabaunsee County, Kansas, United States. As of the 2020 census, its population was 45.


== History ==
Rock Creek Township was established in October 1872 from the western part of Wilmington Township. The first settlers in what would become Rock Creek Township were Ed. Baker, W. Cooper, Mr. Zink and J. R. Wolfe, who settled in 1859. The first school in Rock Creek Township was built in 1873.
Rock Creek Township was home to the now-extinct town of Chalk. The town was founded in the 1850s and originally named Chalk Mound after the limestone and chalk-like deposits in the area. The township and town had a significant African American population with the arrival of Exodusters. Most farmers in the township by 1885 were from Indiana, Ohio, and New York. Chalk had a peak population of around 500 people during the 1880s. The down began declining and the post office was closed in 1907, however, organizations and businesses such as Chalk's 4-H club continued well into the 20th century.


== Geography ==
Rock Creek Township covers an area of 65.87 square miles (170.6 km2), 0.37% of it water. The east branch of Munkers Creek flows through it, as well as Rock Creek.


=== Adjacent townships ===


== Demographics ==
As of the 2020 census, the township had a population of 45, giving a population density of 0.69 people per square mile (0.27 people/km2). The racial makeup of the township was 80.0% White, 4.4% Asian, 2.2% Black of African American, 2.2% from some other race, and 11.1% from two or more races. Hispanics or Latinos of any race were 13.3% of the population.
The 2020–2024 American Community Survey estimated that the township contained 55 households and 55 housing units.

articles.title: Be'er Sheva Natural Region
articles.text:
Be'er Sheva Natural Region

The Be'er Sheva Natural Region or Beersheba Natural Region is a natural region in the Beersheba Subdistrict, in the Southern District of Israel. Beersheba is the largest city in the natural region. 


== Geography ==

The natural region consists of a wide swath of southern Israel in the northern Negev Desert. It is adjacent to the West Bank. It has an area of 2,002 km2. The largest city in the natural region is Beersheba, which contains roughly 40 percent of the natural region's population. Two other important cities in the natural region are Rahat, the largest Arab city in Israel, and Arad, the easternmost city in the natural region. The natural region contains the al-Kasom Regional Council along with portions of the Bnei Shimon, Neve Midbar, and Tamar regional councils.


== Demographics ==
The natural region has a population of at least 527,255 residents, making it by far the most populous natural region in the Southern District. This population figure does not
include Bedouins who live in unrecognized villages, meaning that the actual resident population is higher. The natural region is roughly evenly divided between Jews and Arabs. The Jews live in Beersheba, Arad, the Beersheba suburbs of Lehavim, Meitar, and Omer, and the Bnei Shimon and Tamar regional councils. The Arabs, almost all of whom are Negev Bedouin, live in the seven official Bedouin cities (Rahat, Lakiya, Hura, Tel Sheva, Segev Shalom, Kuseife, and Ar'ara BaNegev), as well as the villages of the al-Kasom and Neve Midbar regional councils, and many more unrecognized villages scattered across the natural region. 


== Administrative local authorities ==


== Voting Patterns ==
In the 2022 election, 40 percent of voters in the natural region voted for the parties of the right-wing coalition led by Benjamin Netanyahu, while 34 percent voted for the Arab parties and 24 percent voted for the parties of the center-left coalition led by Yair Lapid.

articles.title: Gerry Raymond
articles.text:
Gerry Raymond

Gerard Leo Raymond (born June 6, 1959) is an American former professional football offensive guard who played for the Boston/New Orleans/Portland Breakers of the United States Football League (USFL). He played college football for the Boston College Eagles and was selected by the New York Giants in the fourth round of the 1982 NFL draft.


== Early life ==
Gerard Leo Raymond was born on June 6, 1959, in Lewiston, Maine. He attended Lewiston High School.


== College career ==
Raymond enrolled at Boston College to play college football for the Eagles. He was a four-year letterman from 1978 to 1981. As a senior in 1981, he earned Associated Press (AP) third-team All-American and AP first-team All-East honors.


== Professional career ==
Raymond was selected by the New York Giants in the fourth round, with the 102nd overall pick, of the 1982 NFL draft. He was waived on September 6 before the start of the 1982 regular season.
Raymond was claimed off waivers by the Baltimore Colts on September 7. He was active for three games but did not play. An additional seven games were cancelled due to the 1982 NFL players strike. Raymond was released by the Colts on November 24, 1982.
On December 22, 1982,  Raymond signed with the Boston Breakers of the upstart United States Football League (USFL) for the 1983 USFL season. He started all 18 games for the Breakers in 1983, earning College & Pro Football Newsweekly All-USFL honors as the team finished with an 11–7 record. He started all 18 games for the newly-renamed New Orleans Breakers in 1984, garnering The Sporting News All-USFL recognition as the Breakers went 8–10. He played in 15 of 18 games for the Portland Breakers in 1985. The USFL folded after the 1985 season.
Raymond signed with the New Orleans Saints on May 17, 1986. On August 18, it was reported that he had been placed on injured reserve. He was waived in late October 1986.


== References ==

articles.title: Elnizar Lohman
articles.text:
Elnizar Lohman

Elnizar Lohman (Chinese: 艾力尼扎尔·罗合曼; pinyin: Àilìnízhā'ěr Luōhémàn; born 14 April 2008) is a Chinese professional footballer who plays as a centre-back for Chinese Super League club Qingdao West Coast.


== Early life and youth career ==
Lohman was born on 14 April 2008 in Xayar County, Aksu Prefecture, Xinjiang. He grew up in the Evergrande Football School youth system. At age 11, he went to train at the Xinjiang Football Training Centre.


== Club career ==


=== Early career ===
In March 2026, Lohman joined Guangdong Chenxing Juli from the Evergrande Football School on a free transfer.


=== Qingdao West Coast ===
On 15 July 2026, Qingdao West Coast officially announced the signing of Lohman from Guangdong Chenxing Juli.
On 17 July 2026, Lohman made his debut for Qingdao West Coast in a Chinese Super League match against Chengdu Rongcheng, starting and playing 70 minutes before being substituted. In the match, he recorded one tackle, four clearances, and two successful aerial duels. He was substituted in the 70th minute with Qingdao West Coast leading 1–0; Chengdu Rongcheng equalised six minutes later through Felipe, and the match ended 1–1.

articles.title: Broughton Hall, Camberwell
articles.text:
Broughton Hall, Camberwell

Broughton Hall, formerly known as Tara, is a former mansion and now residential aged care facility, located at 2 Berwick Street in Camberwell, in the City of Boroondara, in the inner eastern suburbs of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia.
Built in 1858 on the traditional lands of the Wurundjeri people, the house was added to the Victorian Heritage Register on 18 April 1996 in recognition of its historical and architectural significance; and was also added to non-statutory lists by the Victorian branch of the National Trust on 30 October 1958 and the now defunct Register of the National Estate on an unknown date.


== History ==
Tara – as it was then called – was constructed in c. 1858 for Sir John O'Shanassy, one of the colony's early immigrants and three times Premier of Victoria, between 1857 and 1863. The mansion was designed by J. M Barry, and the facade was completed by 1859. Later in 1883, tenders were called by William Salway for ‘additions, alterations and repairs to Tara, Camberwell for Mr. O’Shanassy’, and, prior to that, by architects William Ellis for new stabling. The Argus of 1884 described the completed interior decoration by Robert Reid and the reconstruction of the interior by William Salway. Reid achieved a great deal of publicity for his creations in the 1880s. His designs from the Ducal Palace at Mantua were used in J. M. Bruce’s Wombaleno where The Argus commented that the cabinet work, gas brackets, brass door furniture were locally made although the carpets and ‘hanging’ were imported from the ‘Old Country’.
By 1884, Matthew Patrick O’Shanassy was the resident owner of the eighteen-roomed mansion, Tara, and the surrounding 19 hectares (46 acres). A brief change of occupancy occurred in 1888 when George Langridge, auctioneer, leased Tara. He also purchased 18 hectares (45 acres) of the grounds and subdivided it in this boom year of 1888. Matthew O’Shanassy regained possession by 1893 until his death in 1900 after which John Coupar, warehouseman, owned and occupied the house. Mrs Annie Coupar continued there for many years during the early part of the twentieth century, followed by a Mrs M Leets in the 1930s. The house was the Tara Guest House in the 1930s. During Mrs Cooper’s period, the lots between Tara and Burke Road were divided into the Tara Estate.

articles.title: Bay Terrace Shopping Center
articles.text:
Bay Terrace Shopping Center

The Bay Terrace Shopping Center is an open-air shopping mall in the Bay Terrace, Queens, New York City. Located at the intersection of 26th Avenue and Bell Boulevard, the center contains retail stores, restaurants, a supermarket, a movie theater, and other services. It is owned and operated by Cord Meyer Development, a real estate development company based in Queens.


== History ==


=== Development and opening ===
The development of the shopping center accompanied the postwar residential expansion of Bay Terrace. During the 1950s, Cord Meyer Development sold portions of land associated with its family's holdings in Bayside for residential development. The company retained a portion of the property for commercial use, providing shopping facilities for the growing neighborhood.
Construction of the Bay Terrace Shopping Center began in 1960, and the center developed during the following decade alongside the surrounding residential community. Its location near near the Clearview Expressway and the Cross Island Parkway made it accessible to residents of Bay Terrace and nearby neighborhoods.
By the early 1990s, the shopping center was undergoing changes to accommodate new retail uses and increased commercial activity. In 1992, a renovation and expansion project was underway, approximately three decades after the center's original development.


=== Redevelopment ===
In October 2023, Cord Meyer Development announced a multiyear redevelopment initiative known as Moving Forward. The project was intended to modernize the shopping center and adapt it to changes in retail, including the growth of online shopping and demand for experiences beyond conventional storefronts. The planned improvements included renovations to building exteriors, parking areas and pedestrian walkways, as well as additional landscaping, outdoor seating and spaces for community events. The project also included upgrades to dining facilities and connections between different levels of the shopping center.
The redevelopment was planned in phases to allow businesses to continue operating during construction. The initiative also sought to make the center more suitable for pedestrians and visitors who use the property for dining, recreation and community activities, in addition to shopping.
In June 2024, construction was underway on several elements of the project, including a new fitness facility in a redeveloped building that had previously housed Victoria's Secret an

articles.title: Murad Al Maamari
articles.text:
Murad Al Maamari

Captain Murad Al Maamari (Arabic: مراد المعمري, romanized: Murād al-Maʿammarī, IPA: [muˈraːd ʔal-maʕmari]) is an Omani former navy officer, entrepreneur and businessman. The first harbourmaster of Sohar Port, he is Oman's first certified marine surveyor.


== Early life and education ==

Murad Ahmed Mohammed Ahmed Al Maamari was born in the village of Harmul, located in the Wilayah (Province) of Liwa, in Oman's Al Batinah North Governorate. He is the brother of Omani politician and activist Talib Al Mamari. Born into a fishing family, Captain Murad learned traditional line, net, cage, and trawler fishing in his youth. He began his military training as an officer cadet, completing academic and navigational studies at the Sur Naval Training Centre. He subsequently attended Britannia Royal Naval College in Dartmouth in the United Kingdom, graduating with first-class honurs. In 2024, Captain Murad received a doctorate in business administration from Kazan Federal University in Kazan, Russia. 


== Navy career ==
Following his graduation, he joined the Royal Navy of Oman as a junior lieutenant, serving as a navigation and communications officer. During his naval service, he held roles as a gunnery officer, operations officer, and welfare officer. Within five years, he rose through the ranks to serve as captain of a warship and was awarded His Majesty's Sword of Honour. Captain Murad later joined the Merchant Navy, serving aboard merchant vessels trading across the Arab states of the Persian Gulf, Yemen, Iran, and other regions.


== Business career ==
Following his service in the Royal Navy of Oman and subsequent work aboard merchant vessels, Captain Murad pursued a career in the commercial maritime sector. Following the creation of the Sohar Industrial Port Company (SIPC), Captain Murad was appointed harbourmaster for the Port of Sohar in 2003 to oversee vessel and cargo operations at the port. In addition to his work at Sohar Port, he was Oman's representative on the committee responsible for the Rules and Regulations of GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) Seaports. 
In May 2017, Captain Murad participated in a 13-member business delegation from the North Al Batinah branch of the Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry to Minsk, Belarus. He signed a memorandum of understanding on behalf of Omani businesspeople to establish a joint investment company with Belarusian partners.

articles.title: Bugwere Kingdom
articles.text:
Bugwere Kingdom

The Bugwere Kingdom is one of the 17 officially recognised traditional kingdoms in Uganda. Located in eastern Uganda, it is one of the four kingdoms within the Bukedi sub-region. It is the home of the Gwere people, who constitute roughly 1.9% of Uganda's total populaiton, though notable Bagwere communities exist outside the kingdom's borders.
Bugwere is formally recognised as a kingdom under Ugandan law. However, the Uganda constitution and =Institution of Traditional or Cultural Leaders Act, 2011 define the kingdoms as purely cultural institution without political power. As such, the Bugwere government's powers are limited to tasks such as promoting and protecting tradition, cultural autonomy, popular participation, community development and fostering unity among the people of the region.


== History ==
According to myth, the Gwere people originated in Bunyoro during their reign of the Kitara Empire. When the Chwezi dynasty's rule over Kitara collapsed, the Bagwere people migrated east to their modern territories.
In the late 19th century, Bugwere was brought under British colonial rule, becoming part of the Protectorate of Uganda. It was administratively amalgamated with neighbouring territories to form the Bukedi district. Independence in 1962 did not result in the establishment of a Bagwere monarchy, unlike in many neighbouring territories though these were abolished in 1967 following the Mengo crisis.
The restoration of monarchies in 1993 and the Ugandan constitution of 1995 opened the possibility for the formation of a Gwere monarchy. In 2006 the Bugwere Kingdom was founded, with Kintu Mubala proclaimed as the first Ikumbania. Mubala was however never crowned. Following the enactment of a new constitution for the kingdom in 2013, John Wayabire I was proclaimed Ikumbania and subsequently recognised by the Ugandan government.
Wayabire I died on 7 February 2021 from Covid-19. This triggered a succession dispute between Wayabire's son, Geoffrey Wayabire II, and Kintu Mubala, who had never renounced his claim to the Gwere throne.
Following multiple years of mediation, an agreement between the two claimants in September 2026 set forth that an electoral process was to be implemented to solve the dispute, giving the heads of the 78 Bugwere clans the decision to elect an Ikumbania.

articles.title: Observance (film)
articles.text:
Observance (film)

Observance is a 2015 Australian film directed by Joseph Sims-Dennett. It premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in Montreal in July 2015.


== Synopsis ==
Parker is paid to move into a building and spy on a woman in her apartment.


== Cast ==
Stephanie King as Tenneal/Subject 1
Lindsay Farris as Parker Woodhouse
Brendan Cowell as Employer
Benedict Hardie as Charlie
Tom O'Sullivan as Bret Buchanan
John Jarratt as Snitch
Roger Ward as Conspirator


== Reception ==
On review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, the film has an approval rating of 71% based on 17 reviews.
The Hollywood Reporter says "the picture draws on everyone from Cronenberg and early Polanski to Shane Carruth in the construction of its existential mystery. While in the end many viewers will find that mystery frustratingly unresolved, many will be moved enough to talk about it; buzz at fests could well lead to an arthouse deal."
The Sydney Morning Herald's Jake Wilson gave it 3 stars and says "Farris modulates his uneasy reactions with skill, but never manages to turn Parker into an interesting character. A bit more humour, and a stronger sense of a society surrounding the main characters, might have allowed Sims-Dennett to lure us further into his sinister imaginative world."
Luke Buckmaster in the Guardian gave it a 3 star review and wrote "Observance feels poised on a knife edge, on some occasions tinkering on the precipice of excellence and on others feeling at risk of slipping into a cabin fever B movie. Somehow Sims-Dennett and his peculiar thriller stand their ground. Whatever you make of the film’s oblique thinking-person’s ending, and whether or not it cuts the mustard from a storytelling point-of-view, Observance is undoubtedly an impressive achievement."
Richard Scheib of Moira gave it 2 stars and noted "The great frustration about Observance is that it is all build-up and no third act. It never provides any answers as to what is going on. There is no explanation about the infection or where it is coming from – in fact, this only seems there in a couple of scenes but the film never pushes it for the sense of a growing sense of decay and horror as you get in Contracted and especially Thanatomorphose."

articles.title: Juventus (choir)
articles.text:
Juventus (choir)

Juventus is a mixed choir based at the University of Latvia. Founded in 1920, it is the oldest university choir in Latvia. Over the years, the choir has been led by some of Latvia’s most distinguished choral conductors, including Haralds Mednis and Daumants Gailis. Since 2014, its artistic director has been Valdis Tomsons.


== History ==
The mixed choir Juventus was founded in 1920 by conductor Artūrs Bobkovics under the name University of Latvia Student Choir. It was the first Latvian choir to promote Latvian choral traditions abroad, performing concerts in Estonia and Lithuania. During World War II, the choir continued its activities but, owing to a shortage of male singers, was forced to prepare a repertoire for a women’s choir.
In 1950, Bobkovics retired and was succeeded by Haralds Mednis, a conductor at the Latvian SSR State Opera and Ballet Theatre. Mednis led the choir for seven years before his choice of repertoire came under harsh criticism from the ruling Communist Party. In 1957, he was replaced by Daumants Gailis.
Under Gailis’s leadership, Juventus achieved some of the greatest successes in its history, winning first prize in the choir competition at the Latvian Song and Dance Festival four times, in 1970, 1973, 1977, and 1985. In 1988 the choir took part in the events of the Singing Revolution by raising the flag of Latvia in Gaudeamus Festival in Vilnius.
Following the restoration of Latvia’s independence in 1990, Juventus became an active participant in international choral competitions and festivals. Its achievements include Grand Prix awards at the Stasys Šimkus International Choir Competition in Klaipėda, Lithuania (2011), the Montreux Choral Festival in Montreux, Switzerland (2017), the International Choral Festival Mundus Cantat in Sopot, Poland (2018), and the Tampere Vocal Music Festival in Tampere, Finland (2025).
Juventus also regularly collaborates with musicians outside the traditional choral sphere. In 2015, the choir performed at the Positivus Festival alongside DAGAMBA and Sinfonietta Rīga. It has also collaborated with Latvian singer Dons.

articles.title: Ken Heupel
articles.text:
Ken Heupel

Ken Heupel is an American former college football coach. He served as the head football coach at Northern State University in Aberdeen, South Dakota, from 1998 to 2004, compiling a record of 44–33. Heupel led the Northern State Wolves to the Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference (NSIC) championship in 1999 and the program's first postseason bowl appearance as an NCAA Division II institution in 2004.
Heupel is the father of Josh Heupel, a former Oklahoma quarterback and the head football coach at the University of Tennessee.


== Education ==
Heupel attended Northern State University, graduating with a bachelor's degree in 1980. He subsequently earned a master's degree from the university in 1983.


== Coaching career ==


=== Northern State ===
Heupel spent 11 seasons as the assistant head coach and defensive coordinator at Northern State before becoming the program's head football coach in 1998.
In his first season as head coach, Heupel guided the Wolves to an 8–3 record. Northern State improved to 9–2 in 1999, completing an undefeated 8–0 conference schedule to capture the NSIC championship. The title was the program's first conference championship since 1992. Heupel was named the 1999 NSIC Coach of the Year.
Following the championship season, Northern State finished 6–5 in 2000, 4–7 in both 2001 and 2002, and 7–4 in 2003.
In 2004, Heupel led the Wolves to a 6–5 record and an appearance in the Mineral Water Bowl, the program's first postseason bowl appearance since its transition to NCAA Division II. Northern State lost to Washburn, 36–33, in the bowl game.
Heupel concluded his seven-year tenure with a 44–33 overall record. His 44 victories ranked fourth in Northern State program history at the time of his recognition in 2014.


=== Recognition ===
In October 2014, Northern State University honored Heupel during its October 25 home football game against St. Cloud State. The recognition coincided with the university's football alumni reunion weekend and marked Heupel's first return to Northern State since his departure in 2004.


== Personal life ==
Heupel and his wife, Cindy, have a son, Josh Heupel, and a daughter, Andrea. Cindy worked as a high school principal.
Josh grew up around the Northern State football program, attending team meals, watching game film, and accompanying his father to football practices and meetings. Josh later quarterbacked Oklahoma to the 2000 national championship before beginning his own coaching career.

articles.title: Romeo and Juliet: A Love Song
articles.text:
Romeo and Juliet: A Love Song

Romeo and Juliet: A Love Song is a 2013 New Zealand film created by Michael O'Neill and Peter van der Fluit and directed by Tim van Dammen. Set in a New Zealand trailer park, it is a rock opera version of Romeo and Juliet where the actors lip synch to recordings of tracks from many different musical styles. O'Neill and Van Der Fluit turned Shakespeare's text into a series of tunes which they brought to van Dammen. He helped turn them into a film with a cast that was mostly "models and interesting looking faces". It stars models models Christopher Landon and Derya Parlak as the titular characters and was filmed in 2011 at a Waipu Cove trailer park community.

The New Zealand Herald's Francesca Rudkin writes"Romeo and Juliet: A Love Song isn't without some wobbles, and some tracks aren't as lyrically clear and catchy as others, but the ambition of this project should be admired." She calls it "a brave piece of film-making for those who appreciate the storytelling magic of music and can't resist the theatrics of a musical." Sunday News says "essentially it's a one-joke film that, by the third act, has well and truly made its point. Purists might complain that the light-hearted treatment trashes the text but for the most part it's fun and proves that Shakespeare's story really is timeless." In the Press James Croot gave it 3 stars and states "although sometimes a truly jarring mix (the a cappella moments are especially grating), which actually serves to lessen the story's emotion, there are some haunting highlights, especially the quiet ballad that accompanies "that balcony scene" (which cleverly here involves Juliet standing on top of her caravan). It's those moments of black humour that lift what could have been car crash trash cinema into something with truly cult potential."

articles.title: Montressa Kirby
articles.text:
Montressa Kirby

Montressa Datone Kirby (born December 1, 1976) is an American former professional football quarterback who played for the Hamilton Tiger-Cats of the Canadian Football League (CFL). He played college football for the Jacksonville State Gamecocks.


== Early life ==
Montressa Datone Kirby was born on December 1, 1976, in Anniston, Alabama. He played high school football at Anniston High School. He threw for 1,900 yards and 20 touchdowns as a senior in 1994, helping Anniston win the class 6A state title while also earning first-team All-State honors.


== College career ==
Kirby enrolled at Jacksonville State University to play college football for the Gamecocks. He was a four-year letterman from 1995 to 1998, and a team co-captain in 1997 and 1998. 
1995 was Jacksonville State's first season in Division I. As a true freshman in 1995, Kirby split time with JeDarius Isaac. On September 6, 1997, against Southwest Missouri State, Kirby completed 28 of 48 passes for 417 yards and five touchdowns, setting single-game school records in all four categories. He finished the 1997 season with school records in completions (218), passing attempts (418), and passing yards (2,817), earning All-Southland Football League honors.
Kirby earned Southland Offensive Player of the Year honors in 1998 after completing 168 of 318 passes for 2,271 yards and 15 touchdowns while also rushing for 310 yards and seven touchdowns. He was also named an All-American in 1998. He finished his college career as Jacksonville State's all-time leader in total offense with 7,688 yards. Kirby was inducted into the school's athletics hall of fame in 2015.


== Professional career ==
After going undrafted in the 1999 NFL draft, Kirby signed with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats of the Canadian Football League (CFL) on March 24, 1999. He was the third-string quarterback during the 1999 CFL season. He dressed in all 18 games, completing two of eight passes for 16 yards and one interception while also rushing five times for 45 yards. On November 28, 1999, the Tiger-Cats won the 87th Grey Cup against the Calgary Stampeders by a score of 32–21. In May 2000, Kirby hurt his shoulder throwing at home. He failed his physical in June 2000 and was released.


== Coaching career ==
Kirby was an assistant football coach at Jacksonville State from 2002 to 2005.

articles.title: Besor Natural Region
articles.text:
Besor Natural Region

The Besor Natural Region is a natural region in the Beersheba Subdistrict, in the Southern District of Israel. Ofakim is the largest city in the natural region. 


== Geography ==

The natural region consists of the northern edge of the Negev Desert in south-western Israel, west of Beersheba and bordering both Egypt and the Gaza Strip. It is named after the Besor Stream, the longest river in southern Israel, which flows through the natural region. It has an area of 1,081 km2. The largest city in the natural region is Ofakim, which contains 58 percent of the natural region's population. There are no other towns in the natural region with more than 2,500 people. The natural region contains the Eshkol Regional Council along with portions of the Merhavim and Sdot Negev regional councils.
The Besor Natural Region was hit hard by the October 7 Hamas-led attacks on Israel. Some of the most horrific massacres and battles of those attacks, such as the Nova music festival massacre, the Be'eri massacre, and the Battle of Ofakim, took place there.


== Demographics ==
The vast majority of the residents of the Besor Natural Region are Jewish. There are no Arab towns in the natural region.


== Administrative local authorities ==


== Voting Patterns ==
In the 2022 election, 71 percent of voters in the natural region voted for the parties of the right-wing coalition led by Benjamin Netanyahu, while 26 percent voted for the parties of the center-left coalition led by Yair Lapid and 0.3 percent voted for the Arab parties.

articles.title: Madeleine Fillon
articles.text:
Madeleine Fillon

Madeleine Fillon, known as La Présidente Fillon or only as La Fillon, was a French brothel madam. La Fillon is known as the procurer of the Prince Regent, Philippe II, Duke of Orléans during the Régence. She is perhaps most known for her role in the Cellamare conspiracy of 1718, when one of the involved parties was a client in her brothel and talked to much, whch resulted in her allerting the authorities and exposed the conspiracy. 


== Early life ==
La Fillon was born to a sedan carrier in Paris. She ran away from home with a man at the age of fifteen after having refused an arranged marriage. 
After having been abandoned by her lover, she turned to prostitution to support herself. 
She sold sex to aristocratic men in the gardens of Palais-Royal, which gave her contacts among rich men. Soon, she switched to procure the services of other sex workers to the clients instead, and had thus transformed from a prostitute to a pimp and madam.  
Prostitution and brothels were banned in Paris since the Mere Cardine in 1566, but in the 18th century, brothels started to occur in Paris again. 
Having established a network of clients among rich and influential people, she was contacted by the lieutenant-general of police, Marc-René de Voyer de Paulmy d'Argenson (1652–1721), who gave her immunity in exchange for acting as a police informant.


== Career ==
La Fillon was the most famed madam in Paris of the regency period (1715-1723), which was infamous for its decadence. Her brothel was an elite brothel who served aristocratic clients. 
There is a famous story as to how she was given the nickname La Présidente Fillon. In 1710 a magistrate from Alençon by the name Fillon arrived in Paris. La Presidente Baillet, married to another magistrate, decided to pay a visit to her eqvivalent, the wife of magistrate Fillon, to show her respect. However, she arrived to the wrong Fillon, and accidentally arrived at the house of the brothel madam La Fillon instead of the wife of President Fillon. 
The misunderstanding lasted for several minutes before Madame Baillet realised were she was and left. 
Madeleine Fillon used the anecdote and spread it all over Paris, which gave her the nickname La Présidente Fillon. 
During the regency, La Fillon reportedly procured girls for the orgies of the Prince Regent the Duke of Orléans himself.

articles.title: Clyde Prickett
articles.text:
Clyde Prickett

Clyde Prickett (born October 3, 1932) is an American former professional stock car racing driver. He competed in NASCAR in the 1960s.


== Racing career ==
Prickett competed in the NASCAR Late Model Sportsman National Championship between 1954 and 1960, finishing fourth in the standings in 1955. He scored at least fifteen wins during his time in the series. Between 1961 and 1971, he also competed in the NASCAR Modified National Championship, scoring at least seven wins.
In 1965, Prickett made his NASCAR Pacific Coast Late Model Division debut at the California State Fairgrounds Race Track, finishing seventh; he finished tenth in the following race at Ascot Park. He attempted eight races in 1966, failing to finish six of the seven races he qualified for as wall as failing to qualify at Ascot Park; in the lone race he finished, he scored a sixth-place result at the California State Fairgrounds. His starts included his NASCAR Grand National Series debut at Riverside International Raceway, where he drove for Wendell Scott; he only completed eleven laps before retiring from the race with transmission issues, finishing 39th.
Prickett ran thirteen of nineteen Pacific Coast Late Model races in 1967, scoring seven top-tens with a best finish of second at Shasta Speedway; he was also awarded the pole in the season finale at Clovis Speedway and led two laps. He finished twentieth in the combination race at Riverside due to distributor issues after 104 laps.
Prickett's final Pacific Coast Late Model Division season came in 1968, where he ran a majority of the schedule; he qualified for sixteen of seventeen attempts, failing to qualify at Orange Show Speedway, and he scored nine top-tens, including his lone career win at Medford Speedway. He finished seventh in the standings. In the combination race at Riverside, his final Grand National start, he was running at he finish and scored a career-best fourteenth.

articles.title: Heorhii Mankovskyi
articles.text:
Heorhii Mankovskyi

Heorhii Borysovych Mankovskyi (Ukrainian: Георгій Борисович Маньковський; born 21 March 1987) is a Ukrainian cardiologist and specialist in interventional cardiology. He holds a Doctor of Medical Sciences degree (2026). Since 12 January 2026, he has served as director general of the Center for Cardiology and Cardiac Surgery of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine, formerly the Scientific and Practical Medical Center for Pediatric Cardiology and Cardiac Surgery. He received the honorary title of Honored Doctor of Ukraine in 2021.


== Early life and education ==
Mankovskyi earned a bachelor's degree in marketing from the National University of Pharmacy in 2008 and a master's degree in the same subject in 2010. Also in 2010, he graduated with honours from Bogomolets National Medical University with a qualification in general medicine.
He completed an internship in internal medicine at the Department of Therapy and Rheumatology of the Shupyk National Medical Academy of Postgraduate Education and qualified in cardiology in 2012. From 2012 to 2014, he undertook a clinical residency at the Department of Interventional Cardiology and X-ray Surgery of the Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology, part of the National Academy of Medical Sciences of Ukraine. In 2023, he completed specialist training in healthcare organisation and management at the Ukrainian Military Medical Academy.


== Career ==
Mankovskyi began working in interventional cardiology during his internship in the department headed by Yurii Sokolov at the Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology. From 2012 to 2015, he worked as a cardiologist in the institute's Department of Coronary and Endovascular Surgery. In 2014, he also worked in the corresponding department at Batumi Referral Hospital in Batumi, Georgia. He undertook further clinical training at Hirslanden Klinik Im Park in Zurich in 2015 and at the German Heart Center Munich in 2016.
In 2015, he joined the Scientific and Practical Medical Center for Pediatric Cardiology and Cardiac Surgery of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine as a cardiologist in its emergency interventional department. He headed the department from 2016 to 2019. He served as deputy director for scientific and clinical work from 2019 to 2023 and as medical director from 2023 to 2025. In 2023, he became an expert adviser to the Ministry of Health on cardiology and cardiac surgery.
On 12 January 2026, he was appointed director general of the centre.

articles.text:
Clemson House, Kew

Clemson House is a house located at 24 Milfay Avenue in Kew, in the City of Boroondara, in the inner eastern suburbs of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia.
The house was designed by Robin Boyd, an architect, architectural writer, educator, and commentator. Born in 1919, as a member of the Boyd family, he came from a creative family background of sculptors, painters, and architects.  
Built between 1959 and 1960 on the traditional lands of the Wurundjeri people, the house was added to the Victorian Heritage Register on 14 November 2002 in recognition of its architectural significance; and was also added to non-statutory lists by the Victorian branch of the National Trust on 18 June 1990 and the now defunct Register of the National Estate on an unknown date.


== Description ==
The Clemson house was designed by Boyd in the International style for the Clemson family and built between 1959 and 1960.
The block slopes steeply to the west from the driveway off Milfay Avenue, with a minor creek flowing down the southern boundary. The landscape includes a large mature eucalyptus dating from well before the house, and informal planting and landscaping which give a bush block feel to the place. Ellis Stones built benching of large stones to stabilise the cutting to the north of the house, and flagstone steps and paving leading to the front entrance.
The main design feature of the house is the single sweep of steeply sloping metal-deck roof in a shallow inward sloping V which floats above and shelters the simple cabin shaped dwelling enclosures below. The roof is supported on a series of eleven white scissor frames of light section timber with square timber columns forming an open colonnade along the outside of the building. The top two bays off the driveway form a carport. Two cabin like living areas with dark painted vertical boarded walls and sloping fibro roofs step down the hill, one for bedrooms and bathroom and the other the kitchen and living area. They are separated by a breezeway with a translucent roof containing the entrance and laundry. Square timber framed windows are fitted to a uniform module of half a structural bay. The final bay under the roof is a deck which stands well above ground level and is surrounded by trees and is backed by the fully glazed wall of the living area.

articles.title: London Art Exchange
articles.text:
London Art Exchange

London Art Exchange (LAX) is a commercial art gallery and art dealer in London, England.  It is operated by London Art Exchange Ltd, which was incorporated in September 2020. The gallery holds exhibitions of contemporary art and has taken part in art fairs and other art projects. In 2025, it hosted the first solo art exhibition by actor and artist Nitin Ganatra.


== History and operations ==
London Art Exchange Ltd was incorporated on 11 September 2020 as a company engaged in the retail sale of commercial art. The company's subsequent filings record its development as a registered business, with gallery activity under the London Art Exchange name recorded from 2023.
London Art Exchange operates gallery spaces in central London. In 2026, it began working with Brunswick Art Gallery in Bloomsbury, with the two galleries collaborating on exhibitions and events.


== Exhibitions and projects ==
London Art Exchange took part in the 2025 Fresh Art Fair at Alexandra Palace. Exhibitions held at the gallery during the year included Deborah Jones's Gilded Wilderness in March 2025 and Gabrielle Malak's Rêve d'Été in August 2025.
In September 2025, the gallery hosted Fragments of Belonging, the first solo art exhibition by actor and artist Nitin Ganatra, at 13 Soho Square, London W1D 3QF. The exhibition featured paintings exploring themes of identity, migration and belonging.
Exhibitions held in early 2026 included Alchemy of the Elements and The Grand Masters: 500 Years of Art on Paper.
In September 2026, London Art Exchange worked with La Maison Ani at the Jumeirah Carlton Tower in Knightsbridge on a project featuring the work of Gabrielle Malak. Two of Malak's paintings, Love Letter and Eternal Été, were displayed alongside dishes created in response to the works. The collaboration was also covered by FLO London.


== Community activities ==
In August 2024, London Art Exchange donated artworks to Hammersmith, Fulham, Ealing and Hounslow Mind (HFEH Mind). The works included Bear Club by Jakob The Artist and Since You Came Along by Mr Phantom, and were displayed at The Circle in South Ealing ahead of a planned fundraising auction. The artworks were also taken to local schools as part of workshops connected with the project.
London Art Exchange has also supported Smurfy in Soho, a West London Mind project involving the street artist Smurfy.

articles.title: Aymà
articles.text:
Aymà

Aymà was a Spanish publishing house founded in Barcelona by Jaume Aymà i Ayala and his son, Jaume Aymà i Mayol. It was the first company to release books in Catalan under the Franco dictatorship (1939-1975). 


== History ==
Created in 1942, the publishing house took its name from its founders, although the legal name went through various stages: Ediciones Aymà, Aymà Editor, Aymà SL Editores, and (from 1957 until its closure in 1983) Aymà Sociedad Anónima Editora. In 1962, father and son sold their shares to businessman Joan Baptista Cendrós, who assumed control of the society. Cendrós appointed Joan Oliver as literary director and incorporated book collections from other publishing houses into the company. In 1983, after ceasing activities, the corporation transferred some of its collections to the Enciclopèdia Catalana Foundation. 
Despite their desire to resume publishing in Catalan, which had been halted by the establishment of the Francoist regime following the Spanish Civil War, the Aymàs had no choice but to begin their venture by printing books in Spanish.  They initially opted for novels by foreign authors who had achieved international renown, such as Pearl S. Buck, G. K. Chesterton or Margaret Mitchell; the translation of Mitchell’s novel Gone with the Wind sold thousands of copies in a few days.  They also focused on popular genres like detective fiction, notably by publishing the books of the French writer Georges Simenon, creator of Inspector Maigret; later, in the 1960s, the firm introduced the work of the British novelist Ian Fleming, author of the spy series popularized by the James Bond films.    
In 1946, after having clandestinely published some titles using false imprints (such as L'aperitiu by Josep Maria de Sagarra, which claimed to have been printed in Perpignan before the Civil War), the publishing house launched the first post-war literary collection in Catalan: the Col·lecció Literària Aymà (1947–1950).   The novel La Bogeria, by Narcís Oller, inaugurated this collection, which encompassed all genres (novels, short stories, theatre, and poetry) and included works by established and emerging Catalan authors. Primera història d'Esther (1948), by Salvador Espriu, was one of the early commercial successes. 
Ediciones Aymà also promoted Catalan literature through the creation of the Joanot Martorell Prize. Established in 1947, it was the first writing competition organized under Francoism, and it lasted (with several interruptio

articles.title: Armytage baronets of Kirklees (2nd creation, 1738)
articles.text:
Armytage baronets of Kirklees (2nd creation, 1738)

The Armytage baronetcy, of Kirklees in the County of York, was created in the Baronetage of Great Britain on 4 July 1738 for Samuel Armytage, High Sheriff of Yorkshire in 1739. He was the great-grandson of Edward Armytage, younger brother of John Armytage, father of the 1st Baronet of the first creation, extinct the previous year. The 6th Baronet of the first creation had left his estates to him.
The 1st Baronet was succeeded by his eldest son, the 2nd Baronet, who sat as Member of Parliament for York. He died unmarried and was succeeded by his younger brother, George the 3rd Baronet, also Member of Parliament for York. His son the 4th Baronet served as High Sheriff of Yorkshire from 1791 to 1792, succeeded by his grandson, the 5th Baronet, a deputy lieutenant of Yorkshire.
In 1899 the title passed to the 6th Baronet, Chairman of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway Company, a deputy lieutenant of Yorkshire and high sheriff of Yorkshire in 1907. The 7th Baronet was a brigadier-general in the British Army and fought in the First World War. At the end of the Second War he was Military Governor of Hamburg in occupied Germany.
The family seat is Kirklees Park, Brighouse, Yorkshire.

The heir apparent is George Alexander Armytage (born 2001), the son of the present holder.


== Extended family ==
Reginald William Armytage (1903–1984), younger son of the 7th Baronet, was a rear-admiral in the Royal Navy. His eldest son David George Armytage (born 1929) is a captain in the Royal Navy.

Judo at the 2027 Pan American Games

Judo competitions at the 2027 Pan American Games in Lima, Peru are scheduled to be held at the Polideportivo 3, located in the Villa Deportiva Nacional cluster, in the San Luis district, in Lima, between July 31 and August 3, 2027.

articles.title: Richard Hallgarten
articles.text:
Richard Hallgarten

Richard Victor Charles Anton Hallgarten (14 January 1905 – 5 May 1932), generally known as Ricki Hallgarten, was a German painter, graphic artist, book illustrator and author of children's literature. A close childhood friend of Erika Mann and Klaus Mann, he collaborated with Erika on the children's play Jan's Wunderhündchen and illustrated her first children's book, Stoffel fliegt übers Meer (1932).


== Early life and family ==
Hallgarten was born in Munich on 14 January 1905. His father, Robert Hallgarten (1870–1924), was an independently wealthy scholar with doctorates in law and German studies, while his mother, Constanze Hallgarten (1881–1969), was a campaigner for women's rights and the peace movement. His paternal grandfather was the banker and philanthropist Charles Hallgarten. His older brother, George W. F. Hallgarten (1901–1975), later became a historian and political scientist. The family was part of Munich's educated bourgeoisie and had assimilated Jewish ancestry.
The Hallgartens lived at Pienzenauerstraße 15 in Munich's Herzogpark neighbourhood, close to the home of the novelist Thomas Mann and his family. The proximity of these families brought Hallgarten into contact with Thomas Mann's children Erika and Klaus, with whom he developed lasting friendships. The Hallgarten family home became a meeting place within Munich's literary and artistic circles.
In 1919, Hallgarten, Erika and Klaus Mann, and Gretel and Lotte Walter, daughters of the conductor Bruno Walter, established an amateur theatre group called the Laienbund Deutscher Mimiker (Amateur Association of German Mimes). The young performers staged plays in their families' homes and gardens. Members of the group also attended the private Ebermayer Institute run by Ernestine and Ottilie Ebermayer in Munich. Hallgarten's friendship with the Mann siblings was subsequently described by Klaus Mann in his autobiographical works Kind dieser Zeit (Child of This Time) and Der Wendepunkt (The Turning Point).


== Artistic career and travels ==
Hallgarten moved to Berlin in October 1924 in the hope of establishing himself as an artist. His father died the following month. At Christmas 1926, he left for Mexico and subsequently travelled to the United States, where he attempted to pursue an artistic career. In New York City, he supported himself through casual employment, including washing dishes and delivering flowers. Erika and Klaus Mann visited him during their travels in 192

articles.title: Mukat lal Sharma
articles.text:
Mukat lal Sharma

Mukat Lal Sharma is an Indian earthquake engineer and seismologist and a professor in the Department of Earthquake Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (IIT Roorkee). He is also the head of the institute's International Centre of Excellence for Dams. His work concerns engineering seismology, seismic hazard and risk assessment, strong ground-motion prediction, seismic microzonation and earthquake early-warning systems.


== Education and career ==
Sharma received a Bachelor of Science degree from Meerut University in 1982, a Master of Technology in applied geophysics from the University of Roorkee in 1985, and a PhD in earthquake engineering from the University of Roorkee in 1992. He joined the Department of Earthquake Engineering at the University of Roorkee as a scientist in 1985 and later served as a lecturer, assistant professor, associate professor and professor. He has held the Professor HAG position at IIT Roorkee since January 2018.


== Research ==
Sharma's research areas include seismotectonics, seismic hazard analysis, digital telemetered seismic arrays, satellite radar interferometry and strong ground-motion prediction. His work has included studies of seismic hazards in the Himalayan region and the development of earthquake early-warning systems.
In 2017, the Hindustan Times, in a report carried by the Press Trust of India, identified Sharma as the principal investigator of IIT Roorkee's Uttarakhand earthquake early-warning pilot. The report said the project had deployed 84 sensors in the Garhwal Himalayas from 2015 and described plans at the time to expand the system and warning infrastructure to additional parts of Uttarakhand. In a 2020 interview with Careers360, Sharma discussed earthquake risk in the Delhi–National Capital Region, earthquake-resistant construction, retrofitting and public preparedness. He explained that earthquake early-warning notifications are issued after an earthquake begins, using seismic recordings to warn locations farther from the source before stronger shaking arrives.
Sharma was a co-author of a 2024 study of the Uttarakhand State Earthquake Early Warning System published in the journal Sensors. The article examined the system in the context of seismic risk in the Himalayan region and surrounding areas of northern India.

articles.title: Joo Young-bok
articles.text:
Joo Young-bok

Joo Young-bok (Korean: 주영복; September 30, 1927 – March 14, 2005) was a South Korean military officer and politician who served as Minister of National Defense.


== Biography ==
Born in Haman, Gyeongsangnam-do, on September 30, 1927, he was a member of the Sangju Joo clan.
After graduating from Ogimachi Commercial Middle School in Osaka, Japan, he completed his training at the Tachiarai Army Flight School in Japan in 1945.
In 1949, he was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the Republic of Korea Air Force as part of the 8th class of Air Force officer candidates. In 1950, he was commissioned again as a first lieutenant through the 2nd intake of the Korea Air Force Academy.
He earned a bachelor’s degree in law from Dankook University in 1959 and a master’s degree from the National Defense College in 1963.
Throughout his career, he held key positions, including Inspector General of the Air Force, Director of Operations at Air Force Headquarters, Director of Personnel at Air Force Headquarters, Commander of the 11th and 10th Fighter Wings, Superintendent of the Air Force Academy, Commander of the Air Force Logistics Command, Vice Chief of Staff of the Air Force, Commander of the Air Force Operations Command, and Chief of Staff of the Air Force from 1974 to 1979. He retired from military service in April 1979.
He served as the longest-tenured Chief of Staff of the Republic of Korea Air Force.
Following the 1979 South Korean coup d'état, in which a new military faction led by Chun Doo-hwan seized de facto power, Joo became Minister of National Defense and was involved in the armed suppression of the Gwangju Uprising. After stepping down as Minister of National Defense in 1982, he served as Minister of Home Affairs. In April 1997, he was sentenced by the Supreme Court to seven years in prison for his role in the 1979 South Korean coup d'état and the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement— specifically for carrying out key tasks during the insurrection and the act of rebellion—but he was later granted a pardon.

articles.title: All Morgen ist ganz frisch und neu
articles.text:
All Morgen ist ganz frisch und neu

"All Morgen ist ganz frisch und neu" (Every morning is quite fresh and new) is a morning hymn with a text written by Johannes Zwick in 1541. The Lutheran hymn became popular again in the 1920s and was then connected to a 1537 melody by Johann Walter. It appears in hymnals including the Protestant Evangelisches Gesangbuch and in many songbooks. It has been translated into English as "Each morning brings us fresh outpoured" and into other languages.


== History ==
The jurist and theologian Johannes Zwick worked in Konstanz as an important figure of the Reformation in the region. He was also active in education of children and care for refugees. He wrote the text of "All Morgen ist ganz frisch und neu", originally in eight stanzas of four lines each, around 1541. It was published in 1545, after Zwick's death, in a booklet Christlicher ganz tröstlicher Unterricht (Christian quite comsoling lesson).
In 1927 two hymnologists found the text of the Lutheran hymn. For publication, they shortened it to four stanzas and connected it to a melody that Johann Walter had composed for Luther's "Vom Himmel hoch, da komm ich her", but Luther used his own melody instead. Their version became popular and appears in hymnals including the Protestant Evangelisches Gesangbuch, as EG 440, and in many songbooks. The Reformed hymnal of Switzerland features six stanzas.
The hymn has been translated into English as "Each morning brings us fresh outpoured" by Margaret Barclay in 1951, into Esperanto as "Novigas freŝe ĉe l' aŭror" by Adolf Burkhardt, into French as "Fraiche et nouvelle chaque jour" by Pauline Martin, and into Polish as "Co rano łaska nowa twa" by Tadeusz Sikora.


== Text ==
The poem has four to eight stanzas, depending on the version, of four lines each, rhyming AABB. It reflects the light of every morning and connects it to God's mercy and faithfulness. The first stanza is based on a verse from the Book of Lamentations. In the following stanzas, several aspects of light are explored. The last stanza is a prayer for steadfast faith without separation from God.

articles.title: Ignacija Fridl Jarc
articles.text:
Ignacija Fridl Jarc

Ignacija Fridl Jarc (born 2 April 1968) is a Slovenian philosopher, literary critic, translator and politician. She has been serving as Minister of Culture of Slovenia since 2026.


== Early life and education ==
Fridl Jarc was born on 2 April 1968 in Slovenj Gradec, PR Slovenia, Yugoslavia. She got a degree in comparative studies and a PhD in 2006 in philosophy with a thesis Plato’s Doctrine of Truth from the Perspective of Beauty and Art.


== Career ==
She have a career in cultural criticism, teaching and institutional management. She also worked at the Slovenec newspaper and at the University of Ljubljana as an assistant teacher of History of the Philosophy, before spending a decade working in management and design in the private sector. In 2018, Fridl Jarc joined the cultural institution Slovenska matica as secretary-editor, where she subsequently took on responsibilities for the management of its activities and professional services. At the same time, she pursued an academic career at the Nova University, where she served as Dean of the Faculty of Slovenian and International Studies between 2023 and 2024 and has taught courses on Slovenian literature and culture.
Her academic work has focused, amongst other topics, on the philosophy of Plato and Slovenian literature. She is the author of the monograph Language in the Philosophy of the Ancient Greeks (2001), devoted to language in the philosophy of ancient Greece, and has contributed to the translation into Slovenian from Ancient Greek of a collection of fragments by the pre-Socratic philosophers. Fridl Jarc is also the author of Fragments of the Pre-Socratics (2012). 
Between 2020 and 2022, Fridl Jarc served as State Secretary at the Ministry of Culture under Minister Vasko Simoniti. After leaving this office, she returned to Slovenska matica. She is member of the Slovenian Democratic Party and since 2025 she is the president of its Cultural Forum.
In May 2026 Fridl Jarc was announced as the Minister of Culture of the Janša new cabinet. She was sworn in on 4 June 2026.

articles.title: Unified State Register of Legal Entities
articles.text:
Unified State Register of Legal Entities

The Unified State Register of Legal Entities (Russian: Единый государственный реестр юридических лиц, abbreviated ЕГРЮЛ / EGRUL) is centralized official database of legal entities in the Russian Federation, including companies and other organizations established under Russian law. It records key information about each legal entity, such as its registered name, legal address, founders or participants, management, registration details, and liquidation status. It is used by government authorities, businesses, courts, banks, and other parties to verify a company's legal existence and registration information.


== History ==
After the dissolution of the Soviet Union in December 1991, Russia's entity-registration system was fragmented. Different public authorities and local administrations maintained registration records, and there was no single, comprehensive federal register equivalent to today's EGRUL. The earlier system involved several types of records and authorities such as regional and municipal registration authorities. Depending on the legal form and location, companies could be registered by local administrations, regional authorities, or specialized registration bodies, such as Moscow's Registration Chamber (Russian: Московская регистрационная палата) which was established by the Mossovet and the Government of Moscow. While tax authorities maintained taxpayer information, tax registration and the legal registration of a company were not yet integrated into the same unified state register. An important part of this system was the network of registration chambers, particularly in major cities and regions. These chambers were not one unified national institution. They were separate bodies operating under the applicable registration rules, often established by regional or municipal authorities. Their responsibilities included registering newly established companies, recording amendments to their founding documents, and issuing registration certificates.
The transition was governed principally by Federal Law No. 129-FZ of 8 August 2001, which entered into force on 1 July 2002. Government Resolution No. 319 of 17 May 2002 designated the Ministry of Taxes and Levies as the authorized registration authority. Following its establishment, registration chambers were liquidated.
