articles.title: A.M. Madeira Andebol SAD
articles.text:
A.M. Madeira Andebol SAD

Académico Marítimo Madeira Andebol SAD, commonly known as Madeira SAD or A.M. Madeira Andebol SAD, was a Portuguese men's handball team based in Funchal, Madeira. Established on 29 September 1998 by Académico do Funchal and C.S. Marítimo, the team competed in the highest division of Portuguese handball, winning the national championship in 2004–05 and the Portuguese Handball Cup in 1998–99.
Madeira SAD participated regularly in European competitions; its greatest European achievement was reaching the final of the 2018–19 EHF Challenge Cup, losing to Romanian club CSM București.
In 2022, the joint sporting organisation was reorganised, with Marítimo assuming control of the First Division team. The existing company adopted the name Marítimo da Madeira Andebol SAD and continued competing in Andebol 1 under Marítimo's identity. Académico returned to independent senior competition, taking over the Second Division position previously occupied by Marítimo's own handball team.


== History ==


=== Foundation (1998) ===
Handball developed as an organised sport in Madeira during the 1970s, with men's teams participating in national championships by 1985. During the following decade, the island's clubs established themselves in the Portuguese national league system. C.S. Marítimo had reached the First Division in 1994–95, whilst Académico do Funchal won the Second Division championship in 1995–96, securing promotion to the top flight. The two clubs subsequently competed independently in the Portuguese First Division, becoming established representatives of Madeiran men's handball.
In the 1997–98 season, Marítimo was challenging for a place among the championship's top four teams, which would compete for the national title and European qualification. Académico, despite operating with a more limited squad, had secured its First Division status. The clubs met in March 1998 while negotiations were already underway to establish a joint sporting company. The proposed partnership sought to consolidate the clubs' senior men's handball resources within a single professional organisation, providing an opportunity to develop a more competitive Madeiran team, capable of challenging the leading mainland clubs and securing regular participation in European competitions. The arrangement also addressed the financial pressures associated with maintaining senior teams at the highest national level.

articles.title: Xiuningella
articles.text:
Xiuningella

Xiuningella is an extinct, enigmatic fossil from the early Ediacaran, and was alive around 602 Ma in the Lantian Formation. It has an slender, cylindrical-shaped body, and is regarded as either putative bilaterian-grade organism, a putative cnidarian-grade organism, or an epibenthic macro-algae, the latter of which is more favoured. It is a monotypic genus, containing only Xiuningella rara.


== Discovery and naming ==
Fossils of Xiuningella were first found and reported from the black shale "Member II" of the Lantian Formation in Xiuning County, Anhui Province of South China in 2011 as "Type D", and which were formally described and named in 2016.
The generic name Xiuningella derives from the place name of Xiuning County, the county in which the fossils were found from. The specific name rara derives directly from the Latin word of the same spelling, "rara", to mean "rare", in reference to the notably rarity of the fossils in the Lantian Biota.


== Description ==

Xiuningella rara are centimetre-scale, slender cylindrical-shaped fossils, set on top of a short and narrow stalk with a potential holdfast preserved in some specimens. The main cylindrical tube, which attains a height of only 18 mm (0.7 in) and a width of 1.4 mm (0.06 in), has a notable axial longitudinal structure occurring in it, which itself is only 0.25 mm (0.010 in) in width and runs along only half the length of the tube. All of this is set upon a short, narrow stalk, which is only 1.3 mm (0.051 in) in length and 0.4 mm (0.016 in) in width, constricting to just 0.2 mm (0.008 in) at the contact point between the stalk and the main body. At the base of this stalk can be found a bulbous, holdfast-like structure, which is 0.5 mm (0.020 in) in diameter.


== Affinities ==
When the fossils were first reported by Yuan et al. in 2011, they had designated fossils of Xiuningella as "Type D", and regarded the form as possibly being a bilateral, worm-like animal similar to the scalidophorans, with the axial structure being its digestive tract, whilst the stalk and bulbous structure were the proboscis. They also made comparisons to a similarly putative bilateral metazoan fossil from the Miaohe biota of the Doushantuo Formation, which is also a ribbon-like compression with an axial structure of a similar width. articles.title: Wane (wood)
articles.text:
Wane (wood)

In woodworking, wane is the part of the rounded surface of a log that is left on a piece of sawn timber. English dictionaries define it as a defective edge or corner of a board or plank, where bark remains or wood is missing because of the curvature of the log. The Century Dictionary describes it as a bevelled edge on a board sawn from a log that has not been squared. A board with wane is waney or wany. In lumber, wane is a defect that grading rules limit; in furniture it may be kept on purpose as a live edge. The noun comes, through Middle English, from Old English wana, "defect". The French term is flache and the Spanish term is gema.


== Causes ==
Wane appears when planks or beams cannot be cut properly because the tree is curved or because the wood grain cannot be followed. A slab, the plank taken by the first cuts on the body of the tree, is a waney plank; the 1814 vocabulary of joinery of the architect J. M. R. Morisot describes it as good for little. In his vocabulary of carpentry, Morisot defined bois flache or bois flacheux as timber whose edges are not sharp and which could not be squared without much waste. He defined équarrir as cutting a log to give it a square shape, and dédosser as dressing a timber with the saw to sharp edges (vive-arête) by cutting away the waney parts.


== Grading and use ==
In lumber grading, wane is a defect. The Wood Handbook of the United States Forest Products Laboratory defines it as bark or lack of wood on the edge or corner of a piece of lumber, regardless of cause, except manufactured eased edges. Wane is one of the visual sorting criteria used to sort lumber into stress grades, with knots, slope of grain, checks and splits, shake, density, decay, annual ring count and percentage latewood, and pitch pockets. Requirements of appearance, fabrication, or ample bearing or nailing surfaces generally impose stricter limitations on wane than does strength. Wane is therefore limited in structural lumber on that basis. In practice, a grade often contains pieces with the strength of a higher grade, because of grade reduction for appearance factors such as wane that do not affect strength.
In furniture, the wane can instead be kept as a feature. Live edge furniture shows the rough, natural and irregular edge of the timber as a design element of the piece, rather than trimming the wood to straight lines. articles.title: Rule of law in India
articles.text:
Rule of law in India

The rule of law in India concerns how far public officials exercise power through known, general and fairly applied rules, and how far citizens, firms and officials are bound by and protected by them in practice. The Constitution of India commits the state to equality before the law, protection of life and civil liberties, and judicial review. The Supreme Court treats rule of law as part of the Constitution's basic structure. Historians trace the idea to debates in ancient texts and the colonial rule, under which law both restrained and entrenched state authority.
Scholars across disciplines have noted a gap between the constitutional commitment and practice. Economists link slow courts and weak contract enforcement to economic development; political scientists have noted criminalisation of politics and growing executive powers of the government; and sociological and anthropological studies have documented the coexistence of formal law with community justice and discretionary policing. Government of India has done several procedural and digital reforms; supporters and critics continue to debate whether the rule of law in India is strengthening or weakening.


== Concept ==

British jurist A. V. Dicey identified three elements of the rule of law: the supremacy of law over arbitrary power, the equality of all persons before ordinary courts, and protection of rights through judicial decisions. Later theorists have distinguished this "thin" definition from a "thicker", more substantive definition of the rule of law, which includes fundamental rights, democracy, and other parameters such as public rules, generality, impartiality, and prospective and uniform application.


== History ==


=== Ancient and medieval traditions ===
Ancient Indian texts discuss the sources of law and rulers' duties. The Arthashastra names four bases of legal decision—dharma, legal transactions, custom and royal edict—and states that each later one prevails over the earlier.


=== Colonial rule ===
The East India Company and later the British Raj presented codified law and courts as a source of legitimacy, and enacted codes such as the Indian Penal Code of 1860.


=== Constitution-making ===
The Constituent Assembly adopted a written constitution with enforceable fundamental rights and judicial review.

articles.title: International Government Communication Forum
articles.text:
International Government Communication Forum

The International Government Communication Forum (IGCF; Arabic: المنتدى الدولي للاتصال الحكومي) is an annual forum on government communication held in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, since 2012 and organised by the Sharjah Government Media Bureau. Held under the patronage of the Ruler of Sharjah, Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al-Qasimi, each edition brings together former heads of state and government, officials and communication and media specialists.


== History ==
The first edition was held in 2012, organised by the Sharjah Media Centre, later renamed the Sharjah Government Media Bureau. The second edition, on 24–25 February 2013, was held under the theme "Effective Communication, Unified Message"; its guest of honour was the then Turkish prime minister Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, and the former United Nations secretary-general Kofi Annan and the former Arab League secretary-general Amr Moussa were among the speakers. The Ruler of Sharjah opened the third edition at Expo Centre Sharjah in February 2014, with the last Soviet president, Mikhail Gorbachev, as guest of honour.
At the sixth edition (22–23 March 2017) the chairman of the Sharjah Media Council, Sheikh Sultan bin Ahmed Al Qasimi, launched the International Government Communication Centre, a research and knowledge centre managed by the Sharjah Government Media Bureau. The news website Sharjah 24 was launched during the 2015 forum. The eighth edition, in March 2018, was held under the theme "Digital Millennium. Where To?" with more than forty speakers from sixteen countries, among them the President of Mauritius, Ameenah Gurib-Fakim, the former Polish president Lech Wałęsa, the inventor of the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee, and the Wikipedia co-founder Jimmy Wales.
The tenth edition was held on 26–27 September 2021 at Expo Centre Sharjah under the theme "Historic Lessons, Future Ambitions", and was opened by Sultan bin Ahmed Al Qasimi. The Ruler of Sharjah opened the fourteenth edition on 10 September 2025 under the theme "Communication for Quality of Life", with 237 speakers in more than 110 events, including 51 panel discussions and 22 workshops, on food security, public health, education, environmental sustainability and the green economy.

articles.title: Sultan bin Mohammed bin Sultan Al Qasimi
articles.text:
Sultan bin Mohammed bin Sultan Al Qasimi

Sheikh Sultan bin Mohammed bin Sultan Al Qasimi (Arabic: سلطان بن محمد بن سلطان القاسمي) is the Crown Prince and Deputy Ruler of the Emirate of Sharjah in the United Arab Emirates, posts he has held since 1999, chairman of the Sharjah Executive Council, and chairman of the emirate's Energy Council since 2024. He is a member of the ruling Al Qasimi family. He is the son of Sheikh Muhammad bin Sultan Al Qasimi, the UAE's first minister of public works, and a grandson of Sheikh Sultan bin Saqr Al Qasimi II, Ruler of Sharjah from 1924 to 1951.


== Crown Prince and Deputy Ruler ==
On 11 May 1999 (25 Muharram 1420 AH) the Ruler of Sharjah, Sheikh Sultan bin Muhammad Al-Qasimi, issued an Emiri decree appointing him Crown Prince of the emirate with the style "His Highness the Crown Prince", and he has since been described as Crown Prince and Deputy Ruler. He chairs the Sharjah Executive Council, the emirate's highest executive body, and in that capacity oversees the implementation of major development projects and the performance of the emirate's government entities.


== Other positions ==
In October 2024 the Ruler of Sharjah issued an Emiri decree forming the emirate's Energy Council under his chairmanship, with the head of the Sharjah Petroleum Department, Sheikh Sultan bin Ahmed Al Qasimi, his deputy Sheikh Mohammed bin Ahmed Al Qasimi, the chairman of the Sharjah Electricity, Water and Gas Authority and the director-general of the Central Finance Department as members. He chairs the board of the Sharjah Academy for Police Sciences and previously chaired the board of directors of Sharjah Islamic Bank for about eighteen years.


== Personal life ==
His mother is Sheikha Meera bint Ahmed bin Rashid Al Mualla; his brothers are Ahmed and Salim, and his sisters are Jawaher, the wife of the Ruler of Sharjah, Jamila, Sawsan and Fatima. He is married to Sheikha Azza bint Saud bin Sultan Al Qasimi, and they have four sons, Mohammed, Saud, Ahmed and Salim, and a daughter, Meera. On 21 December 2024 the marriage contract of his son Sheikh Ahmed to Sheikha Mariam bint Sultan bin Ahmed Al Qasimi, daughter of the Deputy Ruler of Sharjah, was concluded in the presence of the Ruler of Sharjah, and the wedding was held in September 2025.

articles.title: Geneve Flynn
articles.text:
Geneve Flynn

Geneve Flynn is an Australian  speculative fiction editor, author and poet. She co-edited the anthology Black Cranes: Tales of Unquiet Women (2020) with Lee Murray, which won the Bram Stoker Award and the Shirley Jackson Award, and contributed to the poetry collection Tortured Willows (2021), which won a second Bram Stoker Award.


== Background ==
Flynn is of Chinese-Malaysian heritage and her family lived in several countries during her childhood.


== Career ==


=== Editing ===
Black Cranes: Tales of Unquiet Women, co-edited by Flynn and Murray, was published by Omnium Gatherum in 2020. It won the 2020 Bram Stoker Award for Best Anthology and the 2020 Shirley Jackson Award for Best Edited Anthology, and was a finalist for the British Fantasy Award and the Aurealis Award. Raw Dog Screaming Press announced a hardcover edition in 2022, with an afterword by Nancy Holder.
Flynn was assistant editor of Relics, Wrecks, and Ruins, an anthology created as the legacy of Australian fantasy author Aiki Flinthart in support of the Flinthart Writing Residency at the Queensland Writers Centre.


=== Poetry ===
Tortured Willows: Bent. Bowed. Unbroken., a collaboration with Murray, Christina Sng and Angela Yuriko Smith, was published by Yuriko Publishing in 2021 and extends the themes of Black Cranes. It won the 2021 Bram Stoker Award for Best Poetry Collection and placed second for the Elgin Award for full-length collections. Reviewing the collection for LitReactor, Sara Tantlinger described it as an exploration of Asian identity, resilience and power. In 20224 her work, You Swallowed Your Tongue won the Australasian Shadows Awards poetry prize.


=== Fiction ===
Flynn's short fiction has been published by Flame Tree Publishing, Crystal Lake Publishing, Black Spot Books and PseudoPod. Her story "They Call Me Mother", published in Classic Monsters Unleashed won the 2022 Aurealis Award for Best Horror Short Story; her story "Lidless Eyes that See" was a finalist in the same category.


== Awards and honors ==

In 2022 she was awarded a Queensland Writers Fellowship as part of the Queensland Literary Awards (with Melissa Ashley and Mary-Rose MacColl).

articles.title: Royal European Academy of Doctors
articles.text:
Royal European Academy of Doctors

The Royal European Academy of Doctors (Spanish: Real Academia Europea de Doctores; Catalan: Reial Acadèmia Europea de Doctors; RAED) is an academy of holders of doctoral degrees in all fields of knowledge, based in Barcelona, Spain. It traces its origins to 1914, received the title "Royal" in 1989 and added "European" to its name in 2016.


== History ==
The academy began in 1914 as the Agrupación de Doctores Matriculados de Cataluña (Association of Registered Doctors of Catalonia). After a congress of doctors held in Barcelona in 1915, the association was formally constituted in May 1919, with Àlvar Esquerdo as its first president. It was renamed in 1920 and again in 1924, during the dictatorship of Miguel Primo de Rivera. Its activity declined sharply under the Second Spanish Republic and during the Spanish Civil War, and resumed in 1943.
In 1989 it became a public-law corporation under the name Acadèmia de Doctors, regulated by Decree 90/1989 of 13 March, and on 2 October 1989 King Juan Carlos I granted it the title "Royal". It adopted its current name in 2016, after the Spanish Royal Household communicated on 2 June 2016 its approval of the addition of "European". The King of Spain holds the academy's honorary presidency. Alfredo Rocafort became its president in 2012.


== Membership ==
A doctorate is required for numerary membership, which is open to citizens of the European Union and limited to 150 members. According to the newspaper Ara, in March 2024 the academy had 100 numerary, 51 corresponding and 36 honorary academicians, and the academy says that 19 Nobel laureates are among its honorary members. Its honorary members also include the former presidents Rosalía Arteaga of Ecuador and Luis Alberto Lacalle of Uruguay. The academy is based on the third floor of the Foment del Treball building on Via Laietana in Barcelona.


== Medal of Honour ==
The academy's statutes allow its governing board to award the RAED Medal of Honour (Medalla de Honor) to people it considers deserving. The academy presented the medal to King Juan Carlos I on 29 May 2008, and in March 2025 to Sultan bin Ahmed Al Qasimi, Deputy Ruler of the Emirate of Sharjah, an award Emirati media described as the "Golden Medal of Honour". The academy also awarded its Centennial Medal to the former Brazilian president Dilma Rousseff on 12 April 2018.

articles.title: Chocolates Sönksen
articles.text:
Chocolates Sönksen

Chocolates Sönksen, previously named La Bonbonniere, was one of the first chocolate factories in Brazil. Created by Alfredo Richter in 1887, the family company was controlled by his wife and children after his death in 1912, where it got its new identity as "Sönksen".
It quickly became one of the biggest companies of Brazil's sweet sector, and in 1924 it became an anonymous society, being presided over the Falchi family and Ofner's representatives.
Despite its previous success, the company began declining during the 70s, where the rise of new competitors, distribution problems, and changes in São Paulo's industrial parks made it declare bankruptcy in 1983.
On 5 September 1983, a fire of unknown cause destroyed part of the factory, causing millions in losses. The fire happened during the eviction process, which was being confronted by the old employees. It led to the accusation that the employees were to be blamed for the losses, but the investigation was inconclusive.


== History ==
The factory, originally named La Bonbonniere, was founded in 1887 by Alfredo Richter at Líbero Badaró Stret, Central Zone of São Paulo. It was one of the first chocolate factories of Brazil.
In 1912, after Richter's death, his wife Alwine Sophia Sönksen took over the family business. Afterwards, her children began managing the factory under the name of Christian Sönksen & Cia. The factory was moved to a rented building on Vergueiro Street, which was acquired by the company in 1922. In 1924, its corporate name changed to Sönksen Irmãos & Cia and in 1948 it became an anonymous society, named Sönksen Produtos Alimentícios S.A. In 1958, the company inaugurated a store on 24 de maio Street.

Up until the 70s, Sönksen was one of the main companies of the chocolate market in Brazil, losing only to Kopenhagen, but it was soon put on sale and opened a voluntary arrangement in 1977, officially declaring bankruptcy in 1983. Its sudden downfall happened for several reasons. The first was the emergence of new competitors in the market segment, such as Nestlé, Lacta and Garoto. Sönksen's products were more expensive some were sold only at the factory, which led to lower sales. Other important factors were that the company wasn't under the direct management of the Sönksen family, being presided over the Falchi family and Ofner's representatives. articles.title: 1968 Oregon State Senate election
articles.text:
1968 Oregon State Senate election

Elections to the Oregon State Senate were held on November 5, 1968, to elect 15 candidates to the Senate to serve four-year terms, and two to fill the two-year remainders of two unexpired terms. The Democratic Party won 9 seats to the Republicans' 8, resulting in a Senate composition of 16 Democrats and 14 Republicans, a net gain of three for the Republicans. Of the 16 Democrats, three of them were conservative Democrats, and 13 were liberal. The same coalition of conservative Democrats and Republicans that had held Senate leadership since 1961 held on, with Democrat Debbs Potts being re-elected Senate President on January 13, 1969 with 17 votes. Some within the liberal Democratic faction attempted to nominate Republican leader Anthony Yturri, who declined to seek the post due to his pledge to Potts.
This election used the same district boundaries used for the 1962–1966 general elections passed after the 1960 U.S. census. Since the passing of a 1965 law, senators in multi-member districts were elected to designated single-member positions beginning with the 1966 election, as opposed to plurality block voting which had been used previously. Incumbent senators in multi-member districts were assigned numbers based on their vote totals at their most recent general election, with the highest voted candidate getting position 1, second-highest position 2, and so on. Primary elections were held on May 28.

articles.text:
List of crossings of the Lower American River

This is a list of crossings of the Lower American River, the approximately 23 miles (37 km) reach of the American River between Nimbus Dam and its confluence with the Sacramento River, in Sacramento County, California. Crossings include highway and local-road bridges, railroad bridges, and bridges used by pedestrians and cyclists. Several form connections within the American River Parkway.
The existing crossings are listed from downstream to upstream, beginning near the river mouth in Sacramento. Crossings of Lake Natoma and the river upstream of Nimbus Dam are outside the scope of this list. Parallel structures at the same crossing are grouped where indicated. Former crossings are listed separately.


== Existing crossings ==
Dates refer to construction of the listed structure unless an opening, rehabilitation or conversion date is specified. Caltrans bridge numbers are provided where verified in its state or local-agency inventories. A dash indicates that a construction date or bridge number is not supplied here.


== Former crossings ==
The following table includes documented earlier bridges, including predecessors at sites still used for river crossings. The entries are not an exhaustive inventory of nineteenth-century bridges or ferries. Surviving bridges converted from railway or industrial use to trails remain in the existing-crossings table.

Reed also records the establishment of ferries after the March 1861 flood made the lower river’s bridges unusable.


== Upstream boundary ==
Nimbus Dam marks the upstream limit of this list. It was constructed in 1952–1955 and began operating in 1955. As a water-control structure, it is described separately from the transportation bridges.


== Proposed crossings ==
The City of Sacramento has studied a Truxel Bridge crossing between Truxel Road in South Natomas and Sequoia Pacific Boulevard in the River District.

articles.title: Carrie Laben
articles.text:
Carrie Laben

Carrie-Edmund Laben (born 1978) who has also published as Carrie Laben, is an American writer of horror and weird fiction. Their story "Postcards from Natalie" won the 2016 Shirley Jackson Award for Short Fiction. They are the author of the novels A Hawk in the Woods (2019) and Smoke Season (2026).


== Early life and education ==
Laben grew up in western New York. They earned a BS from Cornell University and an MFA from the University of Montana. They live in Queens, New York.


== Career ==
Laben's short fiction has appeared in Clarkesworld, The Dark, Apex, Indiana Review and Outlook Springs. Their story "Something in the Mermaid Way", published in Clarkesworld in March 2007, was nominated for the inaugural Shirley Jackson Award for Best Short Story. "Postcards from Natalie", published in The Dark in July 2016, won the 2016 Shirley Jackson Award for Best Short Fiction, presented at Readercon in July 2017.
Also in 2017, Laben won the Documentary Essay Prize for Writing from the Center for Documentary Studies at Duke University for the essay "The Wrong Place", which draws on their experience as a birdwatcher. They have held residencies including the Anne LaBastille Memorial Writer's Residency (2015), a MacDowell residency (2018) and the Brush Creek Residency (2019).
Laben's debut novel, A Hawk in the Woods, was published by Word Horde in March 2019. It follows twin sisters with supernatural abilities who return to their family's cabin in Minnesota. The novel received a starred review from Publishers Weekly, which called it a "gruesome, wry horror story", and from Foreword Reviews. Reviewers noted its debt to H. P. Lovecraft's "The Thing on the Doorstep".
Their second novel, Smoke Season, was published by Word Horde on June 30, 2026. The publisher describes it as a novel in the tradition of Arthur Machen.
Laben has also written nonfiction about birds for the blog 10,000 Birds and Birding magazine.

articles.title: Mount Mercer (homestead)
articles.text:
Mount Mercer (homestead)

Mount Mercer is a historic pastoral property and homestead at Mount Mercer, in the Western District of Victoria, Australia, approximately 30 kilometres south of Ballarat. Established during the nineteenth century, the estate was originally associated with pastoralist George Mercer and later the Bell family. Its bluestone homestead, constructed during the early 1870s, forms part of a rural complex that has undergone several subdivisions and changes of ownership. The property was acquired by the Passionists in 1973 and was subsequently returned to private agricultural use. The homestead and its surrounding farmland were sold in February 2025.


== History ==
Mount Mercer originally formed part of the holdings of the Derwent Company, which controlled extensive areas of land in the Port Phillip District. Following the company's dissolution in 1842–1843, the Mount Mercer run passed into the ownership of George Mercer, together with the Weatherboard station and portions of the Gheringhap estate. Mercer retained the property until January 1853, when it sold.
By 1859, the property was acquired by the Bell family, who held substantial pastoral interests in western Victoria. Robert Lewis Bell occupied Mount Mercer during the latter half of the nineteenth century. A substantial homestead was constructed from locally quarried bluestone during 1871–1873, providing a permanent residence for the property's occupants. The single-storey building featured spacious interior rooms, high ceilings and verandahs overlooking the surrounding agricultural land.
On 7 December 1881, Robert Lewis Bell was killed by lightning while returning to the estate with his wife, Robina. Bell had been travelling from Ballarat by horse-drawn buggy and passed through Buninyong at approximately 4:30 pm, where his wife joined him for the remainder of the journey. At around 6 pm, as the couple reached the entrance to their property, a lightning strike brought down their horse and struck bell. The electrical discharge travelled along the right side of his body, scorching his clothing and discolouring his skin. Bell was killed instantly. The horse subsequently broke free from the buggy, throwing both occupants to the ground, befoer running loose around a nearby paddock.
Nearby residents noticed the unattended horse and, concerned that an accident had occurred, went to investigate. They discovered Bell's body near the stables, with his wife standing beside him. Although shaken

articles.title: Marina Raphael (brand)
articles.text:
Marina Raphael (brand)

Marina Raphael is a handbag brand founded by fashion designer Marina Raphael and launched in 2018. The brand has collaborated with Swarovski, influencers, and other designers on handbag collections.


== Production and distribution ==
The brand's founder, Marina Raphael, serves as its designer and CEO. Its handbags are produced in Florence, Italy, with quality control outsourced to Swarovski in Austria. Its handbags have been stocked by Harrods, Harvey Nichols, LuisaViaRoma, Neiman Marcus, Moda Operandi, and El Corte Inglés.
The brand's handbags have been carried by Queen Máxima of the Netherlands, Jessica Alba, Paris Hilton, Katie Holmes, Jennifer Lopez, Emma Roberts, and Alicia Keys.


== Collaborations ==
Since 2020, the brand has collaborated with a number of designers and companies. These have included L'Oréal's Vichy Laboratories, for which Raphael also served as the face of its Greek advertising campaigns, influencer Evangelie Smyrniotaki, and stylist Georgia Medley. A collaboration with creative director and sustainability consultant Doina Ciobanu resulted in the brand's first sustainable handbag collection, using a form of vegan leather made as a by-product of industrial apple processing.
Raphael has also collaborated extensively with Swarovski. A collaboration announced in 2020 with Swarovski Group Global Creative Director Giovanna Battaglia Engelbert led to the first handbag line released under the Swarovski marque in the jeweller's 125-year history. A second collaboration followed in 2024, when Swarovski Creators Lab and Marina Raphael released a limited-edition Valentine's Day capsule collection of crystal-embellished handbags.
In 2022, the brand collaborated with fine jewellery designer Eugenie Niarchos on a series of bespoke handbags accompanied by a collection of non-fungible tokens.

articles.title: Académico do Funchal
articles.text:
Académico do Funchal

Académico Clube Desportivo do Funchal (ACDF), commonly known as Académico do Funchal, is a Portuguese sports club based in Funchal, Madeira. Founded on 1 February 1971, the club has participated in several sports, most notably handball, in which its men's and women's teams achieved national success during the 1990s.
The women's handball team won the Portuguese championship in 1997–98, three consecutive Portuguese Cups between 1992–93 and 1994–95, and the Portuguese Super Cup in 1996–97. The men's team won the national Second Division championship in 1995–96 and subsequently competed in the Portuguese First Division.
In 1998, Académico became a founding partner in two separate sporting companies: the men's Académico Marítimo Madeira Andebol SAD, established with C.S. Marítimo, and the women's Madeira Andebol SAD, established with Club Sports da Madeira and Clube Desportivo Infante Dom Henrique. The club subsequently concentrated on youth handball before returning to independent senior men's national competition in 2022.


== History ==


=== Foundation and development (1971–1990) ===
Académico was founded on 1 February 1971 as Clube Desportivo Madeirense by José Manuel Freitas de Silva and a group of local sports enthusiasts. Initially involved in football, the club subsequently adopted the names Académico de Fátima and Académico Clube Desportivo do Funchal. Handball and volleyball were introduced during its early development, with João Coutinho playing an important role in establishing the handball section.
Handball became the club's principal sport, with men's and women's teams competing in regional and national championships. Académico developed a youth training programme and established the Madeira Handball International Tournament in 1985. The competition brought together youth teams from Madeira, mainland Portugal and other countries, becoming an established event in the island's sporting calendar.
Participating teams came from countries including Angola, Brazil, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Russia and Switzerland. The tournament was organised by Académico until 2019.


=== National success (1990–1998) ===
Académico emerged as one of Madeira's leading handball clubs during the 1990s. Its women's team won three consecutive Portuguese Cups from 1992–93 to 1994–95, the Portuguese Super Cup in 1996–97 and the national championship in 1997–98. articles.title: Dirk Bos
articles.text:
Dirk Bos

Dirk Bos (13 September 1862 – 6 May 1916) was a Dutch businessman and politician. He was a member of the Dutch House of Representatives from 1901 until his death in 1916 for the left-liberal Free-thinking Democratic League (VDB), serving as its leader from 1913 to 1916.  


== Early life ==
Dirk Bos was born on 13 September 1862 in Groningen to Derk Bos, and Maria Reintjes. Dirk Bos grew up in a middle class family of relatively modest means, his father being a watchmaker, failed businessman and later a government employee, and his mother being an ambitious non-conformist who insisted on giving Dirk and his five siblings a good education. After attending secondary school in Groningen, Bos studied mathematics and physics at the University of Groningen, where he met Pieter Jelles Troelstra while part of the executive of the Groninger Studentencorps Vindicat atque Polit. He graduated in 1883, and became a teacher at a secondary school in Winschoten, where he would work until 1893. In 1888, Bos also obtained a doctorate at the University of Groningen. 
In the following years, Bos became involved in business, founding a mortgage bank in Veendam together with his brother-in-law in 1890 and becoming co-director of a trading firm in coffee and tea in Winschoten in 1893. 


== Political career ==
Bos first entered into politics on the local level, being elected to the municipal council of Winschoten for the local progressive liberal electoral association in 1893. The year prior, Bos had been chosen as chairman of that electoral association. In 1898, Bos joined the national executive of the Liberal Union.
In the 1897 Dutch general election, Bos first ran for the House of Representatives for the Liberal Union in the strongly progressive liberal Winschoten electoral district. Bos's support for free trade alienated the wealthy farmers of the district, who supported protectionist radical Boelo Luitjen Tijdens instead.
In 1901, Bos broke with the Liberal Union over Bos's advocacy for universal suffrage, joining the left-liberal Free-thinking Democratic League (VDB). During the general elections that same year, Bos ran again in Winschoten, and was victorious, being able to obtain the support of many of the wealthy farmers who had previously voted for Tijdens, who chose not to run.

articles.title: Brooke Warra
articles.text:
Brooke Warra

Brooke Warra (also known as Brookelynne Warra) is an American writer of horror and weird fiction. Her chapbook Luminous Body (2019) won the Shirley Jackson Award for Best Novelette. Her short fiction has appeared in anthologies including Looming Low and Horror for RAICES, in horror magazines, and on horror podcasts.


== Early life ==
Warra grew up in a Finnish-American community in the Pacific Northwest, which has provided inspiration for her work.


== Career ==
Warra's work has appeared in horror magazines, including Sanitarium and Under the Bed, and she wrote episodes for the horror fiction podcasts The Wicked Library and Victoria's Lift.
Her story "Heirloom" appeared in Looming Low: Volume I which debuted at NecronomiCon in Providence, Rhode Island. The anthology was a finalist for the 2017 Shirley Jackson Award for Edited Anthology. Her story "Cherub" was published in Strange Aeons in 2017 and reprinted in 2019 in Yearning to Breathe Free, a charity anthology benefiting RAICES; the same year she contributed a story to Nightscape Press's Horror for RAICES.
In October 2019, Dim Shores published her chapbook Luminous Body, a novelette illustrated by her daughter, Zoe Liegh. It won the 2019 Shirley Jackson Award for Best Novelette.
Warra was one of the editors of the relaunched Sanitarium Magazine in 2019.


== Themes ==
Warra's fiction combines weird fiction with body horror and domestic subject matter. Her publisher, Dim Shores, described Luminous Body as exploring pregnancy, motherhood and family through a cosmic body horror lens. In a 2019 interview on the podcast The Outer Dark, she discussed the book's focus on layered relationships among generations of women, grief, and her interest in moving beyond familiar tropes for women characters in horror.

articles.title: Dale Robinson (American football)
articles.text:
Dale Robinson (American football)

Dale Robinson (born September 2, 1983) is an American former football linebacker. He played college football for the Arizona State Sun Devils and was named the Pac-10 Co-Defensive Player of the Year (with Haloti Ngata) in 2005.


== Early life ==
Dale Robinson was born on September 2, 1983, in Brooklyn, New York. He played high school football at Holy Cross High School in Queens, New York. He set a school record with 118 tackles his senior year, earning Queens Player of the Year and second-team all-state honors.


== College career ==
Robinson played college football at Division II C.W. Post from 2001 to 2002. As a freshman, he led the team in tackles with 97. He transferred to play at Glendale Community College in 2003. Robinson was named the Western States Football League Defensive Player of the Year after posting 10 sacks, three forced fumbles, two fumbles recoveries, and a team-leading 114 tackles.
Robinson then transferred to play for the Arizona State Sun Devils. He started all 12 games at linebacker in 2004, totaling 50 solo tackles, 43 assisted tackles, 4.5 sacks, and one interception. He was named honorable mention All-Pac-10 Conference for his performance during the 2004 season. Robinson played in all 11 games, starting 10, during the 2005 season, accumulating 74 solo tackles, 41 assisted tackles, four sacks, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery, and one pass breakup. He led the Pac-10 in solo tackles and shared the Pac-10 Co-Defensive Player of the Year award with Haloti Ngata.


== Professional career ==
Robison was criticized by pro scouts for his lack of size and speed. He posted a "dismal" 4.76 second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine. After going undrafted in the 2010 NFL draft, Robison signed with the Indianapolis Colts on May 1. He was waived on August 2 but re-signed on August 13. During the preseason, he made six solo tackles and two assisted tackles. Robison was waived again on September 3, 2006, before the start of the regular season.
Robinson was assigned to the Arizona Rattlers of the Arena Football League (AFL) on March 15, 2010. He was placed on reassignment on April 14 but assigned to the Rattlers again on June 17. Overall during the 2010 AFL season, he recorded five solo tackles, two assisted tackles, one sack, one interception, and one blocked kick. On August 16, 2010, he was placed on the team's suspended list.

articles.title: Newbury Township, Kansas
articles.text:
Newbury Township, Kansas

Newbury Township is a township in Wabaunsee County, Kansas, United States. As of the 2020 census, its population was 1,091.


== History ==
Newbury Township was established in 1870 from land formerly part of a Potawatomi reservation that was opened for settlement a year earlier. In September 1872, Maple Hill Township was created from the eastern part of Newbury Township, and in July 1875 Kaw Township was created from the north. The first settlers in what would become Newbury Township after it opened up for non-Native Americans were J. W. Phillips and F. Muchendahler in 1869. The first school in the township was built in 1870.


== Geography ==
Newbury Township covers an area of 78.431 square miles (203.14 km2), 0.57% of it water. Mill Creek, Kuenzli Creek, Paw Paw Creek, Snokomo Creek, Joe Woody Branch, Dog Creek, Mulberry Creek, and Turkey Creek all flow through it.

articles.title: Long (model railways)
articles.text:
Long (model railways)

Long was a Danish manufacturer of model railways. Founded in 1948, it produced a variety of tracks and train models in HO scale, primarily of Danish prototypes, until its dissolution in 1965.
Long's models were noted for their build quality and correctness, but were eventually unable to compete in the market.


== History ==
Long was founded by toolmaker Poul Schneider, who wished to build a model railway together with his son, but was limited by post-World War II shortages of tracks. He began manufacturing tracks on his own, initially marketed in cooperation with the hobby store "Model & Hobby"; as the track pieces, at 25 cm (9.8 in), were longer than familiar Märklin tracks, and English-language names were in vogue at the time, they received the brand name "Long". In cooperation with his colleague Christian Nielsen, Schneider launched a proper production of tracks from a workshop at Theklavej, Copenhagen, in 1948.
Rolling stock production began in 1952, beginning with a freight wagon, and soon followed by a DSB class MO railcar. The Danish State Railways (DSB) introduced the Class MY diesel locomotives in 1954 and had unsuccessfully requested a model from German manufacturers Märklin and Fleischmann. However, a collaboration between DSB and Long was commenced, and Long's class MY model entered serial production in 1956, as the first ever model of that locomotive. The first copy was given to King Frederik IX, who had a keen interest in railways.
In 1960–61, Schneider left the company, leaving Christian Nielsen's nephew John Engberg in charge, and the workshop moved to a new location in Gladsaxe. In its later years, Long's models grew increasingly austere due to financial pressures, and the company closed in the spring of 1965.


== Products ==

Long's track pieces, the company's first product, used a three-rail system compatible with Märklin's HO-scale tracks. Their lineup grew to include straight and curved tracks as well as switches and crossings and other layout accessories.
The range of Danish rolling stock included motive power in the form of a DSB class MO railcar and a Class MY diesel locomotive, as well as passenger carriages of class CC and CD, and a variety of freight wagons. The MO and MY models were initially made for three-rail AC systems, but later also available for two-rail DC.
Between 1956 and 1964, Long train models were marketed in Norway through the company Norlek; they were sold under the brand name Tekno to avo

articles.title: Battle of Zari (2018)
articles.text:
Battle of Zari (2018)

On August 30, 2018, militants from the Islamic State – West Africa Province attacked a Nigerian military base at Zari, Borno State, Nigeria, killing 48 soldiers.


== Background ==
Boko Haram emerged in 2009 as a jihadist social and political movement in a failed rebellion in northeast Nigeria. Throughout the following years, Abubakar Shekau unified militant Islamist groups in the region and continued to foment the rebellion against the Nigerian government, conducting terrorist attacks and bombings in cities and communities across the region. On 7 March 2015, the group publicly declared allegiance to the Islamic State and became known as the Islamic State – West Africa Province (ISWAP).
ISWAP by late 2016 was relegated to an insurgency, but in late 2017 starting with the Magumeri ambush began attacking Nigerian army bases in rural areas of Borno State. In June 2018, the group attacked Gajiram and killed 45 Nigerian soldiers and civilians. A few days later, they attacked Balagallaye, Garunda, and Jilli and killed over 100 more soldiers.


== Battle ==
At the time of the battle, the base at Zari was defended by soldiers in the 145th Battalion. At about 4pm local time on August 30, a large number of jihadists with vehicles stolen during previous attacks arrived at the base. Fighting lasted for about an hour. The Nigerian army intervened with at least one J-7 jet and one Mi-35M helicopter. The helicopters reportedly killed three jihadist leaders, although the aircraft did not carry out any strikes in fear of hitting their own troops. Overpowered on the ground, the Nigerian troops temporarily retreated from the base until ground and air reinforcements arrived.
The attack was claimed the following day in a short statement published by ISWAP. On September 8, ISWAP published a video of the attack, showing 75 of its fighters dressed in uniforms along with the bodies of Nigerian soldiers, some of whom were shot at close range.


== Aftermath ==
According to an anonymous Nigerian officer to AFP, at least 30 soldiers were killed in the attack. Another military source told AFP a similar toll, although the second source said that many jihadists were killed in a bombing. ISWAP's video shows 15 bodies of Nigerian soldiers.

articles.title: Emaan (TV series)
articles.text:
Emaan (TV series)

Emaan is a Pakistani television serial written by Zafar Mairaj, and aired on Express Entertainment in 2012. The leading cast includes Ahsan Khan, Hassan Niazi, Syed Jibran, Munawar Saeed and Ukrainian model and actress Anna Liko in the titular role.


== Plot ==
A middle-class unemployed Karachi boy, Aazi, befriends an American girl, Kathy, through the internet at the internet cafe of his friend, Sajid. They eventually fall in love, and Kathy decides to come to Pakistan because of her fascination with the Eastern family value system. Aazi, however, sees her as an opportunity to obtain a green card. Sajid helps him in this regard, hoping to shift there once Aazi had gone. Aazi's entire family is excited about Kathy's arrival and lends him a helping hand. His sister-in-law, Bushra, is especially excited and even learns to speak English. However, Aazi's father, Rooh Ullah, is unhappy because Aazi has made changes without consulting him. This leads Rooh Ullah to leave the house and move to retirement home.
Kathy's plan to come to Pakistan is initially cancelled, but she eventually arrives a day later. Upon her arrival, Kathy turns out to be sweet and pleasant toward everyone and surprises the family by speaking Urdu. All the family members, along with Sajid and his wife, Naheed, shower Kathy with affection and give her special treatment.
Despite passing a few days, Kathy mentions nothing about her marriage plan, which makes Aazi worried. He eventually asks her about her decision of the marriage, and Kathy refuses to change her religion, contrary to their previous understanding, saying that she needs some time. Fearing that Aazi might change his religion, Aazi's mother, Razia, brings Rooh Ullah back home. Rooh Ullah returns home and develops a strong bond with Kathy. He makes everyone understand that if Aazi and Kathy are willing to marry while maintaining their respective religions, there is nothing wrong with it, as Islam also permits such a marriage.
Aazi and Sajid's childhood friend and neighbour, Abdus Salam, whom they also called as Molvi as he is an Imam in the neighborhood mosque, becomes involved in a difficult situation when Aazi's former girlfriend, Sumbul, elopes from her home because of Aazi. However, Aazi refuses to accept her. Abdus Salam takes her to the hospital after she becomes unconscious and later takes her to his house because she has nowhere else to go. She introduces her as Noor-ul-Huda, claiming to be a member of a Ta

articles.title: Djamel Agaoua
articles.text:
Djamel Agaoua

Djamel Agaoua (born 21 September 1969) is a French businessman and entrepreneur born on 21 September 1969 in Marseille, the founder or head of several companies in the digital economy, and chief executive officer (CEO) from 2017 to 2021 of the instant messaging company Viber, which belongs to the international group Rakuten.
In 2019, through an open letter addressed to Mark Zuckerberg and to the leading figures of the messaging and social media industry, he called for a system of self-regulation, with the aim of achieving higher standards of security in the confidentiality of exchanges between users and of ensuring greater protection of their personal data. In 2022, he joined the senior management of the media outlet Brut. 
After serving for a few months in 2024 as managing director of the NBA Europe, he took over, in October 2024, the leadership of the Kings League, the sporting league founded by the footballer Gerard Piqué.


== Biography ==


=== Youth and education ===
Djamel Agaoua, born in Marseille in September 1969, is the son of a master pastry chef of Kabyle origin. Passionate about mathematics, he was educated in the state school system and entered the École centrale Paris, from which he graduated in 1992 as an economist-engineer . He joined his first company, the international business strategy consultancy Bain & Company, where he spent four years, before moving on to the firm Roland Berger for a further three years. He left this firm in 1999 in order to found his first companies.


=== Founding and running companies ===
Djamel Agaoua co-founded his first start-up with Alexis Renard in 2000: Achatpro, a company devoted to the general procurement needs of businesses. Following a capital increase arising from a second funding round of seven million euros and a substantial stake taken in the company's capital by BRED Banque populaire[7], he sold the company in 2008 to Hubwoo, the world leader in the electronic procurement (e-procurement) market in SaaS solutions, and became the group's chief financial and human resources director[8].
In 2006 he also took over the financial management of BProcess, an electronic invoicing solution[5], which was to be sold on to Ariba in 2011; thereafter he invested in, or took part in the running of, several internet companies, such as the online gaming platform Metaboli[1]. articles.title: Piyuania
articles.text:
Piyuania

Piyuania is an extinct, enigmatic fossil from the early Ediacaran, and was alive around 602 Ma in the Lantian Formation. It has an cyathiform- to cup-shaped body, and is regarded as a putative cnidarian-grade organism It is a monotypic genus, containing only Piyuania cyathiformis.


== Discovery and naming ==
Fossils of Piyuania were first found and reported from the black shale "Member II" of the Lantian Formation in Xiuning County, Anhui Province of South China in 2011 as "Type C" and "Type E", and which were formally described and named in 2016.
The generic name Piyuania derives from the place name of Piyuan, a town near to where the fossils were found. The specific name cyathiformis derives directly from the Latin word of the same spelling, "cyathiformis", in reference to the cup-shaped appearance of the fossils.


== Description ==
Piyuania cyathiformis are centimetre-scale, cyathiform- to cup-shaped fossils, which bear a 2–4 mm (0.079–0.157 in) wide globose holdfast structure at the base, and a small crown of unbranching tentacles inside the body on top. The body itself ranges between 15–50 mm (0.6–2.0 in) in height and 5–20 mm (0.20–0.79 in) at its widest point. Inside this body, referred to as the outer integument, completely envelopes a fusiform inner structure. The structure is darker than the surrounding integument, and is possibly composed of fine longitudinal filaments, ranging between 10–35 mm (0.4–1.4 in) in height and 1–5 mm (0.04–0.20 in) at its widest point. The filaments themselves are only roughly 0.2 mm (0.008 in) at their widest, which is best seen at the middle of the inner structure. At the top end of the inner structure there can be found 8 – 20 tentacle-like structures, which range between 5–15 mm (0.20–0.59 in) in width and 0.1–0.2 mm (0.004–0.008 in) in width. It is noted that the tentacle-like structures could be loose continuations of the filaments seen in the inner structure.


== Affinities ==
When the fossils were first reported by Yuan et al. in 2011, they had designated fossils of Piyuania as two separate types, "Type C" and "Type E". "Type C" fossils were regarded as cnidarian-like organisms, whilst "Type E" fossils were instead regarded as worm-like organisms. During collection of more fossil material, Wan et al. noted in 2016 that it became apparent that these two forms were of the same creature, with the two differing types likely being differently preserved specimens. articles.title: Maryse Bard-Martel
articles.text:
Maryse Bard-Martel

Maryse Bard-Martel (born January 12, 1995) is a Canadian soccer coach and former player, who currently serves as interim head coach of the Montreal Roses FC in the Northern Super League.


== Early life ==
Bard-Martel began playing youth soccer at age four with CS Union des Milles-Îles. She later played youth soccer with FC Boisbriand. She was named to the 2013 Canada Summer Games All-Star Team.


== College career ==
In 2013, Bard-Martel began attending the University of Memphis, where she played for the women's soccer team. In August 2013, she was named the AAC Rookie of the Week and College Sports Madness AAC Player of the Week. In her first season, Bard-Martel set freshman program records in saves (79), shutouts (6) and minutes played (1856:59). 
In October 2014, she was named the AAC Goalkeeper of the Week. In October 2016, she was named the AAC Goalkeeper of the Week on two occasions. Over her four years at Memphis, she finished her time ranked first in career goalkeeper minutes played (7,259), second in career wins (44) and second in career saves (267).


== Club career ==
In 2013, Bard-Martel played with the Laval Comets in the USL W-League. 
In 2014, she joined the Ottawa Fury. She went unbeaten in five total starts, with a 0.207 goals-against average and a .944 save percentage, leading the team to a third-place finish in the league playoffs, after taking over as starter following an injury to starting keeper Jillian McVicker in the division championship match.
In April 2015, she signed with the Colorado Pride.


== International career ==
In 2012, Bard-Martel played with the Canada U17 team at the 2012 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. In June 2013, she attended a camp with the Canada U20.


== Coaching career ==
After graduating college, Bard-Martel served as a coach at IMG Academy before joining the Missouri State Lady Bears as assistant coach and goalkeeper coach for two seasons in 2017 and 2018.
In August 2020, Bard-Martel was hired as an assistant and goalkeeping coach with the Oklahoma Sooners women's soccer team. 
In 2022, she was name the goalkeepers coach for the Canada women's national under-20 soccer team, including at the 2022 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup. She continued to serve in the role, as of 2025.
In February 2023, she was named an assistant coach with the UConn Huskies women's soccer team.
In March 2024, she was named the goalkeeping coach with Utah Royals FC of the National Women's Soccer League.

articles.title: Mir Ali Beg I of Sheikhan
articles.text:
Mir Ali Beg I of Sheikhan

Mir Ali Beg I, also known as Mîr Elî Begê Mezin ("Mir Ali Beg the Great"), was a Yazidi prince (mir) of Sheikhan who ruled in the early 19th century. He was captured during the genocide of Yazidis by Soran emirate and executed at Geli Ali Beg waterfall after refusing to convert to Islam.


== Reign ==
Ali Beg was the son of Mir Hasan Beg, ruler of the principality of Sheikhan. By his time the principality had shrunk to a few districts inhabited by Yazidis, stretching from Dohuk to Harir and from Mosul to the Shingal mountains. Its administrative centre and the ruler's residence was the settlement of Baadre.
Under Hasan Beg, the Sheikhan principality entered a period of relative prosperity. In 1806 he oversaw the rebuilding of the Lalish sanctuary, consolidating its role as the central pilgrimage site of the Yazidi community. His reign ended with his treacherous murder at the hands of a prince of Amadiya, an event that left a lasting impression on Yazidi collective memory. In 1820, the travellers Claudius James Rich and his wife Mary Rich, spending a night at a Yazidi village, heard a lament for the slain Mir performed by a blind guitarist named Lasso. Approximately fifty years after his death, a German orientalist transcribed a poem commemorating a battle between two Bahdinan princes in which warriors from Sheikhan and Dennedi tribe avenged Hasan Beg's killing.
Hasan Beg was succeeded as Mir by Salih Beg, who was regarded with considerable respect by the Yazidi community but was murdered by an adversary in Mosul. His death initiated a prolonged period of dynastic instability and internal strife within the principality. Order was eventually restored with the accession of Ali Beg, who reunited the princely line.
Sheikhan was semi-independent but a vassal of the emir of Amedi in the Bahdinan emirate, which protected the Yazidis from hostile neighbouring Kurdish tribes. Both the Kurdish emirates and Sheikhan formed part of the Ottoman Empire. After inheriting the throne, Ali Beg built close ties with neighbouring Kurdish princes and became politically active in the region.

The British traveller Austen Henry Layard, who met Ali Beg's son Hussein Beg in 1846, describes Mir Ali Beg as popular, brave and capable enough to defend his people against the neighboring Muslims and Kurds, reporting:"The last independent chieftain of the Yazidis of Sheikhan was Ali Beg, the father of Hussein Beg. articles.title: Hôtel de Ville, Denain
articles.text:
Hôtel de Ville, Denain

The Hôtel de Ville (French pronunciation: [otɛl də vil], City Hall) is a municipal building in Denain, Nord, in northern France, standing on Rue de Villars.


== History ==

Following the French Revolution, the new town council initially met in the home of the mayor at the time. This arrangement continued until 1847, when the council led by the mayor, Adolphe Deslinsel, decided to commission a purpose-built town hall. The site they selected was an old farm on the west side of the old town square (now Place Wilson), close to the Church of Saint-Martin. The building was designed in the neoclassical style, built in ashlar stone and was completed in 1850.
The design involved a symmetrical main frontage facing onto the old town square. The complex was laid out as a main block of nine bays with a pair of arcaded pavilions in front. One of the pavilions accommodated the fire brigade, while the other accommodated the police station. The central bay of the main block featured a round-headed doorway with a moulded surround and a keystone. There were also round-headed doorways in the second and eighth bays. The remainder of the building was fenestrated by round-headed windows on the ground floor and by square-headed windows on the first floor. The central three bays were flanked by banded pilasters supporting an entablature, a cornice and a parapet and there was originally a square bell tower at roof level.
An imperial staircase, carved from blue stone and adorned with bronze goddesses, was installed in 1891. In 1947, a small museum was established in the town hall. This developed into the Musée d'archéologie et d'histoire locale (Museum of Archaeology and Local History), which still occupies the building.
In the late 1970s, in response to the decline in the local steel industry, the council led by the mayor, Henri Fiévez, decided to establish a modern town square and a modern town hall. The site they selected was on the south side of Rue de Villars. An equestrian statue of Claude Louis Hector de Villars, 1st Duke of Villars by the sculptor, Henri Gauquié, had already been installed in the area in front of the proposed town hall in 1912. It had been destroyed by German Forces in 1918 during the First World War, but recast and re-installed in 1922.
The new town hall was designed in the modern style, built in concrete and glass and was completed in around 1980. The design involved a square-shaped structure facing onto the new square. The ground

articles.title: Kuzie Kuzmanich
articles.text:
Kuzie Kuzmanich

Marine John "Kuzie" Kuzmanich (January 28, 1927 – March 19, 2016) was an American professional stock car racing driver. He competed in NASCAR in the 1960s.


== Racing career ==
Kuzmanich and his best friend Don Collins built their first stock car while in high school. He ran his first race with a forged ID under the name Fred Jackson due to being underage to compete. In the 1940s and 1950s, Kuzmanich ran local events at Jantzen Beach Arena and Portland Speedway. He won a late model championship in 1958 and picked up sponsorship from Bud Meadows Pontiac. He finished third in the standings in 1960 and second in 1961 after switching to a smaller model of car. Kuzmanich won O.A.R.A. championships at Portland in 1962 and 1963.
Kuzmanich simultaneously made his NASCAR Grand National Series and NASCAR Pacific Coast Late Model Division debut in a combination race at Marchbanks Speedway in 1960, finishing 30th; he also made a start at the California State Fairgrounds Race Track, finishing sixth. He ran one combination race in 1961, finishing eighth in his third and final Grand National start. 
Kuzmanich returned to the Pacific Coast Late Model Division in 1964, running at least thirteen races with three poles and ten top-tens and a best finish of second at Portland. He finished seventh in the standings. He made at least four starts in 1965, scoring a pole at Portland and second-place finishes at Evergreen Speedway and Portland. He made his only recorded USAC Stock Car Series start at Marchbanks in 1965, finishing sixth. Kuzmanich made two Pacific Coast Late Model starts in 1966, finishing sixth at Douglas County Speedway and scoring his first and only career win at Portland. He made three starts in 1967, crashing out of two races and finishing fourth at Portland. Kuzmanich ran his final races in the series in 1968, scoring two top-tens with a best result of fifth at Portland.


== Personal life ==
Kuzmanich was born in Portland, Oregon to Matt and Elise Kuzmanich. He graduated from Benson High School and shortly after enlisted in the United States Coast Guard, where he served as a merchant marine during World War II until his honorable discharge in August 1945. He met and married Mary Lexa in 1948, and they had two children, Nancy and Joseph; Kuzie and Mary divorced in 1991. He enjoyed yearly trips to Puerto Vallarta, Mexico during the winter, where he had many friends.

articles.title: I Wish You Way More Than Luck
articles.text:
I Wish You Way More Than Luck

I Wish You Way More Than Luck is the third studio album by American band Lo Moon, released on April 5, 2024, through Strngr Recordings and Thirty Tigers. The album was produced by the band and Mike Vernon Davis and mixed by Alan Moulder. Its ten tracks include the singles "Evidence", "Water", and "Connecticut".
The album was inspired in part by lead singer Matt Lowell's return during the COVID-19 pandemic to the chapel at Pomfret School in northeastern Connecticut, where he had attended high school. Revisiting the location prompted him to reflect on his formative experiences with music and the discovery of his artistic voice. The album's title comes from the closing line of a commencement address delivered by author David Foster Wallace at Kenyon College in 2005.


== Background and development ==
Work on I Wish You Way More Than Luck began around December 2020, following the release of Lo Moon's second album, A Modern Life (2022). During the pandemic, Lowell returned to Pomfret School in Connecticut, where he had spent four years as a student. He had originally attended the school to play hockey, but his experiences there, including the impact of the September 11 attacks on his family in New York, helped lead him toward songwriting.
At the school's chapel, Lowell revisited the place where he had first performed an original song in front of an audience. That song, "The City Cries Its Tears", began as a poem he had written after the September 11 attacks and was performed for the school community. In later interviews, Lowell described the experience as a turning point that helped him discover his interest in singing, playing guitar, and expressing himself through lyrics. Returning to the chapel during the pandemic prompted him to consider how those early experiences had shaped him as a musician.


== Recording and production ==
The band began recording material in January 2021 at a studio belonging to Adam Granduciel of The War on Drugs, after touring plans had been disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Mike Vernon Davis, who had worked with the band on its debut album, served as engineer and co-producer. The band sought a sound that more closely reflected its live performances, and Lowell credited Davis with helping create a recording environment that encouraged this approach.
The album was mixed by Alan Moulder. Lowell said that some of Moulder's mixing decisions initially surprised the band, particularly on "Waiting a Lifetime

articles.title: Leon Śliwiński
articles.text:
Leon Śliwiński

Leon Śliwiński (3 November 1915 – 14 September 1999), wartime codename "Jean-Bol", underground alias "Jean Sablon", was a Polish naval intelligence officer who served as head of maritime intelligence for Réseau F-2, a major Allied intelligence network operated in France during World War II by the Second Department of Polish General Staff. Holding the rank of Lieutenant in the Polish Navy, he directed the collection of naval intelligence across occupied France from 1940 until his arrest in late 1942.
Under Śliwiński's direction, the Marine Section of Réseau F-2 developed an intelligence apparatus encompassing the French Atlantic and Mediterranean coastlines. His network provided the British Admiralty with blueprints and reports on German submarine pen complexes at Brest, Lorient, and Saint-Nazaire, as well as coastal artillery batteries, radar installations, and Atlantic Wall fortifications. According to British and post-war evaluations, Śliwiński's section provided approximately 80 percent of all actionable naval intelligence originating from occupied France that reached London during 1941 and 1942.
Arrested in Nice in December 1942 by the Italian OVRA, Śliwiński was imprisoned in Sanremo and later in the Alpine fortress of Embrun. In September 1943, following the Armistice of Cassibile, he escaped from Embrun and evaded German security forces. In mid-1944, he crossed the Pyrenees into Spain, was interned at Miranda de Ebro camp, and secured release through British diplomatic intervention. Reaching Great Britain in July 1944, he served in the Polish Navy Headquarters and the Second Department in London, while graduating in law from the University of Oxford in 1945.
Following the war, Śliwiński settled in Casablanca, Morocco, where he established mining and maritime transport enterprises and served from 1951 to 1990 as Honorary Consul of the Polish government-in-exile. He used his commercial ventures to provide employment and economic refuge to exiled Polish military commanders who had been stripped of their citizenship by the communist authorities in Poland, including General Stanisław Gano and Rear Admiral Józef Unrug.


== Early life and background ==
Leon Śliwiński was born on 3 November 1915 in Moscow, then part of the Russian Empire, into an educated Polish family. His father, also named Leon Śliwiński, was a Warsaw attorney (adwokat), and his mother was Lidia Śliwińska (née Archipow). In 1922, following the Polish–Soviet War and the n

articles.title: Mariana Benenge
articles.text:
Mariana Benenge

Mariana Benenge (born 1998), also known as Mariana Revlon, is a Congolese-born dancer, choreographer and fashion designer based in Paris. She is known for choreography that blends street dance styles like waacking and voguing with contemporary performance, notably through her collaborations with musical artists Aya Nakamura, Ghali, Tshegue, and Yseult. An active member of the Parisian ballroom scene, Benenge is also involved in feminist and LGBTQ+ advocacy, particularly concerning the visibility of Black and queer communities, gender-based harassment, and the creation of spaces outside the male gaze.


== Early life and education ==
Benenge was born in Democratic Republic of the Congo, in 1998, and is of Luba heritage. Her early exposure to dance was rooted in Luba traditions from the Kasai region, particularly mutuashi, characterized by rhythmic hip movements and pelvic isolations, as well as modern Congolese dance styles such as ndombolo.
Raised by her mother, Claudine Benenge, whom she has credited for her foundation in community values, she moved to France at the age of 12. While working part-time jobs from the age of 15, she completed her Baccalauréat in economics and social sciences. She subsequently enrolled in a dance academy, where she was introduced to waacking, and soon afterward discovered voguing through the Parisian ballroom scene. Both styles became central to her artistic practice.


== Career ==


=== Dance and choreography ===
Benenge's early freestyle footprint was established within the competitive Parisian ballroom scene and the street dance battle culture at Centquatre (104), where she trained in underground styles like krumping, waacking, hip-hop and voguing. This environment served as a transition to the competitive circuit, leading her to compete in underground battles across Europe, including the prominent freestyle street dance tournaments Red Bull Dance Your Style and Summer Dance Forever.
She subsequently transitioned into professional commercial spaces, working as a choreographer and movement director across music videos, live performances, and contemporary dance, most notably with musical artists including Aya Nakamura, Ghali, Tshegue, Yseult, Omah Lay, Lala &ce, Bonnie Banane, Corine, and Ehla. In the fashion and beauty industries, she has provided posing and movement direction for brands including Chanel, YSL Beauté, Maison Margiela and Isabel Marant.

articles.title: Olympe's Marriage
articles.text:
Olympe's Marriage

Olympe's Marriage (French: Le Mariage d'Olympe) is an 1855 play by French writer Emile Augier, written both as a response to Dumas's 1852 play La Dame aux Camelias. Augier's drama takes place over a course of several months in the year 1854.  
The play premiered at the  Théâtre du Vaudeville on July 17, 1855..   
In 1901, Clyde Fitch adapted Olympe's Marriage into the dramedy The Marriage Game, relocating the action to Edwardian England and changing the dramatis personae's nationality accordingly. 


== Plot ==


=== Act I ===
In a fashionable watering place in the fictitious town Pilnitz, situated in Germany, the Baron de Montrichard and an elderly Marquis discuss the recent death of Olympe Taverny, a Parisian courtesan. According to newspaper reports, Olympe died in California after contracting yellow fever. As the Marquis has never returned to France since the June Rebellion, he was unfamiliar with Olympe and consequently has never seen her, while de Montrichard was a frequent customer. The Marquis is joined by the ailing Marquise and their granddaughter Genevieve de Wurzen, who has been raised in Germany and Austria. The three leave for another area of the spa. 
In the meantime, Baudel, who has occasionally interjected in the conversation between the Baron and the Marquis, decides to formally make the former's acquaintance. Although Baudel introduces himself as Anatole de Beausejours, Montrichard quickly deduces that he is not of aristocratic origins. Baudel reveals that Baudel is his patronymic name. His father was a milliner who married a wealthy woman, but Baudel's inheritance still fails to grant him entry into the world of the aristocracy. Baudel offers to pay Montrichard to stage a duel with him; thus, Baudel will be accepted by society. Montrichard is in want of money, desires to marry Genevieve, and has grown somewhat fond of Baudel, so he assents. Baudel leaves and promises to send Montrichard his seconds. 
Olympe Taverny, whose real name is Pauline Morin, enters shortly thereafter. Although Montrichard recognizes her, she assures him that he is mistaken; she insists that she is the Countess de Puygiron, another person. Montrichard knows she is lying, and calls her bluff. Pauline reveals that she is really Olympe Taverny, and has faked her death in order to ensure that she enters a life of respectability as the wife of Henri, Count de Puygiron, whose marriage has still not been revealed to his family. articles.title: Anna Akeley
articles.text:
Anna Akeley

Anna Mandler Frost Akeley (May 5, 1904 – June 26, 2004) was an Austrian-born American physics lecturer and radiologist. She taught at Purdue University from 1942 to 1971.


== Early life and education ==
Mandler was born in Vienna, the daughter of Paul Mandler and Emma Löw-Beer. Her family was Jewish, but not religious. Anna was baptized and she attended a Catholic school. Her mother was a pianist, and her father was a businessman. She studied religion in college for about a year, and earned a diploma in radiology at the Roentgen Institute, then began working as an editor and translator at a publishing house. 


== Career ==
Despite having no formal credentials, Akeley began teaching physics at Purdue University in 1942, after she fled wartime Europe for Indiana to be with her American husband. She recalled being ill-prepared to teach the subject in English, but studied with her husband to improve her subject matter and language skills. One of her first students was Nobel Prize winner Ben Roy Mottelson. In 1966 she received the Best Instructor Award in Purdue's College of Science. In 1969 she received the Helen B. Schleman Gold Medallion Award, given to the female faculty member who made extraordinary contributions to women's education at Purdue. She retired with emeritus status in 1971.
In 1995, Akeley donated the couple's extensive art collection, with works by Diego Rivera, Leonora Carrington, Käthe Kollwitz, Guillermo Meza, Rufino Tamayo, and others, to small museums, including the Smart Museum of Art at the University of Chicago, the University of South Dakota, the Purdue Galleries, and the Art Museum of Greater Lafayette. She also donated an Oxford English Dictionary to the Purdue library system, as the system's two-millionth volume.


== Personal life ==
Mandler married twice. Her first husband was named Frost. In 1942, she married American physicist Edward Stowe Akeley, the ex-husband of cryptanalyst Evelyn Niemann Akeley, and the son of Lewis Akeley. Her husband died in 1984, and she died in 2004, at the age of 100, in West Lafayette. Her papers are in the Purdue University archives.

articles.text:
Pandemonium (2023 film)

Pandemonium is a 2023 French supernatural horror film written and directed by Quarxx. Starring Hugo Dillon, Arben Bajraktaraj, Ophélia Kolb, Manon Maindivide, Carl Laforêt and Sidwell Weber, the film follows a man who discovers that he has died in a road accident and finds himself condemned to an afterlife of suffering. Its narrative incorporates elements of an anthology film, using interconnected stories to explore guilt, moral judgement and damnation.
The film is Quarxx's second feature, following All the Gods in the Sky (2018). It had its world premiere at the Neuchâtel International Fantastic Film Festival in 2023 and subsequently screened at several international genre film festivals. It received an international streaming release through Arrow Films in May 2024.


== Plot ==
Nathan awakens on a deserted, fog-covered mountain road beside the wreckage of a car and motorcycle accident. Initially relieved to have survived, he encounters Daniel, the motorcyclist involved in the collision, who tells him that they are both dead. Nathan refuses to believe him until he discovers his own body inside the wrecked car.
Two mysterious gateways appear, apparently leading to heaven and hell. As the men discuss their lives and the circumstances of their deaths, they reveal actions that may have determined their fate. Nathan admits to having ended the life of his seriously ill wife, which he considers an act of mercy, while Daniel reveals that he was responsible for the death of a young girl.
Nathan eventually enters hell, a desolate landscape populated by corpses and tormented souls. There he encounters a demonic figure and discovers that touching the bodies of the damned allows him to experience episodes from their former lives.
One such story concerns Nina, a disturbed young girl living in a large Gothic house with her family. She has formed a relationship with Tony, a disfigured man living beneath the house, whom she draws into her increasingly violent fantasies. Her story culminates in the destruction of her family.
Another story follows Julia, a mother whose teenage daughter Chloé has died by suicide after enduring severe bullying. Unable to accept the death, Julia continues behaving as though her daughter were alive. Flashbacks reveal Chloé's suffering and Julia's failure to recognise the severity of her distress.
