articles.title: Effectuation
articles.text:
Effectuation

Effectuation is a concept describing a way of deciding under uncertainty. As part of entrepreneurship research, effectuation portrays a strategy process in which an entrepreneur or a team starts from the resources already at hand and allows goals to emerge, instead of fixing a goal first and then assembling the means to reach it. Effectuation is to be used in situations, where a business needs to find new business opportunities or business models in circumstances, in which predictions are not possible due to high uncertainty. The term was introduced by the entrepreneurship scholar Saras D. Sarasvathy in 2001. A 2025 bibliometric review counted 680 journal articles on the concept published between 2001 and 2024. Effectuation has also drawn sustained criticism, over whether it qualifies as a theory and whether it accounts for how new ventures come about.


== Origins ==
The concept of effectuation was developed by the entrepreneurship scholar Saras D. Sarasvathy in 2001 as part of her doctoral work under the supervision of Herbert A. Simon and Lester Lave. She did research on how experienced entrepreneurs with several founded ventures would reason through a set of decisions in a hypothetical start-up. She found that experienced founders, in situations of great uncertainty, paid less attention to predictive information, were more concerned with limiting what they could lose, and put more emphasis on assembling partnerships. Sarasvathy found the following five principles or heuristics applied by the experienced founders:


== The five Principles of Effectuation ==
"Pilot in the plane" - Control versus Prediction: seeking influence over an unpredictable future instead of forecasts of it
"Bird in hand" - Means: starting with "Who I am (abilities) / What I know (expertise and experience) / Who I know (networks)"
"Affordable loss" - Focus on Downside: committing only what can be lost rather than what promises the best expected return
"Crazy quilt" - Co-Creation Partnership: building the venture out of commitments from partners who select themselves into it
"Lemonade" - Leverage Contingencies: treating surprises as material to work with rather than as deviations from plan 


== Criticism ==

articles.title: Lantianella
articles.text:
Lantianella

Lantianella is an extinct, enigmatic fossil from the early Ediacaran, and was alive around 602 Ma in the Lantian Formation. It has an conical-shaped body, and is regarded as either a putative cnidarian-grade organism or an macro-algae. It contains two species, L. laevis and L. annularis.


== Discovery and naming ==
Fossils of Lantianella were first found and reported from the black shale "Member II" of the Lantian Formation in Xiuning County, Anhui Province of South China in 2011 as "Type A", and which were formally described and named in 2016.
The generic name Lantianella derives from the place name of Lantian, a town near to where the fossils were found. The specific name of L. laevis derives directly from the Latin word of the same spelling, "laevis", to mean "smooth", in reference to the smooth appearance of the fossils. The specific name of L. annularis derives directly from the Latin word of the same spelling, "annularis", in reference to the annulations up the body of the fossils.


== Description ==
Lantianella are centimetre-scale, conical-shaped fossils, which bear a globose holdfast structure at the base, and a crown of unbranching tentacles at the top opening. The body of the cone is commonly composed of longitudinal filaments or ribs, and sometimes bears transverse annulations. There are two species, with notably differences in appearance, which are as follows:


=== L. laevis ===
L. laevis has a globose to sub-tubular holdfast structure, which ranges between 2–4 mm (0.08–0.16 in) in diameter. The main conical body is flattened to a fan-shape in the rock and is composed of irregularly spaced longitudinal filaments or ribs, which are considerably denser at the base than the top, with a height ranging between 10–55 mm (0.4–2.2 in), and a maximum width of 3–15 mm (0.12–0.59 in) at the distal end. The distal end is likely either rounded or scalloped in nature, although this is noted to likely be the result of tectonic deformation. The filaments range between 0.3–0.8 mm (0.012–0.031 in).
Coming out from the top of the cone is a crown of 10 – 30 tentacle-like structures, which are 5–20 mm (0.20–0.79 in) in length and 0.2–0.7 mm (0.008–0.028 in) in width. These structures are ribbon-shaped, and were likely flexible in life, and bear no branching.


=== L. annularis ===

articles.title: Mahmud Ali al-Banna
articles.text:
Mahmud Ali al-Banna

Mahmud Ali al-Banna (17 December 1926 – 20 July 1985) was an Egyptian Quran reciter. He was known for his radio broadcasts and recordings of Quranic recitation and served as a reciter at several prominent mosques in Egypt. He also participated in the establishment of Reciter's Union of Egypt, serving as its deputy head after its formation in 1984.


== Early life ==
Al-Banna was born on 17 December 1926 in the village of Shubra Bas, in the Shibin El Kom of Monufia Governorate, Kingdom of Egypt. He memorised the Quran at the village's traditional Quran school (kuttab) under the instruction of Musa al-Mantash, reportedly completing his memorisation at the age of eleven.
He subsquently moved to Tanta to study Islamic religious sciences, at the Ahmad al-Badawi Mosque. There he studied the Quranic readings (qira'at) under Ibrahim ibn Salam al-Malaki 


== Career ==


=== Early career and Egyptian radio ===
Al-Banna moved to Cairo in 1945, where he continued his recitational studies under Darwish al-Hariri, a teacher of maqamat (Arabic musical modes). In 1947, he was appointed reciter for the Egyptian Society of Muslim Youth, where performed at the organisation's ceremonies and events.
In 1948, al-Banna recited at an event attended by Ali Mahir Pasha, Abd el-Krim el-Khattabi, and other notable attendees. Following the performance, he was encouraged to join Egyptian Radio. He joined the broadcaster that year, and his first live radio recitation took place in December 1948, when he recited passages from Surah Hud.
His radio appearances and recordings contributed to his recognition as a Quran reciter in Egypt.


=== Mosque appointments ===
In the late 1940s, al-Banna was appointed reciter at Ain al-Hayat Mosque in Cairo. During the 1950s, he served as a reciter at Imam al-Rifa'i Mosque.
In 1959, he moved to Ahmad al-Badawi Mosque in Tanta, where he remained until 1980. He then became a reciter at Al-Hussein Mosque in Cairo, a position he held until his death.


=== Recordings and international visits ===
Al-Banna recorded Quran recitations for Egyptian Radio. His recorded works included a murattal recitation of the Quran, completed in 1967, and a mujawwad recitation. He also recorded murattal recitations for broadcasters in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

articles.title: Karishma Kathariya
articles.text:
Karishma Kathariya

Karishma Kathariya (Nepali: करिश्मा कठरिया) is a Nepalese politician and former school teacher who is a member of the 7th Pratinidhi Sabha.
Her political journey started with the Nagrik Unmukti Party in 2022. She joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party in 2025 and was elected through proportional representation under the Tharu female cluster. She is the first member of parliament in the Pratinidhi Sabha from the Kathariya community. She is a central member of the Rastriya Swatantra Party, elected at the first national convention held in Chitwan.


== Early life and education ==
Kathariya was born on February 23, 1997, into a middle-class Tharu family in Gauriganga, Kailali district, Nepal. She is the daughter of Raj Kumar Kathariya and Tara Devi Kathariya. She completed her primary education at Kshtiz English Boarding School and secondary education at Janpriya Secondary School in Tikapur. She did her bachelor's degree in Management from Tikapur Multiple Campus. She is married to Rajesh Chaudhary.


== Professional career ==
She started her career as a teacher. She became the school headmaster of Jyoti Primary School in Tikapur at the age of 23. She taught there for about four years before entering formal politics. She was also involved in JCI Janaki, an affiliate chapter of JCI Nepal. She was the president for three years of Kistiya Mahila Agricultural Organization, a cooperative bank.
She is a co-founder of Arogya Agriculture Trade and Pvt. Ltd. and Karishma Impex.


== Politics ==
She joined the Nagrik Unmukti Party in 2022. The party also included her name as a proportional representative in the 2022 Nepalese general election, but at that time she could not make it to parliament. Following the 2025 Nepalese Gen Z protests, she joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party in 2025. She was nominated as a proportional representative member of parliament from the Rastriya Swatantra Party in the 2026 Nepalese general election. She is now a member of the Finance parliamentary committee for the Rastriya Swatantra Party in the Pratinidhi Sabha since April 2026.

articles.title: Mamoa da Eireira
articles.text:
Mamoa da Eireira

The Mamoa da Eireira is a megalithic dolmen, or burial tomb, situated close to the Atlantic Ocean coast at an altitude of 30 metres, in the parish of Afife, within the Viana do Castelo Municipality in the north of Portugal. Rock paintings have been discovered at the site. The dolmen is unusual because of its "V" shape, with no clear division between the entrance and the burial chamber and with the orthostats being the same height in both.


== Location and history ==
The monument is located on the northwest slope of the Serra de Santa Luzia, about 400 m east of the coastline and in the vicinity of the Afife floodplain to its south, which is traversed by the Afife river. It dates from the 5th millennium BC (Middle Neolithic) with subsequent usage until the 3rd millennium BC (Chalcolithic).


== Description ==
The word mamoa is used in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula to refer to dolmens, which are more commonly known as antas elsewhere in Portugal. The Mamoa da Eireira is one of the best-preserved dolmens in the area, being composed of 16 granite orthostats of similar height, mainly inclined inwards, which are placed in a V shape, oriented east-west. The capstone has been displaced from its original position but is still on the site. The shape of the dolmen differentiates it from most other dolmens in Portugal, which have a pronounced corridor of smaller stones that lead to the burial chamber. The Mamoa da Eireira was originally covered by a tumulus with a diameter of 28 metres, much of which can still be seen.


== Excavations and findings ==
The Mamoa da Eireira was first referred to by Francisco Martins Sarmento in 1882 and by Émile Cartailhac in 1886. There were four excavations in the 1980s by Eduardo Jorge Lopes da Silva, some in collaboration with the National Archaeological Institute of Aquitaine in France, but the complete results were never published. Some further work was done in 2013–14 by Fábio Soares. Ten engraved stones have been found, largely with zigzag or serpentine patterns, the purpose of which has not been identified. One or two contain what Soares considered to have been "anthropomorphic figures". One of the orthostats, which also contains red pigment, can be seen at the  the Casa dos Nichos in Viana do Castelo, which also exhibits some of the other findings, including flint, quartz, and schist arrowheads, flint blades, polished stone axes, and a large number of quartzite flakes and shaped pebbles. articles.title: Salomon Cappadocia Ultra Trail
articles.text:
Salomon Cappadocia Ultra Trail

Salomon Cappadocia Ultra-Trail is an ultramarathon trail running event held in Cappadocia, Turkey. The race takes place in the hills and valleys of the Cappadocia region and starts in Ürgüp. According to the 2026 race regulations, the main race covers approximately 119 km, with a total elevation gain of 3,761 metres. Participants must complete the course within 24 hours. The event also includes shorter races, such as the Salomon Cappadocia Medium Trail (CMT), Salomon Cappadocia Short Trail (CST) and Salomon Cappadocia Mini Trail (CMIT). This race also offers UTMB-qualified courses, including the CUT, CMT, and CST races, which allow runners to earn or maintain their UTMB Index  


== Routes ==
Salomon Cappadocia Ultra-Trail (CUT) is the longest race of the Salomon Cappadocia Ultra-Trail event. The course covers approximately 119 km, with a total elevation gain of 3,761 metres, and starts and finishes in Ürgüp, Türkiye. The route passes through Ortahisar, İbrahimpaşa, Zemi Valley, Göreme, Pigeon Valley, Uçhisar, Love Valley, Çavuşin, Akdağ, Mustafapaşa, Damsa Lake, Taşkınpaşa, Karlık and Taş Ocağı. The race has a time limit of 24 hours. 
Salomon Cappadocia Medium Trail (CMT) is a 63 km trail running race with approximately 1,946 metres of total elevation gain. The race starts and finishes in Ürgüp, Türkiye. The route passes through Ortahisar, İbrahimpaşa, Zemi Valley, Göreme, Pigeon Valley, Uçhisar, Love Valley, Çavuşin and Akdağ before returning to Ürgüp. The race has a time limit of 12 hours and 30 minutes. 
Salomon Cappadocia Short Trail (CST) is a 38 km trail running race with approximately 1,120 metres of total elevation gain. The race starts and finishes in Ürgüp, Türkiye. The route passes through Ortahisar, İbrahimpaşa, Zemi Valley, Göreme and Red Valley before returning to Ürgüp. The race has a time limit of seven hours.
Salomon Cappadocia Mini Trail (CMIT) is a 14 km trail running race with approximately 385 metres of total elevation gain. The 14K distance was first introduced in 2025. The route passes through Ortahisar before returning to Ürgüp. The race has a time limit of four hours and is open to participants aged 16 and over. 
Salomon Cappadocia Team Games: The event also includes the Cappadocia Team Games, a series of relay trail races held over the 119 km, 63 km and 38 km courses. Teams consist of two runners for the 119 km race, six runners for the 63 km race, and three runners for the 38 km race. Team members

articles.title: Numb (2025 film)
articles.text:
Numb (2025 film)

Numb (Japanese: しびれ, Hepburn: Shibire) is a 2025 Japanese drama film directed by Takuya Uchiyama. It follows the childhood and life of Daichi (Takumi Kitamura), a mute man, and his mother Aki (Rie Miyazawa), as they navigate abuse and the hardships of life.


== Plot ==
In Niigata, a boy named Daichi and his mother, Aki, are subject to extreme physical abuse from Daichi's father. By the time Daichi is 11, they have escaped and end up living in a roof shed in abject poverty — Aki has become a sex worker to earn money, and has developed alcoholism, while Daichi, now mute as a result of his trauma, resorts to stealing the most basic groceries and collecting water from the river. One day, while running away in town, he chances upon Ivan, an illegal Russian migrant worker from Vladivostok who offers to be his friend and gives him a ride home. He continues to run into trouble, as the homeowner whom he steals his groceries from catches him — though sympathetic and giving him food, she makes him promise not to come again. He runs to an underground Russian club, where he is caught by the owner, who chases him out. Returning, he finds that his home has caught on fire.
As a 15-year-old, Daichi and Aki have relocated to the apartment of his aunt, Tomoko, a devout Jehovah's Witness. Aki now suffers from cirrhosis, but is not giving up drinking as she believes the disease has gone too far. She pays money to her boyfriend, who resembles Daichi's father and gives her alcohol. Coming back one day, Daichi finds that Aki has signed a do not resuscitate form with Tomoko's approval — he confronts his aunt but she brushes him off. Later, he wakes up to find Aki's boyfriend attempting to drown her and abusing her much like Daichi's father. Unable to do anything, Daichi attempts to drown himself in the sea, but is saved by Ivan, who recognizes him and tells him that his life should not be dominated by sadness and his childhood trauma.
Ten years later, Daichi works as a bartender while also dealing drugs on the side to earn money for his mother. Upon a visit to her in the hospital, she apologizes, tells him that she does not need his money since she has been a bad parent and because she is receiving money from Daichi's father, who is still alive and had heard about her situation. Using the address provided on his father's envelope, Daichi grabs a kitchen knife and decides to exact revenge on him — he finds him in a run-down house, where he attempts to apologize.

articles.title: Dolly Babe
articles.text:
Dolly Babe

Dolly Babe is an American rapper based in Dallas, Texas.  She is best known for her breakout song "Pink Blush" and its remix featuring Megan Thee Stallion, which also marked her debut appearance on the Billboard Hot 100. She previously gained local attention in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and went viral online for songs including "Beyonce".


== Biography ==
Dolly Babe is based in Dallas, and released her first song in 2022. She began garnering local attention in 2023 for her "diva persona and unapologetically outspoken lyrics" in songs like "Bama" and "Get Cute", and her music videos were noted by Dallas and Fort Worth-based influencers. She was named a Rapper to Watch by the Dallas Observer in January 2024. She released 9 singles in 2024.
Her first TikTok hit was her 2024 song "Beyoncé", which was inspired by Beyonce's 2008 song Diva. The song went viral on TikTok. She stated that she received permission from Beyonce to keep the song up.
Her song "Pink Blush" first brought her international attention, being called the TikTok song of the summer by Complex and charting in the TurnTable Top 100 Songs. It reached over 14 million views, and received reposts from singers including Madonna and Rihanna. A TikTok trend also became popular of a group of people, usually all men, "seductively" mouthing the words to her "cunnilingus-exalting" post-chorus. Billboard noted her "bubbly, tongue-in-cheek delivery" and "omantopeia-laden bars" when declaring the song both "TikTok's favorite audio of late" and "a legitimate streaming hit". She delayed the song's music video release until August 2026.
She signed to 300 Entertainment in September 2026, and subsequently released a remix of Pink Blush featuring Megan Thee Stallion, which both Rolling Out's David Kesiena and That Grape Juice's Rashad mused may make it onto the Billboard Top 100. They were ultimately proven right: the song debuted at rank 58 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for the week of October 10, 2026. As of October 20, 2026, the song had been charting on the Billboard Hot 100 for 3 weeks. Complex named Dolly Babe #49 on their 100 Hottest Rappers Right Now list for October 2026.

articles.title: Matej Gashtarov
articles.text:
Matej Gashtarov

Matej Gashtarov (Macedonian: Матеј Гаштаров; born 15 November 2006) is a Macedonian professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for Red Star Belgrade and the North Macedonia national team.


== Career ==


=== Early career ===
Gashtarov began playing football in the youth academy of Metalurg before joining Vardar. He later moved to Serbia and joined the youth system of Red Star Belgrade in August 2024, after spending time with Mineralac.
On 30 April 2025, he signed his first professional contract with Red Star Belgrade. During the 2024–25 season, he played for the club's under-19 team in the UEFA Youth League and was part of the squad that won the Serbian youth league title.
Gashtarov made his senior debut for Red Star Belgrade on 15 August 2025, coming on as a substitute in a Serbian SuperLiga match against Mladost Lučani.


=== Loan to Borac 1926 ===
In January 2026, Gashtarov joined Borac 1926, based in Čačak, on loan from Red Star Belgrade. Before the move, he had also spent time with Grafičar, a club associated with Red Star's player-development system.


=== Return to Red Star Belgrade ===
In July 2026, Gashtarov returned to Red Star Belgrade following his loan spell. On 9 July 2026, the club announced that he had extended his contract until 2029. He subsequently featured for the first team during the 2026–27 season.


== International career ==
Gashtarov has represented North Macedonia throughout all youth international levels, leading to a debut for North Macedonia's senior national team in the 2026–27 UEFA Nations League matches in September 2026.

articles.title: Igazeuma Adikema Okoroba
articles.text:
Igazeuma Adikema Okoroba

Igazeuma Adikema Okoroba is a Nigerian Science and Sustainability award winner with expertise in sustainability and development sociology , civil society media and the oil and gas sector. In 2021, she was appointed the head of sustainability at Dangote Cement Plc.


== Early life and education ==
Igazeuma was born at , Ahoada East local government area in Rivers State, Nigeria. She obtained her first degree at Rivers State University, following the completion of National Youth Service Corps she furthered her study in sustainability at the University of Exeter and has a PhD in Sustainability from the University of Port Harcourt.


== Career ==
Igazeuma began her career as a development officer at TotalEnergies in Nigeria, followed by General Manager position of Sustainability Nigeria and Pan Africa at Dangote Cement Plc, with years of experience as a development sociologist.


== Research ==
Igazeuma's research is focused on sustainable development, corporate social responsibility; and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG). She has published articles in academic journal as well as a tedtalk and conference abstracts.

articles.title: Satybaldy Burşaqov
articles.text:
Satybaldy Burşaqov

Satybaldy Eresūly Burşaqov (born 24 August 1968) is a Kazakh diplomat and politician serving as the member of the 1st Kurultai since 2026. Previously, he was the Kazakh ambassador to North Macedonia, Cyprus and Israel.


== Early life and education ==
Satybaldy Eresuly Burşaqov was born on 24 August 1968 in Pervomaysk, a village in Chapaevsky District (now Akzhaik District), West Kazakhstan Region, Soviet Kazakhstan.
In 1993, after graduating from the Almaty Pedagogical Institute of Foreign Languages with a degree in English and Russian education, he remained at the institute as a lecturer. That same year, he joined the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan (MFA) as a desk officer, later becoming an attaché of the European Department under the leadership of Minister Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Concurrently, in 1994, he completed courses at the Foreign Service Academy in Islamabad, Pakistan.
In 1995, following his graduation from the Netherlands Institute of International Relations Clingendael, Burşaqov was appointed to the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Hungary, where he served as an attaché, and was subsequently promoted to third and then second secretary. In 2000, upon returning to Kazakhstan, he worked in the Department of Europe and America of the MFA as a first secretary, counselor of the Department of Bilateral Cooperation, and head of division.
In 2002, Burşaqov was posted to Belgium, serving as a first secretary and later as a counselor at the Embassy of Kazakhstan.
In 2007, following Tokayev's election as chairman of the Senate, Burşaqov returned to Kazakhstan. Until Tokayev's resignation in 2011, he served within the Senate Office as deputy head and subsequently head of the Inter-Parliamentary Relations and International Cooperation Department.


== Political career ==
From 2011 to 2012, Burşaqov headed the International Relations and Protocol Department of the Majilis Office. Between 2012 and 2017, he served as Deputy Permanent Representative of Kazakhstan to UNESCO, and from 2017 to 2019, he was deputy chairman of the International Information Committee of the MFA.
Following the resignation of president Nursultan Nazarbayev and Tokayev’s assumption of the presidency in 2019, on 29 March, Burşaqov was appointed head of the Foreign Policy Center of the Presidential Administration. Four months later, on 22 July, he took charge of the Foreign Policy and International Relations Department of the Presidential Administration.

articles.title: Víctor Andrés Marroquín-Merino
articles.text:
Víctor Andrés Marroquín-Merino

Víctor Andrés Marroquín-Merino Torres (born 1 November 1998) is a Peruvian political consultant, artist and historian. A ranking member of the Peruvian Aprista Party (APRA), he has been the party's National Secretary of International Relations since October 2026.
Born in Chicago and raised in Lima, Marroquín-Merino studied law at the University of Lima before turning to acting. He trained at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts in New York and graduated from New York University's Tisch School of the Arts before embarking in graduate studies at the University of Oxford, specializing in Latin American studies.
As a consultant, Marroquín-Merino co-founded a public affairs and political strategy firm, and served in Enrique Valderrama's campaign at the 2026 presidential election. He has appeared regularly as a political analyst on Peruvian media.


== Early life and education ==
Marroquín-Merino was born in Chicago to Peruvian parents, and moved with his family to Lima at the age of three. He attended Newton College, a British–Peruvian school in Lima, and later the Miraflores Adventist College, where he completed his secondary education.
He studied law at the University of Lima before turning to acting in 2018, training at the American Academy of Dramatic Arts (AADA) in New York under instructors including David Dean Bottrell and Timothy D. Stickney.
After completing an associate degree at AADA, he transferred to New York University's Tisch School of the Arts, where he earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts triple-majoring in theatre, politics, and history. His honors thesis, "Death, Memory, and Persuasion: Political Oratory as Performance in Latin America", supervised by artist-scholar Sebastián Calderón Bentín, examined political speech as performance, focusing on speeches by Jorge Eliécer Gaitán, Fidel Castro and Alan García. At NYU, he was a member of the College Democrats, and from 2022 to 2024, he worked as a journalist for the Peruvian digital newspaper Diario El Gobierno.
He then read for a MSc in Latin American Studies at the University of Oxford, as a member of St Cross College. While at Oxford, he was active in the Oxford Union and the Oxford University Conservative Association. He was first elected to the Union's Secretary's Committee for Hilary Term 2025, and subsequently to its Standing Committee for Trinity Term 2025, becoming, according to El Comercio, the first Peruvian elected to that body. articles.title: Nadiia Kushnir

Nadiia Kushnir

Nadiia Kushnir, pseudonym Nadjozna (born 28 January 1993 in Lviv) — a Ukrainian designer and children’s book illustrator. She became known as the creator of the online comic strip ‘The Goose’.


== Biography ==
She studied at the Ukrainian Academy of Printing and the Ukrainian Academy of Design.
Organiser and coordinator of the nationwide literary and artistic project ‘Gorytsvit’. Member of an international organisation for non-formal education MitOst.
She has illustrated over 80 books for children, teenagers and adults, including "About Zyuzya the Mosquito" and "Kuzya, Zyuzya and Company" by Vsevolod Nestaiko, "The Alphabet" by Svitlana Kisar, "A Tale of the Curious Kitten" by Johanna Kordis, "Lyalya" by Jacek Denel, and others, for the publishing houses "Veselka", "Urbino", "Vivat", "Kalvaria", "Fundacja Centrum Badan Polska-Ukraina".
In 2017, Nadiia Kushnir was named one of the best children’s illustrators in independent Ukraine by the Bukmol website, her best works were named as the illustrations for Tetiana Stus’s picture book "Where is Oira?" and her own book "How the Goose Sought His Love".
In 2021, at the age of 28, she was included in Forbes Ukraine’s 30 Under 30 list as an illustrator.
2024, due to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Nadiia with her son relocated to Canada, Ottawa.

articles.text:
Arkadiusz Sikora

Arkadiusz Sikora (Polish: [arˈka.djuʂ ɕiˈkɔ.ra]; born 20 June 1973) is a Polish politician, economist, and business executive. Since 2023, he is a member of the Sejm of Poland, representing the constituency no. 1, centered on the cities of Jelenia Góra and Legnica in Lower Silesian Voivodeship. He is a member of the New Left party, and previously belonged to the Democratic Left Alliance and the Democratic Party.


== Biography ==
Arkadiusz Sikora was born on 20 June 1973 in the town of Głubczyce in Opole Voivodeship, Poland. In 1997, he graduated with a degree in finance and banking from the Wrocław University of Economics. Sikora worked in the banking sector and for the company DSI, a subsidiary of KGHM Polska Miedź. From 2003 to 2011, he was a head specialist in the Budget and Finance Department of the Lower Silesian Voivodeship Marshal Office in Wrocław. He was also a deputy director of the Wrocław Cultural and Arts Centre, and a deputy director of the Spartan Wrocław Training Centre. From 2000 to 2002, Sikora was a deputy chairperson of the association handball team Śląsk Wrocław, and from 2013 to 2023, he was a deputy chairperson of the Association of Directors of Local Government Cultural Institutions.
Sikora was a member of the party Democratic Left Alliance, and from 2000 to 2002, he was the chairperson of the Lower Silesian Voivodeship division of its youth wing, the Young Democratic Left Association. During the 2002 local election, he was elected to a seat in the Wrocław City Council, serving from 18 November 2002 to 12 November 2006. He received 1.250 votes (6.03%). In 2005, he left the Democratic Left Alliance, and joined the Democratic Party. During the 2005 parliamentary election, he was its candidate to a seat in the Sejm of Poland, from the constituency no. 3, centered on the city of Wrocław in Lower Silesian Voivodeship. He did not receive the mandate, gaining 292 votes (0.08%). He unsuccessfully run for the election to the Wrocław City Council during the 2006 local election, being on the electoral list of the electoral alliance Left and Democrats, receiving 1,760 votes (5.74%). Afterwards, he returned to the Democratic Left Alliance, and in 2016, he became the secretary of the party structures in Lower Silesian Voivodeship.

articles.title: Rixt Meijer
articles.text:
Rixt Meijer

Rixt Meijer (born 21 February 1982) is a Dutch former long-track speed skater, marathon speed skater, and cyclist who specialized in all-round speed skating. She trained with the Friesland regional branch of the Royal Dutch Skating Federation (Koninklijke Nederlandsche Schaatsenrijders Bond; KNSB). In 2013, she became the Dutch national champion in marathon speed skating on artificial ice.


== Career ==
Meijer was born in Sneek, but grew up in IJlst. In the winter of 1985, at the age of three, she stepped onto the ice for the first time on a ditch behind her house. That same year, her father took part in the Elfstedentocht, which inspired her to take up ice skating as well. She decided to pursue skating at the age of five. When she was fifteen, she competed in the national championship for young skaters (pupillen), where, to her own surprise, she finished in third place. She was rewarded for this achievement by being selected for the local rink's competitive squad.
She achieved her first top-10 finish at a senior national championship at the 2002 Dutch All-round Championships, where she made her début by placing eighth. She did not improve upon this result until 2011. At the 2010 Dutch Single Distances Championships, she competed in the 1500 metres and 3000 metres, finishing 17th and 16th, respectively.
In 2012, Meijer won silver at the Dutch National Championships on natural ice after winning the sprint from the peloton. In 2013, however, she had to leave the race owing to a broken skate.
On Boxing Day 2012, Meijer became the Dutch national champion in marathon speed skating on artificial ice. She crossed the finish line in second place, but after Lisanne Soemanta fell at the finish and was subsequently disqualified, Meijer was declared the winner. It was her first victory on artificial ice.
At the 2013 Dutch Single Distances Championships, she won bronze in the 5000 metres. This achievement came as a surprise to her and earned her a spot in the World Cup competitions. During her first World Cup race in the 5000 metres, she won the B-group.
In 2014, Meijer was selected for the World Cup mass start events. During the race in Seoul, she helped Irene Schouten in the overall standings. Schouten finished second, while Meijer herself placed fourth, after Martina Sáblíková had broken away.

articles.title: Damilare Kuku
articles.text:
Damilare Kuku

Damilare Kuku is a Nigerian writer and actress. She is the author of the short story collection Nearly All the Men in Lagos are Mad (2021) and the novels Only Big Bumbum Matters Tomorrow (2024) and Women Rent Men and Secrets Here (2025). As an actress, she has appeared in Nollywood films and television, including the lead role in The Wildflower (2022).


== Early life ==
Kuku grew up between Lagos and Ile-Ife. She has said that she was fascinated by stories from childhood.


== Career ==
Kuku's career has spanned acting, radio presenting, producing, directing and writing.


=== Acting ===
In 2022, Kuku played the lead role of Rolake Dabiri in The Wildflower, directed by Biodun Stephen. The film follows three women living in the same compound who experience different forms of assault from men around them, and also stars Deyemi Okanlawon, Toyin Abraham and Sandra Okunzuwa. It won the audience-voted Best Film award at the 10th Nollywoodweek Film Festival in Paris in 2023.


=== Writing ===
Kuku's first book, the short story collection Nearly All the Men in Lagos are Mad, consists of twelve stories about women's relationships with men in Lagos. Masobe Books published it in Nigeria in 2021, followed by editions from Swift Press in the United Kingdom and HarperVia in the United States. It topped the 2022 Rovingheights bestseller list.
Simon & Schuster acquired UK and Commonwealth rights to a two-book deal with Kuku, and HarperVia acquired North American rights to her first novel, Only Big Bumbum Matters Tomorrow, which was published in both territories on 18 July 2024. The novel follows Temi, a young woman who announces that she plans to have a BBL and move to Lagos, which upsets her family.
Her third book, Women Rent Men and Secrets Here, was published in Nigeria by TBLNG Press in 2025.

articles.title: Hula Concession purchase
articles.text:
Hula Concession purchase

The Hula Concession purchase was the acquisition by the Palestine Land Development Company (PLDC) of the land and rights to drain and reclaim Lake Hula and its surrounding marshes in northern Mandatory Palestine in 1934. One of a number of concessions in Mandatory Palestine, it had originally been granted by the Ottoman Empire in 1914 and was subsequently held by the Syro-Ottoman Agricultural Company, a group of mostly Beirut-based investors headed by Salim Ali Salam, to whom the PLDC agreed to pay £191,974 for the concessionary rights.
The concession covered approximately 56,940 metric dunams, or about one-third of the Hula Valley. It was a drainage and reclamation concession over state land, with an option to acquire the land. Under the original agreement, the concessionaires were to purchase the reclaimed land from the government at a pre-agreed price after draining it and bringing it under cultivation.
The British administration formally approved the transfer on 29 September 1934, and the concession area was handed over to the PLDC on 29 November. The conditions included the reservation of 15,772 metric dunams for Arab cultivators and required the new concessionaires to meet the cost of draining and irrigating that land without recovering those costs from the cultivators.
The purchase did not result in the immediate drainage of the lake and marshes. Financing difficulties, negotiations over government participation, competing water rights and political conflict delayed the scheme, and no major drainage work was undertaken before 1948.


== Background ==

The Hula Valley formed the northernmost section of the Jordan rift valley within Mandatory Palestine. Before drainage, it included Lake Hula, permanent marshes, seasonally flooded land to the north and comparatively dry land south of the lake. A basaltic barrier south of the lake restricted the discharge of the Jordan River, contributing to winter flooding.
The marshes supported an existing economy based on cultivation, fishing, water buffalo husbandry and papyrus harvesting. Papyrus was used to make mats and baskets, construct homes and provide other household materials. Glenna Anton wrote that these activities formed part of a relationship in which the inhabitants and the wetland environment shaped one another, rather than the marshes constituting an unused landscape awaiting development.

articles.title: Days and Nights (1944 novel)
articles.text:
Days and Nights (1944 novel)

Days and Nights (Russian: Дни и ночи) is a 1944 novel by Soviet war correspondent and author Konstantin Simonov about the Battle of Stalingrad. The novel was translated into English and published in the U.S. in November 1945, where it remained on the fiction best seller list for eleven weeks. One American reviewer called it "the best Soviet book so far published here about what the Russians call 'The Great Patriotic War'." Simonov would go on to write the more critically acclaimed World War II trilogy, The Living and the Dead, but at the time of his death in 1979, Days and Nights was the work he was most known for internationally.


== Synopsis ==
The novel begins with a quote from Alexander Pushkin's narrative poem Poltava, including the lines:

In September 1942, 29-year-old Captain Alexei Saburov waits at a train station in the village of Eltonskaya, east of the Volga River. He meets Colonel Babchenko and is told to assemble members of a new battalion and ferry across the river to Stalingrad, where the Red Army has been engaged in fierce fighting with German forces for over a month. The river crossing uses a barge and small steamer to transport all the equipment, soldiers, and medical staff. Prior to reaching the west bank of the Volga, the steamer is bombarded by German shells, and numerous passengers fall into the water. Saburov, a tall man and a strong swimmer, rescues an 18-year-old hospital assistant, Anya Klimenko, with whom he had been speaking during the crossing.

In a midnight officers' meeting with Babchenko and Colonel Protsenko, Saburov is ordered to retake three Stalingrad apartment buildings that were recently seized by the Germans. Saburov divides his battalion into three companies; each is tasked with capturing a building in a surprise night attack. The operation succeeds, and Saburov sets up a command post in the basement of the building that he led the attack on. Protsenko visits the command post and warns Saburov how hard it will be—with no reinforcements coming—to fight off German counterattacks and retain control of the buildings:"[Y]ou've got to teach the men... Day and night you've got to teach them. Because if you don't train a soldier today, then tomorrow he'll get himself killed. And not simply killed. Getting killed, after all—that's what war is for, but to be killed stupidly and cheaply, that's what's sad."

articles.title: 2018 FIP World Padel National Pairs Championships
articles.text:
2018 FIP World Padel National Pairs Championships

The 2018 FIP World Padel National Pairs Championship was the sixteenth edition of the world doubles tournament organized by the FIP, the governing body for international padel. Both the men’s and women’s events were held concurrently with the national team's world championships, and for the sixth time, participation was restricted to pairs representing the same country.
In the women's category, the world's number 1 and number 2 ranked pairs, continued their strong form from the World Padel Tour tournaments, reaching the final with a 2–2 tie in their head-to-head record. In the decisive match, twins Majo and Mapi Sánchez, playing in their twelfth final of the year, defeated Gemma Triay and Lucia Sainz, securing their sixth title of the season and becoming world champions in the doubles category for the first time.
In the men’s category, for the seventh time since 2006 (with the exception of 2012), the vast majority of the top-ranked players chose not to compete in the world doubles championship, opening the door for the two best-ranked pairs among the entrants to reach the final. In the battle for the title, Alejandro Galán and Juan Lebrón defeated Javi Ruiz and Uri Botello via walkover. This marked Galán’s first world doubles championship, while Lebrón successfully defended the title he had won in 2016. This was the first title and tournament together for Galán and Lebrón as a pair, a partnership that would go on to dominate the World Padel Tour circuit from 2020 to 2022.

articles.title: Zhang Yu (actor)
articles.text:
Zhang Yu (actor)

Zhang Yu (Chinese: 章宇; pinyin: Zhāng Yǔ; born Zhang Xin on 25 September 1982) is a Chinese actor. Zhang became widely known in 2018 through three films: An Elephant Sitting Still, Dying to Survive and A Cool Fish. His performance as the leukaemia patient "Huang Mao" in Dying to Survive won him the Asian Film Award for Best Supporting Actor and earned him nominations at the Golden Horse Awards and the Golden Rooster Awards, and in 2019, he received the Best New Actor award at the Beijing College Student Film Festival. His later work includes the films Her Story (2024) and Front Teeth (2026) and the television series The First Shot (2024) and Crimes Against Humanity (2025).


== Early life and education ==
Zhang was born Zhang Xin on 25 September 1982 in Duyun, in the Qiannan Buyei and Miao Autonomous Prefecture of Guizhou. His parents and maternal grandparents had moved to Duyun from Chongqing during the Third Front campaign to work at the city's bridge factory, and he grew up in the factory's community, attending its school for employees' children and speaking "railway dialect", a variety close to Sichuanese used inside the factory. He loved singing in high school, but after he failed the entrance examination for vocal music, he was persuaded to try acting instead and was admitted to the College of Arts of Guizhou University. In 2003, while still a student, he was cast by the director Wang Xiaoshuai in a small role in Shanghai Dreams, which was filmed in Guiyang, which was his first film.


== Career ==


=== Stage and early film roles (2005–2017) ===
In 2005, Zhang joined the Guizhou Provincial Drama Troupe, where he rose to play leading roles in productions that won national awards. In 2008, after a provincial tour, he left the troupe for Beijing without formally resigning, having written in his diary, "In 2008, I should be in Beijing." His early years in Beijing were difficult; he worked as an assistant director and took small parts, mostly in independent films. In 2011, he played the lead role, Mengzi, in Pistol, a short film by the advertising director Lü Huizhou. His other films of this period included Feng Xiaogang's Aftershock (2010), Cai Shangjun's People Mountain People Sea (2011) and Song Chuan's Ciao Ciao (2017).

articles.title: Khima B.K.
articles.text:
Khima B.K.

Khima B.K. (Nepali: खिमा वि.क.) is a Nepalese politician and professional health nurse who is a member of the 7th Pratinidhi Sabha. She has been a member of the Rastriya Swatantra Party since 2025 and was elected through proportional representation under the Dalit female cluster. She is among one of the five professional nurses from the Rastriya Swatantra Party to become a member of parliament in the Pratinidhi Sabha. She is a central committee member of the Rastriya Swatantra Party, elected from first national convention held in Chitwan.


== Early life and education ==
Khima was born in 1999 into a Dalit family in Dangisharan, Dang district, Nepal. She is the daughter of Ghanshyam B.K. and Pramila B.K.. She completed her Diploma in Nursing from Lord Buddha Nursing College, Kohalpur, Banke in 2020.


== Professional career ==
After completing her diploma in nursing, she began working at various hospitals in Dang district. She also traveled to Dubai to work as a nurse, but returned to Nepal after about two months due to low salary and allowances. She then resumed her nursing career at a hospital in Bhairahawa.


== Politics ==
She joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party in 2025, following the 2025 Nepalese Gen Z protests. She was nominated as a proportional representative member of parliament from the Rastriya Swatantra Party in the 2026 Nepalese general election. She is now a member of the Women and Social Affairs parliamentary committee for the Rastriya Swatantra Party in the Pratinidhi Sabha since April 2026.

articles.title: Kreab
articles.text:
Kreab

Kreab is a Swedish communications consultancy that works in corporate and financial communications and public affairs. It was founded in Stockholm in 1970 as Kreativ Information AB and is still based there. After a merger with Gavin Anderson & Company, a subsidiary of the Omnicom Group, it traded as Kreab Gavin Anderson from 2009 to 2015. In 2018 it had offices in 25 countries. The group includes a Finnish company in Helsinki and an office in Brussels that works on European Union policy for corporate clients. Former politicians from Sweden and Finland have worked for the firm. In the 1970s and 1980s Kreab wrote and published material for Swedish business on nuclear power and the environment. Its contacts with the Sweden Democrats in 2015 led to the departure of the head of its Swedish operation.


== History ==
Kreab was founded in Stockholm in 1970 as Kreativ Information AB by Peje Emilsson, Jan-Erik Ander and Peder Olin. It is one of the oldest public relations firms in Sweden. In the year the firm was founded, Emilsson ran the Moderate Party's election campaign.
In 1972 Emilsson recruited the physicist Tor Ragnar Gerholm, and Kreab and the Swedish Employers' Confederation (SAF) used him to write material about the future for schoolchildren. Kreab published Gerholm's book Varför kärnkraft? (Why nuclear power?) in 1975. Before the 1980 Swedish nuclear power referendum, SAF reissued it and other Kreab texts through the organisation Näringslivets energiinformation. In 1984 Kreab and SAF produced the pamphlet What about the Future?, written by Gerholm and the American futurist Herman Kahn. In their study of climate obstruction in Sweden, Vowles, Ekberg and Hultman place Kreab and Gerholm, with SAF and the Federation of Swedish Industries, among the first business-linked voices that tried to counter the environmental and anti-nuclear movement.
Kreab opened an office in Brussels in 1992. In 2008 it organised the first public event of the Stockholm Initiative, later known as the Climate Realists, a network that disputes the scientific consensus on human-caused climate change.
By 2008 Kreab had 150 full-time staff and a turnover of about 300 million Swedish kronor.
In February 2009 Kreab merged with Gavin Anderson & Company, a British financial communications firm owned by the Omnicom Group. The new company, Kreab Gavin Anderson Worldwide AB, was based in Stockholm and had 350 staff and 500 clients in 25 countries, with a turnover of about 500 million kro

articles.title: Duncan Mubiru
articles.text:
Duncan Mubiru

Duncan Mubiru (born March 17 1974), popularly known as Kikankane, is a Ugandan rally driver who competes in the Uganda National Rally Championship and other regional rally events. He won the national rally championship in 2021 and the Pearl of Africa Uganda Rally in 2023. He is known for competing in cars including the Subaru Impreza WRX STI and Ford Fiesta Proto.


== Rally career ==
Mubiru began competing in rallying in 2011. Over his career, he has driven several rally cars, including Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution models, a Subaru Impreza WRX STI and a Ford Fiesta Proto. His nickname, "Kikankane", has become widely associated with his rally appearances in Uganda.


=== 2021 National Rally Championship ===
Mubiru won the 2021 Uganda National Rally Championship driving a Subaru Impreza WRX STI GVB. The championship was a major achievement in his rally career.


=== 2023 Pearl of Africa Uganda Rally ===
In May 2023, Mubiru won the Pearl of Africa Uganda Rally driving a Ford Fiesta Proto with co-driver Joseph Bongole. The crew finished in a time of approximately two hours, 30 minutes and 54 seconds, ahead of Byron Rugomoka and Hakim Mawanda. The victory fulfilled one of Mubiru's stated ambitions in the sport.
Mubiru attributed the victory to preparation, fitness and careful driving, while also crediting his co-driver's mechanical knowledge for helping the crew manage problems during the event.


=== Regional rally competitions ===
Mubiru has also represented Uganda in regional rally events, including the Safari Rally in Kenya. In March 2026, he was entered in the event with co-driver Joseph Kamya, driving a Subaru Impreza WRX STI GVB to compete for Africa Rally Championship points.
In October 2026, Mubiru won the Central Motor Club's Gulu rally for a second consecutive year. Driving a Ford Fiesta Proto with co-driver Hamza Lwanga, he finished 42.2 seconds ahead of Moses Lumala.


== Achievements ==
Uganda National Rally Championship: 2021
Pearl of Africa Uganda Rally: 2023
Central Motor Club Gulu Rally: 2025, 2026

articles.title: Eve's Sour Apples
articles.text:
Eve's Sour Apples

Eve's Sour Apples is a 1934 collection of feminist essays by Irene Clyde, the pen name of English international lawyer and writer Thomas Baty. Published in London by Eric Partridge Ltd. at the Scholartis Press, it examines distinctions between the sexes, heterosexual marriage, reproduction and femininity. Clyde argued that conventional divisions between the sexes encouraged domination and opposed the expectation that women should marry.
The essays also defend aristocratic manners and associate femininity with refinement, opposition to violence and pacifism. Legal scholar Karen Knop has compared these ideas with Baty's later writing on international law.


== Background and publication ==

Clyde had published the feminist utopian novel Beatrice the Sixteenth (1909) and helped establish the Aëthnic Union, which opposed fixed distinctions between the sexes. In 1916, Clyde was among the founders of Urania, a privately circulated feminist journal that challenged conventional gender roles and marriage.
According to historian T. Maait Pepperell, Eve's Sour Apples reused wording from essays published in Urania in 1919 under the name Theta. The essays defended aristocracy and associated the cultivated classes with feminine refinement. Urania had stated that Theta alone was responsible for the opinions expressed.
Eve's Sour Apples was published in London in 1934 by Eric Partridge Ltd. at the Scholartis Press.


== Content ==


=== Sex and marriage ===
Clyde rejected the division of humanity into masculine and feminine categories. Discussing the book in the context of feminist and religious thought, historian Joy Dixon interprets it as criticising both the hierarchy between the sexes and the traits assigned to each. Clyde regarded heterosexual intercourse as bound up with domination and possession.
Clyde also opposed heterosexual marriage. Historian Sonja Tiernan cites a passage in which Clyde describes a woman's refusal to marry as a response to the institution itself, not an act of self-denial. Tiernan relates this position to Urania's criticism of heterosexual marriage and its presentation of relationships between women as an alternative.


=== Biological sex and reproduction ===

articles.title: British Animation Awards
articles.text:
British Animation Awards

The British Animation Awards (BAAs) are biennial awards recognising achievements in British animation, including animated films, television programmes, commercials, music videos and student productions. The awards originated in 1988 and were reorganised in the 1990s, with the present biennial format established in 1996 by Jayne Pilling. They recognise both established and emerging animators, with winners selected through industry juries and public voting.


== History ==
The origins of the British Animation Awards have been traced to 1988, when the awards were inaugurated under the aegis of the Welsh broadcaster S4C. The awards were subsequently substantially reorganised, including changes to their jury composition and the introduction of audience participation in the selection of winners.
The present biennial format was established in 1996 by Jayne Pilling, who directed the awards until 2018. The first ceremony under this format was hosted by comedian Willie Rushton. The awards have been held every two years since 1996.
The 2002 awards marked an expansion in international participation, with animators from outside the United Kingdom invited to enter for the first time. That year's competition received more than 1,000 entries from Britain and overseas, from which 40 finalists were selected. Audiences participated in selecting winners through screenings at 17 cinemas across the United Kingdom. Pilling explained that the international expansion was intended to expose British filmmakers to developments in animation elsewhere in the world.
The ceremonies have generally been held at London's National Film Theatre, subsequently known as BFI Southbank, although the Shaw Theatre has also hosted the event. Presenters have included comedians Jeremy Hardy, Linda Smith, Joe Pasquale, Caroline Mabey, Thom Tuck, Aisling Bea and Miles Jupp. Hardy developed a longstanding association with the awards, presenting several ceremonies. Following his death in 2019, he was commemorated at the 2020 ceremony.
In 2018, Pilling announced her retirement as director, alongside producer Gulsen Yanik. She was succeeded by Helen Brunsdon. By that year, the awards had presented more than 240 prizes.

articles.title: Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis
articles.text:
Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis (Bengali: বাংলাদেশ খেলাফত মজলিস) is an Islamist political party in Bangladesh founded on 8 December 1989. The party is led by Mamunul Haque as its Ameer, with Yusuf Ashraf serving as the Senior Naib-e-Ameer and Jalaluddin Ahmed as the Secretary General. Its electoral symbol is a rickshaw. The party is a component of the 11-Party Alliance. In the 2026 Bangladeshi general election, the party secured its first-ever parliamentary seats in history.


== History ==
Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis was established on 8 December 1989 at the Engineers Institution auditorium under the initiative of a faction of the Bangladesh Khilafat Andolan led by Azizul Haque, the Islamic Jubo Shibir led by Ahmed Abdul Kader, a faction of Bhashani's NAP, and Tamaddun Majlish organizer and Language Movement veteran Masud Khan. Maulana Abdul Ghaffar served as its first Ameer. He was later succeeded by Azizul Haque, and subsequently by Maulana Habibur Rahman. 
In 2005, Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis split into two factions. One faction retained the name Khelafat Majlis and remained within the BNP-led alliance, while the other faction broke away and continued operations under the name "Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis". Prior to the 2008 general election, a 5-point agreement was signed between Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis and the Awami League, wherein the Awami League pledged not to enact any laws contrary to the Quran and Sunnah if elected. However, the agreement could not be fully implemented due to pressure from secular and leftist factions.
Following the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government on 5 August 2024, the party gained prominence in national politics. In the 2026 general election, the party joined the 11-Party Electoral Alliance.

articles.title: 2026 Portuguese housing protests
articles.text:
2026 Portuguese housing protests

A series of protests took place in Portugal in reaction to the country's ongoing affordable housing crisis. Demonstrations started as early as March 2026 protesting rising housing costs, but escalated to larger and on-going protests after the police violently intervened on an encampment on 15 October 2026 in Porto, injuring over 30 protesters. In reaction, the protests grew to other cities around the country, leading to dozens of arrests.


== Background ==


=== Housing crisis in Portugal ===
Housing costs and rental prices had been soaring for many years in Portugal, particularly in major urban centers, as wages have not increased to the same extent. Housing construction in the country collapsed following the bursting of the Portuguese property bubble in 2008 and the subsequent real estate crisis, causing a housing shortage in places where it was needed the most. Since 2015, housing prices have increased 180%, 70% just since 2021, because of several factors, from a big increase in population, due to a wave of immigration, a stagnation in new construction, burdened by heavy bureaucracy, to foreign speculation investements.
The 2026 protests arise in a context of contestation of the new rental legislation, criticized by left-wing parties, who call it the "eviction law" and "rental accelerator". The Secretary-General of Partido Socialista, José Luís Carneiro, accused the government of making "an incomprehensible alliance" with far-right party Chega in the new rental law.


== Timeline ==


=== Early demonstrations ===
In March 2026, over 90 organizations connected to the Casa para Viver platform held multiple protests across 16 cities to protest rising renting costs and forced evictions. These organizations, which include trade unions, tenants unions, and municipal groups, demanded the government to put the over 723,000 vacant properties in the country to use for the people. Protesters criticized the recent budget proposal of the government that defined a "moderate rent" that can be as high as 2,300€ per month. Isabel Mendes Lopes, of the Livre party, accused Prime Minister Luís Montenegro of "living in a bubble".
On 10 October, thousands of protesters marched through the city center of Lisbon against the rising cost of living and housing.

Ehren Hazell

Ehren Hazell (born 20 April 1999) is a field hockey player from Australia.
He competes in Hockey Australia's premier domestic competition, the ONE Active Hockey One League. 


== Personal life ==
Hazell was born in Tamworth, New South Wales.


== Hockey One ==
Throughout has career, Hazell has represented sides in three Australian states, New South Wales, Tasmania and Western Australia.
During his youth, he represented the Workies Hockey Club in Tamworth. Following a move to Sydney, he continued his club representation with the Norwest Strikers. During this time, he represented New South Wales in domestic national championships, including two seasons with the NSW Pride in the Hockey One.
In 2022 Hazell made the move to Perth to compete in the Hockey WA Premier One competition following his inclusion in the Australian Development Squad. In the league, he competes for the Fremantle Cockburn HC.
Following his move to Western Australia, Hazell made the decision to transfer teams in the Hockey One, moving to the Tassie Tigers for the 2023 season. He has been an integral member of the squad since, becoming one of the team's highest goalscorers.

articles.title: Shing Nei Tobu Naam Tar Singha
articles.text:
Shing Nei Tobu Naam Tar Singha

"Shing Nei Tobu Naam Tar Singha" is a Bengali song by the playback singer Kishore Kumar, written by Gauriprasanna Mazumder and composed by Hemanta Mukherjee. It was released as part of the film Lukochuri on June 27, 1958. It is considered to be the first rock and roll song of Bengali language, featuring fast-paced lyrics, along with a humored theme and fun-mooded lyrics. It was also included in music albums and cassettes designated for Durga Puja festival in Bengal. It is regarded as one of the most popular songs of Kumar, and is referred to as an evergreen Bengali song.
The song's music given by Mukherjee was inspired by the 1919 American song "Oh By Jingo!", specifically the 1949 cover version by American singer Danny Kaye. It was also influenced by other western music.


== Composition ==
"Shing Nei Tobu Naam Tar Singha" is a "quirky and fun Bengali song", having fast-paced and nonsensical lyrics. It is said to be the first rock and roll in the Bengali language, written by lyricist Gauriprasanna Mazumder, composed by singer Hemanta Mukhopadhyay, and recorded by the playback singer Kishore Kumar. It also has brass instrumental sections which was not previously used in the same method in songs.
In the film, Kishore Kumar sang the song while dancing to it, with his dual role character also shown in a few scenes. It is considered as a "comedic relief" in consideration of the visuals, storytelling, and story of Lukochuri.


== Performances and influence ==
Actress Rakhee Gulzar was heard singing "Shing Nei Tobu Naam Tar Singha" in front of the Victoria Memorial monument in Kolkata, after spotting a few lion statues at the gates, which the The Times of India described as "a playful, nostalgic gesture that reflected her signature grace and spontaneity." This took place during the shooting of the 2025 film Aamar Boss, directed by Shiboprosad Mukherjee. Mukherjee remarked that Rakhee Gulzar was happy about the place and the food at Kolkata, which reminded her of old memories, and was happy about it, with Mukherjee saying "She asked us to take a picture of her in front of the statue of the lion, and then she started singing the song, Shingh nei tobu naam tar shingho."
The song was sung in the Anandalok Tarar Khonje competition at Kalamandir on November 11, 2007, organized by Kolkata Film and Television Institute. It was featured in the second round of it, where the contestants sang it in a proper lip-syncing along with other classi

articles.title: Second Economic Committee
articles.text:
Second Economic Committee

The Second Economic Commission (Korean: 제2경제위원회) is an agency in North Korea tasked with coordinating the country's defense industry. 


== Overview ==
Beginning in the 1960s, Kim Il-sung promoted the development of the munitions industry while advocating for the simultaneous pursuit of economic development and national defense construction; the Second Ministry of Machine-Building Industry was established during this process in 1967. As munitions production expanded significantly, the organization evolved into a committee in 1971. Although originally under the Central People's Committee, it was transferred to the jurisdiction of the National Defence Commission in 1993. The Second Economic Committee oversees various enterprises and munitions factories, independently producing the majority of materials and equipment required to bolster military capabilities. In 2026 the Second Economic Committee was placed under the Cabinet of North Korea.


== Structure ==
1st General Bureau: Production of small arms and ammunition
2nd General Bureau: Production of mechanized equipment
3rd General Bureau: Production of military artillery
4th General Bureau: Production of missiles and rockets
5th General Bureau: Production of chemical weapons
6th General Bureau: Production of communication equipment
7th General Bureau: Production and acquisition of aircraft

articles.title: Niedax
articles.text:
Niedax

Niedax Holding GmbH serves as the parent company of the Niedax Group and is headquartered in Linz am Rhein, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. The group has remained family-owned since it was established in 1920 and manufactures products for electrical and building installation technology. The Niedax Group operates at 81 sites, including 25 production facilities, in over 30 countries. It has joint ventures with FEMI-CZ and Steelline, both based in Italy, as well as with the R&M Electrical Group in Southampton, UK, and ABB in North America.
The company develops and produces cable management systems for use in buildings, industrial facilities, and infrastructure projects.


== History ==
Niedax was founded in Berlin in 1920 by engineers Alexander Niedergesäß and Fritz Axthelm as Niedergesäß & Co. OHG. The company initially manufactured fastening materials for the electrical industry.
After World War II, the company was rebuilt and opened a branch in Linz am Rhein. A hot-dip galvanising facility began operations in St. Katharinen in 1975. By the end of the 1970s, production had been relocated to St. Katharinen, while the company's administration remained in Linz am Rhein. In 1995, Bruno Reufels and Egon Winggen took over the company's management from Franz Kolmer following his retirement.
From 1995 onwards, Niedax began expanding its international operations. The company acquired Elektraplan in 1996 and the Dutch firm Alinco in 1999. On 1 January 2000, it took over the Kleinhuis Group, based in Lüdenscheid, followed by Rico GmbH & Co. KG in 2004. Most of the larger acquisitions were made during periods of economic crisis, particularly the 2008 financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. During this time, Niedax also bought two steel service centres.
Egon Winggen retired in 2007 and was succeeded by Alexander Horn, who joined Bruno Reufels as managing director.
A new operational management team took up its duties on 1 January 2023. Since the summer of 2023, the Niedax Group has been purchasing CO2-reduced steel from various suppliers and processed the material at its own production facilities.
In 2024, Niedax took over the Spina Group, an Italian manufacturer of cable management systems and distributor of electrotechnical materials for industrial facilities. In November 2024, Niedax and ABB established the joint venture Abnex Inc., which brings together the two companies' North American cable tray businesses.

articles.title: Leli Incident
articles.text:
Leli Incident

The Leli Incident (Chinese: 乐里教案) was a diplomatic and civil unrest incident triggered by the killing of Frédéric Mazel (Chinese: 鄧玉函), a French Catholic missionary traveling through Loly (present-day Leli Town, Tianlin County, Guangxi), on the night of 31 March 1897. The perpetrator, You Weihan (Chinese: 游维翰), was a member of the Tiandihui who had participated in the Sino-French War. Motivated by resentment over the war and a desire to seize money and valuables, You killed the missionary and another Chinese Catholic clergyman. The incident subsequently led to diplomatic demands and armed unrest.


== Background ==

During the Sino-French War, Guangxi organized border residents and military forces to defend the frontier and sent troops into Vietnam. After the war ended, the Qing government incorporated some former Tiandihui members into local militias but disbanded the remaining anti-French fighters without providing them with adequate support. Many were left to disperse across the border regions of Guizhou, Yunnan, and Guangxi, where they became known as roving armed bands.
You Weihan, a member of the Tiandihui, organized a force of more than a thousand men and operated along the borders of Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou. During his movements, he arrived at Loly, established contact with local Tiandihui organizations, and recruited nearby residents to expand his following.
While he was in Loly, Tiandihui members and local residents told him that the Catholic church engaged in usurious lending and that its members lured naive women into the faith and used religious conversion as a pretext for sexual misconduct. Having witnessed atrocities committed by French troops during the Sino-French War, as well as the involvement of French Catholic missionaries in the invasion, You became deeply resentful. He reportedly declared, "Whenever I see a French priest, no matter how important he is, I will kill him."


== The incident ==
On 22 March 1897, Frédéric Mazel, a missionary of the Paris Foreign Missions Society, traveled from Baise to Loly and stayed at the local church. He was accompanied by two local clergymen, Wei Yasheng and Lu, who had been sent by the Changjing church to Baise to escort him.
Members of the local Tiandihui informed You Weihan, who was stationed at Hekou and Pingwang, about Mazel's presence. Believing that Mazel carried medicines and money, You decided to lead an armed force to the church to seize these possessions.

articles.title: Kim Seong-eun (politician)
articles.text:
Kim Seong-eun (politician)

Kim Seong-eun (Korean: 김성은; December 20, 1924 – May 15, 2007) was a South Korean military officer and politician. He served as the 15th Minister of National Defense and as the 4th Commandant of the Republic of Korea Marine Corps.


== Biography ==
Born in Gaeumjeong-ri, Sangnam-myeon, Changwon-gun, South Gyeongsang Province (present-day Gaeumjeong-dong, Seongsan District, Changwon-si), he was commissioned as an ensign (equivalent to the current rank of second lieutenant) in the Republic of Korea Navy in 1946 and joined the Republic of Korea Marine Corps upon its founding in 1949. During the Korean War, he commanded the Battle of Tongyeong—the South Korean military's first independent amphibious operation—a battle credited with giving rise to the Marine Corps' famous nickname, "Ghost-Catching Marines".
Because he neither participated in nor supported the May 16 military coup of 1961, he was ordered to report to Army Headquarters the following day and narrowly escaped assassination alongside the Chiefs of Staff of the Navy and Air Force. He subsequently served as a member of the Military Revolutionary Committee and the Supreme Council for National Reconstruction. He served as the 10th President of the Republic of Korea Veterans Association for eight months (July 18, 1962 – March 4, 1963) and as the 15th Minister of National Defense for five years (March 16, 1963 – February 27, 1968). Notably, he holds the record for the longest tenure of any South Korean Defense Minister and remains the only minister to have come from the Marine Corps. He resigned as Defense Minister, taking responsibility for the January 21 Blue House raid in 1968.
A devout Presbyterian (Tonghap), he attended Shinil Church in Sindang-dong, Seoul, after retiring from the military. During the Roh Moo-hyun administration, he campaigned against the push to transfer wartime operational control led by his later successor, Defense Minister Yoon Kwang-ung. He passed away on May 15, 2007, at Severance Hospital in Sinchon-dong, Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, and was laid to rest in the Generals' Section of the Daejeon National Cemetery.
Kim Seong-eun Hall, an auditorium completed in 2008 within the Republic of Korea Marine Corps Education and Training Group in Pohang, was named in his honor.

articles.title: Joseph Vyttila
articles.text:
Joseph Vyttila

Joseph Vyttila was an Indian Malayalam language writer from Kerala. He had published 15 novels, 5 collections of stories, and 2 plays. In 2012 he received the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award for Overall Contributions (2011). 


== Biography ==
Joseph was born on May 23, 1939 in Vyttila in present-day Eranakulam district of Kerala. He was born as the fifth of nine children of Pappachan and Anastasia of the Ayathuparambil family, an old Latin Catholic family in Vyttila.
In early years, Joseph was an expert in constructing ring wells. His routine involved well-digging during the day and writing novels at night.
He authored the book Ashramam based on his experiences while residing at Swami Nirmalananda's ashram. He passed his SSLC examination from St. Rita's High School, Ponnurunni, and pursued further studies at the Chalakudy ITI. Throughout his career, he worked in various roles, including attendant, clerk, proof-reader, accountant, and editor and was also employed at the Samastha Kerala Sahithya Parishad Press.


=== Personal life and death ===
Joseph was married to Elizabeth. While in the ninth grade, Elizabeth developed an interest in Joseph after reading his novel Ashramam. Her admiration for him grew over time, although she had never met him at the time. The couple had three children, John William, who works as a music teacher, Deepa Joseph, a teacher at Kumbalangi SH High School, and Aparna Joseph. He died on January 9, 2024, while undergoing treatment following a stroke, at a private hospital in Kochi. Funeral was held at Vyttila St. Raphael Church. He died before completing his novel that incorporated autobiographical elements and the history of Kochi.


== Contributions ==
Joseph began his writing career at the age of 18 by publishing the work Charamavarshikam. After that he published works like Pavangalude Panchali, Ashramam, and Papankeerthanam in the following year. He had published 15 novels, 5 collections of stories, and 2 plays. The novel Bharathanatanam based on the life and contributions of playwright P. J. Antony was written after six years of research and study. Nithyavismayathode was his latest published novel.
Joseph started a theatre troupe named 'Navadarshana', but it was not successful. The troupe's play, 'Amavasi', was directed by Ramu Kariat. articles.title: Erlinda Villalobos
articles.text:
Erlinda Villalobos

Erlinda Villalobos (September 1, 1942 – October 11, 2026
) was a Filipino film, radio and television actress.


== Career ==


=== Early years ===
Erlinda Villalobos started her career in the entertainment industry as a radio talent with ABS-CBN Iloilo working there until the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos closed the ABS-CBN during the martial law era. Villalobos moved to Bacolod, working at the Radio Mindanao Network from 1974 to 1983.
In Bacolod, she met fellow voice talent and character actress Vangie Labalan who convinced her to become an actress in Manila. Labalan recommended Villalobos to producers in the capital.
In Manila, Villalobos did radio commercials, using her fluency in the Cebuano, Ilonggo and Filipino languages. From the 1980s and 1990s, she worked as dubbing supervisor for Synch Masters, a company of Labalan which dubbed Mexican telenovelas and anime shows in Filipino.
She was recommended by Labaran to appear in the 1990s television show Pira-pirasong Pangarap. Director Joel Lamangan was satisfied by Villalobos' performance, with the actress appearing in eight episodes in total. She later appeared in Bakekang (2006) and Momay (2010). She still did radio, doing work for drama shows May Kurot sa Puso and Ito ang Buhay Ko for Radyo Inquirer from 2010 to 2011.


=== Later years ===
Villabos made her debut in the indie film industry in the 2011 Cinemalaya film Niño.
Villabos' best known work was the 2015 film Manang Biring, depicting an eponymous elderly woman who was diagnosed terminal cancer. She considered the 2013 Cinemalaya film Ekstra as her breakthrough film, having the opportunity to act alongside Vilma Santos.
Villalobos appeared in other films such as Bambanti (2015), Pamilya Ordinaryo (2016), Smaller and Smaller Circles (2017), Glorious (2018), Bahay na Pula (2022), Firefly (2023), Mallari (2023), The Happy Homes of Diane Hilario (2025) and Until She Remembers (2026). In television, Villalobos appeared in Alyas Robin Hood, Ang Probinsyano, Batang Quiapo, Lolong.
Her last film was Amir, which is expected to be released at the 2026 Metro Manila Film Festival.


== Personal life and death ==
Erlinda Villalobos was previously married. She was already a widow when she moved to Manila sometime in or after the 1980s. She died on October 11, 2026 due to pneumonia.
