Park Byung-kwon

Park Byung-kwon (Korean: 박병권; January 8, 1920 – September 20, 2005) was a South Korean military officer and politician who served as the 14th Minister of National Defense of South Korea.
He was a member of the Miryang Park clan and was born in Nonsan-gun, South Chungcheong Province.


== Biography ==
Born on January 8, 1920, in Nonsan, South Chungcheong Province, he entered the Department of Liberal Arts at Yonhi College in 1940 and obtained his bachelor's degree in 1944; that same year, he was forcibly conscripted as a student soldier.
Following Korea's liberation, he initially joined and was active in the Joseon Student Soldier League. However, he later withdrew—along with figures such as Min Ki-sik and Choi Seok to join the Student Soldier Corps and oppose the League. When the United States Army Military Government in Korea established the Military English School on December 5, 1945, he applied and passed the first round of admissions on January 5, 1946.
After being commissioned as an Army second lieutenant, he participated in the founding of the Korean Constabulary Defense. Following his service with Company A of the 1st Regiment in Seoul, he traveled to Busan, where he was involved in conducting recruitment activities.
He was promoted to Army major in February 1947 and served as the regiment's third commander starting in December of that year. On July 25, 1948, he was transferred to the Department of National Defense (the predecessor to the current Ministry of National Defense). He served as an aide-de-camp to the first Minister of National Defense, Lee Beom-seok, before being appointed in January 1949 as the Chief of Academic Affairs and a battalion commander within the Korea Military Academy's cadet corps. Subsequently, in October 1949, he was promoted to Army Colonel and assumed command of the cadet corps regiment.
When the Korean War broke out in 1950, he conducted delaying operations as the Chief of Staff of the 5th Infantry Division. Four months later, in October 1950, he was promoted to Deputy Commander of the 5th Infantry Division and led operations to suppress communist guerrillas in areas such as Jirisan, Gimcheon, and Yeongju. The following year, in February 1951, he participated in the Battle of Hongcheon, and in March, he was transferred to serve as Deputy Commander of the 2nd Infantry Division. On June 30, he was promoted to Brigadier General and led operations including the Battle of Omisan in Yeongyang, North Gyeongsan

articles.title: Karama Genocide Memorial
articles.text:
Karama Genocide Memorial

The Karama Genocide Memorial is a memorial site for victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. It is located in Karama Sector, Huye District, in the Southern Province of Rwanda.
In April 1994, thousands of Tutsi gathered at the Catholic parish of Karama, where they were told they would be safe. Most of them were killed on 21 April 1994. The memorial now holds the remains of about 70,000 victims.


== Location ==
The memorial is in Karama Sector, one of the fourteen sectors of Huye District. It stands near the Catholic church of Karama, on high ground. It is reached by a dirt road from the road between Huye and Nyaruguru.
In 1994, Karama was part of Runyinya commune, in Butare Prefecture.


== History ==


=== 1994 massacre ===
During the genocide, local officials sent Tutsi fleeing attacks in Runyinya and nearby communes to the Catholic parish of Karama. They were told it was a place of refuge. The refugees were gathered in the church, the schools and the nearby market. A count in April 1994 recorded about 75,000 people at Karama a few days before the massacre.
The refugees were besieged and starved. Their main water source was poisoned. On 21 April 1994, at about 10 a.m., soldiers, gendarmes and militiamen attacked. Local villagers joined them. The attackers used grenades, guns and machetes. The killing went on until the afternoon. Many of those who fled towards Burundi were chased and killed on the way. Estimates of the number killed at Karama range from 40,000 to more than 50,000.


=== Creation of the memorial ===
After 1994, the mass graves around Karama were slowly exhumed. The remains were gathered in a temporary building on the parish grounds. In 2011, funds were allocated to build a proper memorial. Remains from 1,335 pits recorded in the former Runyinya commune were later reburied at the site.
The memorial holds the remains of about 70,000 victims. Survivors and local leaders have asked for new exhibition buildings and a better access road. They have also asked for the site to become a district-level memorial.


== Commemoration ==
Every year, Kwibuka ceremonies are held at the memorial. On 21 April 2024, members of the Parliament of Rwanda, led by the President of the Senate, François-Xavier Kalinda, attended the commemoration. Five victims of the genocide were buried at the memorial on that day. In June 2018, staff of the Ministry of Justice, led by minister Johnston Busingye, visited the memorial.

articles.title: Hyun Suk-ho
articles.text:
Hyun Suk-ho

Hyun Suk-ho (Korean: 현석호; May 23, 1907 – December 2, 1988) was a South Korean manager, politician and diplomat. Born in Yecheon-gun, North Gyeongsang Province, he belonged to the Yeonju Hyun clan and used the pen name Sukgye. He served as the 23rd Minister of Home Affairs and as Minister of National Defense of the Republic of Korea.


== Biography ==
He graduated from Daegu Higher Agricultural and Forestry School in North Gyeongsang Province. Later, he moved to Gyeongseong (Seoul) for further studies and earned a bachelor's degree from Keijō Imperial University. After passing the Higher Civil Service Examination (Administrative Division) in 1933, he began his career in the police force. After Korea's liberation, he worked as a business executive—serving as a planning officer for the United States Army Military Government in Korea's Central Economic Committee (1947), Vice President of Namsun Electric (1949), and Managing Director of Gyeongseong Electric (1951)—before being elected to the National Assembly (3rd term) in 1954 representing the Liberal Party in his hometown of Yecheon County. Later, as a key figure in the "New Faction" of the Democratic Party, he was appointed Director of the Organization Department at the party's central headquarters (1956). He was elected to the National Assembly again (5th term) representing Yecheon County in 1960. During the Second Republic, he was appointed Minister of National Defense, resigning after only 20 days as due to severe infighting between the "New Faction" (led by Chang Myon) and the "Old Faction" (led by President Yun Po-sun) within the Democratic Party, Chang was forced to reshuffle his cabinet almost immediately to appease rival party members. As a result, Hyun stepped down on September 12, 1960, to clear a path for alternative political appointments. He was then appointed for a short period as Minister of Home Affairs and in 1961 he was again appointed Minister of National Defense. He resigned from his second term as Minister of National Defense following the May 16 coup (May 20, 1961). After being imprisoned and subsequently released, he participated in the reconstruction of the Democratic Party (1963). He later became the director of the Catholic Doctrine Research Institute (1967) and spent the remainder of his life studying Catholic doctrine.

articles.title: Arno Brys
articles.text:
Arno Brys

Arno Brys (born Arnold Jozef Maria Brys; 7 June 1928 – 28 August 2025) was a Belgian draughtsman, graphic artist and designer.
Brys was best known as a designer of parades and processions. He drew costumes, flags, giants and floats. His best-known work was for the Procession of the Golden Tree and the Procession of the Holy Blood in Bruges. He also designed stained glass windows, murals, posters and occasional graphics.


== Biography ==


=== Early life and education ===
Arno Brys grew up in Ostend. He came from the large family of Leon Brys (1897–1975) and Veneranda Salens (1903–1992). He went to school at the Onze-Lieve-Vrouwecollege in Ostend. As a child, he admired the woodcuts of Jozef Cantré and Victor Stuyvaert. He was also very interested in the work of James Ensor.
In 1944–1945, the family was evacuated from the restricted coastal zone. The family then lived for a time in Zwijnaarde. There, Brys won a competition for a float for the liberation celebrations. This was his first commission.
Brys studied at the Higher Institute Sint-Lucas in Ghent. He graduated in 1951 with the highest distinction. He learned heraldry, etching, ceramics and glass art there. During his studies, he already drew posters. He also made illustrations for newspapers and for the weekly magazine Tintin.


=== Career ===

Brys taught at the art academy of Roeselare (1952–1963). He also taught at the Higher Institute Sint-Lucas in Ghent (1952–1990), now part of LUCA School of Arts. There, he founded the department of functional graphic design in 1972.
In 1955, Brys married the artist and tapestry embroiderer Beatrix Uleyn. The couple settled in Bruges. They had five children. The architect Jan Tanghe designed their house and studio in Sint-Andries. The house is called Evenhoghe and was built in 1959. It received the Van de Ven architecture prize.
Brys became known above all as a designer of parades, processions and open-air plays. He designed costumes, flags, processional giants, floats and parade boats. From 1958, he redesigned the Procession of the Golden Tree. He designed hundreds of costumes, six giants, a dragon and several floats for it. He was also the artistic supervisor of this parade for some years.
In 1969, the future of the Procession of the Holy Blood seemed under threat. Brys and Antoon Viaene worked to renew the procession. Together with the city of Bruges, they drew up a ten-year plan. Brys drew the costumes, the flags and the props. Many of his desig

articles.title: Kamonyi Genocide Memorial
articles.text:
Kamonyi Genocide Memorial

The Kamonyi Genocide Memorial is a memorial site for victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. It is located in Gacurabwenge Sector, Kamonyi District, in the Southern Province of Rwanda.
The memorial honours the Tutsi killed in the area in 1994. More than 47,000 victims are buried in its mass graves. The site stands at Kibuza, beside the Kigali–Huye road.


== Location ==

The memorial is on Kibuza hill, in Gacurabwenge Sector. This sector is also the seat of Kamonyi District. The site lies beside the paved Kigali–Muhanga road, which is part of the Kigali–Huye road. It is near the Gacurabwenge Sector office and is easy to reach from Kigali.
Before 1994, the Kamonyi area was part of Gitarama Prefecture. Research by the National Commission for the Fight against Genocide (CNLG) shows that commune and national officials there urged the population to carry out the genocide. Testimonies say that Tutsi were driven from nearby parishes and markets to the Kibuza area. Many were killed there in attacks by the Interahamwe and soldiers. Their remains were later moved to the Kamonyi memorial.


== History ==
After the genocide, survivors and victims' families collected the remains of Tutsi killed in Musambira, Gacurabwenge and nearby communes. They were helped by local authorities and the survivors' association Ibuka. The remains were brought to Kibuza hill. The site was slowly developed into a memorial with brick mass graves, collective tombs and a place of remembrance.
In the mid-2000s, the British charity Survivors Fund (SURF) funded a building near the memorial for remembrance work and archives. In 2015, this building was officially handed over to the CNLG. It was to be used as a research centre on the genocide against the Tutsi.
In 2025, the Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement (MINUBUMWE) announced that a national centre for archives and research on the history of the genocide would open in Kamonyi. The aim was to make Kamonyi a hub for research and remembrance.


== Features ==

The memorial has concrete mass graves. They hold the remains of thousands of victims from different places in the area, especially the former Musambira commune. Stones and markers recall the killings at Kibuza and in the nearby sectors.
The memorial hosts Kwibuka commemoration ceremonies. Groups of students and delegations from public and private institutions also visit it for civic education and remembrance. The research building funded by SUR

articles.title: Břetislav Novák
articles.text:
Břetislav Novák

Břetislav Novák (2 March 1938 – 18 August 2003) was a Czech mathematician who worked in number theory, particularly analytic number theory. He spent his whole career at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics of Charles University in Prague, where he was a student and later a colleague of Vojtěch Jarník. He is best known for his work on lattice points in multidimensional ellipsoids and for the "Novák numbers", integers n that divide 2n + 1.


== Life and education ==
Novák was born in Pardubice and grew up in nearby Chrudim, where he attended primary school (1944–1949) and secondary school (1949–1956). He took part in the Mathematical Olympiads as a student, placing sixth in the national round in 1955 and winning the competition outright in 1956.
From 1956 to 1961 he studied mathematics at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics of Charles University. There he became a student of Vojtěch Jarník, who supervised his diploma and CSc. theses. Novák graduated in 1961 cum laude and, under Jarník's influence, decided to devote his career to number theory.
He received the degrees RNDr. and CSc. (equivalent to a PhD) in 1967, became a docent (associate professor) in 1972, received the DrSc. in 1980, and was appointed full professor in 1982.


== Career ==
Novák remained at Charles University throughout his career. He was a half-time tutor while still a student (1959–1961), then a tutor (1961–1964) and a lecturer (1964–1972). After his habilitation he became an associate professor in 1972, and in 1982 he was appointed full professor of mathematical analysis, a post he held until his death.
He spent the winter term of 1962/63 at Moscow State University and that of 1972/73 at the University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign.


=== Administrative and professional activities ===
Novák headed the Department of Mathematical Analysis from 1971 to 1990 and was vice-dean of the faculty in 1973–1976 and 1980–1989. He joined the Union of Czechoslovak Mathematicians and Physicists in 1956, was elected to its Central Committee in 1978, and served as its chairman from 1987 to 1990 and as chairman of its Mathematical Section from 1993 to 1996. The Union awarded him its first-degree award, named him a distinguished member in 1981 and an honorary member in 1993. articles.title: Kaduha Genocide Memorial
articles.text:
Kaduha Genocide Memorial

The Kaduha Genocide Memorial is a memorial site and burial ground for victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. It is located at Kaduha, in Nyamagabe District, in the Southern Province of Rwanda. In 1994, Kaduha was part of Gikongoro Prefecture.
The main massacre took place at the Kaduha parish on 21 April 1994. The memorial holds the remains of more than 47,000 victims. President Paul Kagame opened it in July 2001.


== Location ==
The memorial is in Bamba village, Kavumu Cell, Kaduha Sector, Nyamagabe District. It stands close to the Catholic parish, a school and a health centre. The area has steep hills and deep valleys.


== History ==

In April 1994, thousands of Tutsi took refuge at the Kaduha parish. They hid in the church, the school and the health centre. Kaduha was one of several massacre sites in Gikongoro. The other main sites included Murambi, Cyanika and Kibeho.
The attack began at dawn on 21 April 1994. The killers used grenades, guns and traditional weapons. They attacked the church, the parish buildings, the school and the health centre. Before the attack, refugees had dug trenches. The trenches were presented as latrines. After the massacre, they were used as mass graves.
A 1996 study by the Rwandan Ministry of Higher Education found that more than 20,000 people died at the Kaduha parish.
In 2022, a court in Paris tried Laurent Bucyibaruta. He was the prefect of Gikongoro in 1994. The court found him guilty of complicity in genocide. The verdict covered the massacres at Murambi, Cyanika and Kaduha. He received a sentence of 20 years in prison.


== Memorial ==
The people of the district built the memorial with their own contributions. President Paul Kagame officially opened it in July 2001. In his speech, he asked Rwandans to remember the genocide so that it never happens again.
According to the memorial records, 47,311 victims were buried there by 2013. Remains are still added when new bodies are found. A commemoration is held each year. Survivors say it should take place on 21 April. The exact date is set by local authorities.

Sister Milgitha Kösser was a German nun. She ran the Kaduha health centre from 1973. She witnessed the massacre. She kept an album of 193 photographs taken between 1992 and 1995. The album documents the destruction at Kaduha. Historians use it to study the genocide at Kaduha.

articles.title: Lee Jong-chan (politician)
articles.text:
Lee Jong-chan (politician)

Lee Jong-chan (Korean: 이종찬; March 10, 1916 – February 10, 1983) was a South Korean military officer and politician. He served as the 8th Minister of National Defense, Ambassador to Italy, and a member of the 9th and 10th National Assemblies.


== Biography ==
He served as a military officer during both the Japanese colonial period—having been an officer in the Imperial Japanese Army and the Republic of Korea era. He is regarded as someone who opposed the dictatorship by emphasizing the political neutrality of the military.
After graduating from the Imperial Japanese Army Academy in June 1937 and serving in regions such as Manchuria and the South Seas Mandate, he returned to Korea following liberation. He spent the next three years in self-imposed seclusion, reflecting on his past service in the Japanese military. However, in 1948, he accepted repeated requests to join the Republic of Korea Armed Forces, entering the service as a specially commissioned Army colonel.
He saved Park Chung-hee from being purged after Park became implicated in the aftermath of the Yeosu–Suncheon rebellion. Lee served in the Korean War. During the Second Republic, 
At the time, Lee Yong-moon and Park Chung-hee attempted a coup, seizing upon President Rhee's unjust demand for martial law troops—a move the United States effectively tacitly approved.
In 1952, he was approached by figures such as Lee Yong-moon and Park Chung-hee with a proposal for a coup d'état, but he rejected it and reported it to Prime Minister Chang Myon. He was dismissed as Army Chief of Staff in July 1952.


=== During the Second Republic ===
He served as the Commandant of the Army College for seven years before retiring as a Lieutenant General in 1960. Although he had been humiliated by the President during his tenure as Commandant, he twice rejected Park Chung-hee's proposal—made prior to the May 16 military coup—to appoint him as the supreme leader of the military revolution.
Following the April Revolution in 1960, he served as Minister of National Defense in the interim cabinet led by Ho Chong. During his tenure, he strove to uphold the military's political neutrality by purging officers who had colluded in the rigged March 1960 election and by requiring the Chiefs of Staff of the three military branches and the Marine Corps Commandant to take an oath of allegiance to the constitution. articles.title: Paul de Tornada
articles.text:
Paul de Tornada

The Paul de Tornada is a freshwater marsh in the parish of Tornada, about 5 km from Caldas da Rainha in western Portugal. It has been a Ramsar wetland of international importance since 24 October 2001. In 2009 it became a Local Nature Reserve (Reserva Natural Local). The Geoparque Oeste describes it as the main freshwater wetland in the Oeste region.
The reserve covers about 50 hectares. Roughly half is permanently flooded, and the rest floods in winter rains and dries into muddy banks in summer.


== Management ==
According to the Ramsar listing, the site is private land rented to two environmental organisations, GEOTA and Associação PATO, with support from national and local government. Next to the reserve is the Centro Ecológico Educativo Paul da Tornada – Professor João Evangelista, an environmental education centre run jointly by GEOTA and PATO. It also serves as the reserve's visitor and interpretation centre. The site has an observatory and a trail of about 4 km.


== Flora ==
The vegetation is typical of freshwater marsh. It includes yellow flag iris, bulrush (Typha spp., including Typha latifolia), common club-rush, common reed, and white willow. The marsh is especially important for protecting reed beds and the birds that live in them.


== Fauna ==


=== Birds ===
Ramsar lists the site mainly for its variety of species, especially migratory birds. PATO counted 61 bird species in a recent monitoring survey.

Breeding birds include the little bittern, purple heron, western swamphen, and Eurasian coot.
Summer visitors include the common swift, barn swallow, common house martin, Eurasian reed warbler, great reed warbler, and Savi's warbler.
Winter visitors include the spotted crake, which the regional planning authority calls a priority species.
Passage migrants include the bluethroat, which is rare in Portugal, along with the sedge warbler, whinchat, and western yellow wagtail.
Raptors seen regularly include the black-winged kite, barn owl, northern goshawk, and Eurasian sparrowhawk. The black kite and western marsh harrier appear from time to time.
Introduced species that now breed here include the black-headed weaver and common waxbill.


=== Other animals ===
The Eurasian otter and the European pond turtle live in the reserve. Both are listed as threatened in Portugal's Livro Vermelho dos Vertebrados de Portugal (Red Data Book of Portuguese Vertebrates) and are protected under the Bern Convention. A local guide notes that the Eu

articles.title: Mata da Margaraça
articles.text:
Mata da Margaraça

The Mata da Margaraça (officially the Mata Nacional da Margaraça) is a forest of about 68 hectares (170 acres) on the north-northwest slope of the Serra do Açor, in the municipality of Arganil in central Portugal. It sits between about 600 and 850 metres above sea level, near the village of Pardieiros in the parish of Benfeita.
The government decree that set up the Serra do Açor Protected Landscape describes the forest as one of the rare relics of natural vegetation on the schist slopes of central Portugal. It belongs to the Council of Europe's European Network of Biogenetic Reserves and is part of a Natura 2000 Site of Community Importance.


== Protection ==
The forest had legal protection from 1979. On 3 March 1982, Decree-Law 67/82 created the Serra do Açor Protected Landscape. Inside it the decree set up two special zones: the Partial Nature Reserve of the Mata da Margaraça and the Recreation Reserve of the Fraga da Pena, a nearby waterfall. A 2019 government resolution states that the main purpose of the protected landscape is to preserve the Mata Nacional da Margaraça. The forest has been owned by the national nature conservation institute since 1985.
The protected landscape covers about 382 hectares, although more recent official documents give 373 hectares. A co-management plan for the protected landscape was later presented, with keeping the forest intact as its main goal.


== Ecology ==


=== Vegetation ===
The forest is dominated by sweet chestnut and pedunculate oak. Its understorey includes plants typical of laurisilva (laurel forest), such as Portugal laurel, bay laurel, holly, and laurustinus. Field elm, hazel, wild cherry, and strawberry tree also grow there. Cork oak is less common and grows mostly around the edges.
Scientists describe the forest as a small surviving pocket of laurel forest. Laurel forest was widespread in Portugal during the Tertiary, before the last glacial period, when the climate was warmer and wetter. Relative humidity stays above 80 percent almost all year, and temperatures rarely go above 30 °C, even in the dry season. Researchers call this an "insular-like effect" inside a mountain range that otherwise has a mostly Mediterranean climate.


=== Fungi ===

articles.title: Slab (sawmilling)
articles.text:
Slab (sawmilling)

In sawmilling, a slab is the outer piece cut from a log when the log is squared or sawn into boards. It has one flat, sawn face. The rest of its surface is the rounded outside of the log, with or without bark. The slabs are the first and last boards cut from a log. Taken together they are called slabwood. Slabs were usually left as waste and burned, but a thick slab could yield a rough board.


== Terminology ==
English dictionaries define the slab as the outside piece cut from a log in squaring it, or as any of the outer parts of a log sawn off while the log is made into planks. The verb to slab means to cut these pieces from a log so that it can be squared, or sawn into boards with square edges. In Australia, slab also meant a piece of timber two or three inches thick, hewn with the axe rather than sawn, used for the walls of rough houses, and in Australian and New Zealand English a slab building is one made of such coarse planks. This is the sense of slab hut.

The French term is dosse. The Grand dictionnaire terminologique of the Office québécois de la langue française defines it as any outer part of a log that the saw removes when the log is ripped lengthwise: a piece with one flat face, while the other side keeps the rounded surface of the log, with or without bark. In Quebec French, and sometimes in France, the spoken word is croûte ("crust"). Taking the slab off a log is called découvrir la grume or blanchir la grume ("uncovering" or "whitening the log"), and the flat face so made is a découvert. In his 1814 vocabulary of carpentry, the architect J. M. R. Morisot defined dosses as the pieces taken off with the saw to bring a timber to sharp edges (vive arête) and to an even size, and the verb dédosser as dressing a timber with the saw to sharp edges by cutting away the parts that still show wane. In the same vocabulary, dosse also meant a thick plank used as lagging on the centring of a vault, to hold back earth in a trench, or as a sheet pile in a cofferdam. The board sawn next after the slab is the contre-dosse. Morisot's vocabulary of joinery describes the slab itself, a waney plank from the first cuts on the trunk, as "good for little", and the contre-dosses as of better use. The architect Jean-Baptiste Rondelet explained the two terms in his treatise on building. The slabs are the first cuts made on the trunk, after the bark has been removed, to square it. articles.title: Cambarinho Botanical Reserve
articles.text:
Cambarinho Botanical Reserve

The Cambarinho Botanical Reserve is a 24-hectare (59-acre) protected area on the northern slopes of the Serra do Caramulo, in the municipality of Vouzela, Portugal. It was set up by Decree 364/71 of 25 August 1971 to protect a stand of Rhododendron ponticum subsp. baeticum, which is known locally as loendro and elsewhere as adelfeira. A Vouzela walking-trail leaflet calls it the first national botanical reserve in Portugal.
The reserve is a Natura 2000 Special Area of Conservation (site code PTCON0016) and lies entirely inside the Vouga-Caramulo Local Natural Park. It burned completely in the wildfires of 2017 and again in July 2026.


== Geography ==
The reserve is in the parishes of Campia (15.5 ha) and Cambra e Carvalhal de Vermilhas (8.4 ha), and covers part of the valley of the Cambarinho stream. The plant grows naturally along tributaries of the Alfusqueiro River, where the moisture and soil suit it.


== The loendro ==
Rhododendron ponticum subsp. baeticum is a shrub that grows two to four metres tall, usually in sheltered valleys close to small streams. It belongs to the heath family, Ericaceae, and has large violet flowers. The local name loendro is also used in Portugal for oleander, an unrelated plant.
The plant is considered a survivor of the flora of the Tertiary period that died out in most places during the ice ages. In Portugal it was first recorded in 1799 in the Serra da Fóia, Monchique. In 1884 the botanist Júlio Henriques of the University of Coimbra found it along the Alfusqueiro during an expedition to the Serra do Caramulo. Smaller populations exist in Monchique, Odemira, and the Sierras del Aljibe in Cádiz, Spain.
The plant is poisonous, and livestock used to die after eating its leaves. Attempts to transplant it have failed because it is very delicate.


== Habitats ==
The ICNF management plan lists five protected habitat types:

The plan rates all three main target habitats as being in poor or inadequate condition and still declining. The only fauna species of note it lists is the marbled newt.


== Threats ==
Before 2017, maritime pine dominated the reserve and the land around it, which the ICNF says may have helped the fire spread. Since the fire, regrowth of eucalyptus in the western part of the reserve, about 13 percent of its area, competes with the native habitats for water and nutrients and raises the fire risk. The plan also warns that heavy scrub clearing and tree thinning for fire prevention

articles.title: Lines & Circles (album)
articles.text:
Lines & Circles (album)

Lines & Circles is the third studio album by American pop group O-Town, released on August 24, 2014, through All About The Melody. It was the group's first full-length album since O2 (2002) and their first following their reunion as a four-member group without original member Ashley Parker Angel.


== Background and release ==
Following their reunion, O-Town premiered a preview of “Skydive” on SoundCloud on May 28, 2014. The song was released as the lead single from Lines & Circles on July 27, 2014. Group member Trevor Penick described it as a dramatic, mid-tempo song that builds from piano and vocals to an orchestral arrangement featuring the group's four-part harmonies.
“Chasin’ After You” was subsequently released as another single from the album.
The album contains ten tracks.


== Critical reception ==
Pip Ellwood-Hughes of Entertainment Focus noted that although the group demonstrated strong vocal abilities, Lines & Circles lacked a clear musical identity because it attempted to appeal to different audiences. She criticised “Skydive” for resembling Westlife's style and described “Sometimes Love Ain't Enough” and “Lines & Circles” as generic.
However, Ellwood-Hughes praised “I Won't Lose” and “Buried Alive” for their stripped-down arrangements and emphasis on the group's vocals. She concluded that the album failed to leave a lasting impression and that the group had “lost their identity somewhere in the mix”.
Robert Ward of Renowned for Sound described Lines & Circles as an album of inconsistent quality, while acknowledging the effort the group had put into the record.
Ward noted that opening track “Chasin’ After You” retained the group's original sound, praising its catchy chorus despite finding the vocals on the verses less effective. He described “Skydive” as a melancholy ballad built around piano and strings, although he felt its chorus hook was slightly off-beat. He singled out “Rewind” as a highlight for its distinctive beat and moody synthesiser melody, while considering “Playing with Fire” merely adequate. He found “I Won't Lose” similar in quality to “Playing with Fire” despite its greater emphasis on guitar, and considered “Right Kind of Wrong” a slight improvement due to its upbeat arrangement.
Discussing the latter half of the album, Ward felt that “Buried Alive” lacked interest despite its stripped-down acoustic arrangement. He described “Got to Go” as a soulful track with a swaggering rhythm but found it only pas

articles.title: NAC (National Archives Catalog)
articles.text:
NAC (National Archives Catalog)

The National Archives Catalog is the online catalog of the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), the agency that keeps the permanent records of the United States federal government. It is NARA's main tool for describing its holdings, and it gives access to electronic records and digitized copies of archival material. As of October 2026, the catalog held 532,047,895 digitized pages.
The catalog searches several NARA resources at once, including archival descriptions, digitized and electronic records, and authority records. More than 95 percent of NARA's holdings are described at least at the series level. Searchable text also includes optical character recognition (OCR) output from digitized documents and tags, comments, and transcriptions added by volunteers.


== History ==


=== Online Public Access ===
NARA released the Online Public Access (OPA) prototype on 27 December 2010. Before then, researchers had to search separately in the Archival Research Catalog (ARC) for descriptions, in Access to Archival Databases (AAD) for electronic records, and on Archives.gov. OPA brought these searches together in one place. At launch the prototype held all ARC data, seven AAD series with 10.9 million permanent electronic records, and one million records from the Electronic Records Archives that were not available anywhere else online.


=== Citizen contributions ===
NARA's Innovation Hub, opened in July 2015, included a scanning lab where members of the public could scan archival records. In the following period, more than 57,000 page images scanned by the public were added to the catalog, putting those records online for the first time. Through the Citizen Archivist program, volunteers add tags, transcriptions, and comments to catalog records.


=== Digitization milestones and redesign ===
In August 2022 the catalog passed 200 million digitized pages. NARA credited internal offices and outside partners such as Ancestry and FamilySearch, along with technical upgrades to its image upload process.
A fully redesigned catalog was introduced in September 2022 and formally launched on 21 November 2022. It added a mobile-first design, better image viewing, faster search, and Login.gov accounts for Citizen Archivist contributions. articles.title: Kabgayi Genocide Memorial
articles.text:
Kabgayi Genocide Memorial

The Kabgayi Genocide Memorial is a memorial site and burial ground for victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. It is located in Kabgayi, in Muhanga District, Southern Province, Rwanda.
The memorial honours the many Tutsi who sought refuge in Kabgayi during the genocide. Many of them were killed there, or taken away and killed elsewhere.


== Location ==

The memorial is on Kabgayi hill, south of the town of Muhanga, formerly called Gitarama. It is near the Kabgayi Cathedral, Kabgayi Hospital and several schools of the Catholic Church.


== History ==


=== Refuge at Kabgayi ===
During the genocide, Kabgayi became a refuge for thousands of Tutsi. They came from the communes of Gitarama Prefecture, especially Mushubati, Tambwe, Ntongwe, Mugina, Taba and Buringa. Others had fled the killings in Kigali. They sheltered in the primary school, the Petit Séminaire of Kabgayi, Saint-Joseph secondary school and the CND convent. They hoped that church land would protect them, as it had in 1959.
From 15 April 1994, Father Vjeko Ćurić, a Franciscan priest, drove refugees from Kivumu to Kabgayi. He paid bribes to the Interahamwe at roadblocks. In May 1994, Human Rights Watch estimated that about 50,000 displaced people were in Kabgayi, most of them Tutsi. The government of the time refused to recognise the neutrality of Kabgayi Hospital.


=== Killings ===
Life for the refugees in Kabgayi was very hard. Killers attacked the site often and chose people to kill. Anyone who tried to leave could be caught and killed by the Interahamwe. Many Tutsi, especially men and boys, were gathered and put on ONATRACOM buses. They were taken to Ngororero and killed there. Human Rights Watch also reported that groups of people were taken from the Tutsi refugee camp at the church centre in Kabgayi and killed. Survivors also say that women and girls were raped, and that men were taken to unknown places and killed.
On 2 June 1994, at about 9 a.m., the Rwandan Patriotic Front took Kabgayi and rescued the refugees who were still there.


== Features ==

The memorial lies below the hill of Kabgayi Cathedral, near the hospital. Like other memorials in Rwanda, it hosts the annual Kwibuka commemoration ceremonies required by law.

articles.title: Cyarwa Genocide Memorial
articles.text:
Cyarwa Genocide Memorial

The Cyarwa Genocide Memorial is a memorial site and burial ground for victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi. It is located in Tumba Sector, Huye District, in the Southern Province of Rwanda.
The memorial holds the remains of more than 11,000 victims of the genocide.


== Location ==

The memorial is in Tumba Sector, in Huye District. It lies near the city of Huye, formerly called Butare.


== History ==
The Cyarwa memorial is one of the commemoration sites linked to the genocide in the former Butare Prefecture. Many massacres took place in this prefecture in 1994.
The 28th commemoration was held at Cyarwa on 21 April 2022. At this event, witnesses said that the killings in the area began after a speech by the interim president Théodore Sindikubwabo. He gave this speech in Butare on 19 April 1994 and urged people to kill. The Minister of Health, Daniel Ngamije, described Sindikubwabo as a doctor who chose to become a killer.


== Features ==

The Cyarwa memorial holds the remains of more than 11,000 victims of the genocide.
On 15 May 2021, the remains of 48 victims were reburied with dignity at the memorial. Forty-seven of them had been found in Akamuhoza village between 26 and 28 April 2021. One had been brought from Ngoma Sector. The ceremony was attended by the Vice-President of the Senate, Espérance Nyirasafari, and by Théodate Siboyintore, president of Ibuka in Huye District.


== See also ==
Rwandan genocide

articles.title: Arthur Gerlt
articles.text:
Arthur Gerlt

Arthur Erich Richard Gerlt (13 May 1903 – 17 February 1996) was a German resistance fighter and mayor of Bemerode, which later became a district of Hanover, Germany.


== Life ==
Arthur Gerlt worked as a metalworker at the Wülfel Ironworks (Eisenwerk Wülfel) in Hanover. Following the Nazi seizure of power in 1933, he joined the resistance group Committee for Proletarian Unity (Komitee für Proletarische Einheit), led by Eduard Wald. In 1935, Gerlt was arrested  on charges of “preparation to commit high treason.” He subsequently spent 13 months in pretrial detention before being sentenced to two years and ten months in prison. He served his sentence alongside other political prisoners at Hamelin Prison.
After Hanover was liberated by American troops on 10 April 1945, two members of the Social Democratic Party of Germany appealed to the British military authorities on Gerlt's behalf. As a result, on 1 July 1945, he was appointed mayor of Bemerode, replacing the incumbent Nazi Party mayor (NSDAP).
Following Bemerode's first municipal elections after the Second World War, Arthur Gerlt was elected municipal director (Gemeindedirektor). At the time, Bemerode was a village of approximately 900 inhabitants, yet it was required to accommodate and feed 750 refugees. Some were housed in a refugee camp, while others were placed in the homes of existing residents, and not all long-established inhabitants were willing to accept the newcomers. The compulsory requisitioning of available living space therefore did not proceed smoothly. Some residents reportedly attempted to avoid having their homes requisitioned through various tricks and evasions, creating considerable tensions. Furthermore, local farmers were required to organise food supplies for the refugees, something they were not always willing to do. 
Gerlt was not reconfirmed in his position by the municipal council at the end of 1947, and following that he moved to Bad Essen, where he became director of a convalescent home for victims of Nazi persecution. 


== Commemoration ==
Approximately a decade after Arthur Gerlt's death in 1996, his great-granddaughter, Katharina Langfeldt, researched and documented the history of her great-grandfather's life. In recognition of her work, she received an award from German Federal President Horst Köhler in 2007.
Following this, Klaus Kaiser, then an SPD representative on the district council, initiated a proposal to name a street after the former mayor of Bemero

articles.title: Yufang
articles.text:
Yufang

The Yufang was an ancient Chinese state categorised as a fangguo by the Late Shang people, which existed around the reign of Di Yi. It is noted for waging a significant war against the Shang dynasty.


== Name ==

Yu (盂) is a name to a type of bronzeware, specifically a kind with two handles and no cover, used for sacrificial offerings of wine or food.


== History ==

The Yufang are mentioned as having attacked the Shang in the 9th year of Di Yi's reign, with no documented mentions prior to that point. The inciting incident appears to be noted in Hebu《合補》11242:

甲戌王卜，貞：……盂方率伐西或（國），……西田，……盂方，綏余一人，余其比多田甾征盂方，亡左自上下于徹……
On the Jiawu day, the King (Di Yi) performed scapulimancy. Charge: The Yufang have led an invasion into the Western Kingdom (Xiguo?) [...] Western fields [...] the Yufang, they approach. I, the ruler, shall mobilize the tian (田) to launch a punitive expedition against the Yufang. But will there be assistance from my ancestors? 

A joining of Heji《合集》36518 and Cunbu《存補》5.146.1 reveals that the Yufang had seemingly rebelled and stationed themselves in a place called Gao (高):

乙巳，王貞：啟呼祝曰：「盂方人，其出伐，屯高」，其令束䢔于高，弗每，不萈（緩）翦。王占曰：吉。其令束䢔高，每。吉。在九月。
On the Yisi day, the King (Di Yi) charged: "The people of the Yufang are attacking and have stationed themselves in Gao." Should I order my troops to subdue(?) Gao, but not every time, and not to slack?  The king prognosticated: Auspicious. Should we order [this], each time, [is that right]? Auspicious. It was in the ninth month.

Jiang Yubin (蔣玉斌) argues this was a rebellion based on reading tun (屯) in its respective oracle bone inscription as chun (蠢) "to wriggle." This would make sense, as having an Earl (伯) implies some amicable relations with the Shang state prior to the war. Little is known about the war itself, including the outcome, though an inscription from Di Yi's tenth year describes him hunting a short-horned water buffalo on his way back from an excursion.


== Location ==
The Yufang was seemingly located in Henan, west of Yin, but the precise settlement has not been identified. Based on geographic descriptions, Ma Panpan (2022) argues that the Yufang must have been attacking from the west of Shang, given proximity to the Qinyang (沁陽) region in which Di Yi would hunt animals. However, Guo Moruo argued that it must have been southeast, which relied on a theory that Di Yi was also fighting a war against the Renfang; this is generally not held anymore and attributed to Di Xin instead. The Chines

articles.title: Waldo Lyon (Nebraska pioneer)
articles.text:
Waldo Lyon (Nebraska pioneer)

Waldo Lyon (1810 – October 17, 1884) was an American farmer, land speculator, and pioneer of Wisconsin and Nebraska.  He was the founder and namesake of Lyons, Nebraska; a staunch advocate for temperance, he established a strict and lasting prohibition on alcohol sales within the town.  He served one term in the Nebraska Senate, representing Burt and Washington counties in the 1875 term.  Before moving to Nebraska, he was an early settler of Dodge County, Wisconsin, and served one term in the Wisconsin State Assembly, representing Dodge County's 3rd Assembly district during the 12th Wisconsin Legislature (1859).  


== Biography ==
Waldo Lyon was born in Vermont in 1810.  As a young man, Lyon resided in Connecticut.
He went west to the Wisconsin Territory in the early 1840s, and became one of the earliest settlers in what is now the town of Oak Grove, Dodge County, Wisconsin.  Shortly after arriving in Wisconsin, Lyon became active with the Whig Party, and ran as a Whig Party candidate for delegate to Wisconsin's 1847–1848 constitutional convention.  The Democratic slate won all three delegate slots from Dodge County.
After the ratification of the constitution in March 1848, Lyon sought the Whig nomination for Wisconsin Senate, in the 10th Senate district, but the Whig convention nominated Charles S. Bristol instead; Bristol lost the general election.  A year later, the Whigs nominated Lyon as their nominee for state Senate, but he was also defeated in the 1849 general election.
Over the next several years, Lyon remained active as a leading Whig in Dodge County, but didn't make further runs for office as a Whig.  During those years, he was also active in the movement to establish agricultural societies in the state, and was one of the initial officers of the Dodge and Jefferson Counties Agricultural Society.  
In 1854, the Whig Party folded and the Republican Party rose up in its place.  Lyon quickly adhered to the new Republican Party, and, in 1858, he was the Republican nominee for Wisconsin State Assembly in Dodge County's 3rd Assembly district.  This time, Lyon was elected; he went on to serve in the 12th Wisconsin Legislature.  
In 1859, there was a split within the Dodge County Republican Party, and Lyon ran for re-election as an independent candidate against the regular Republican nominee Jonathan W. Nash.  Nash prevailed in the general election by 12 votes.

articles.title: Byma
articles.text:
Byma

Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos S.A. (BYMA) is an Argentine stock exchange and financial market infrastructure operator based in Buenos Aires. It provides securities trading, clearing and settlement services and, through its subsidiary Caja de Valores, central securities depository services.
BYMA was created after Capital Markets Law No. 26,831 reorganized the Argentine capital market. It was formed through a spin-off of the Mercado de Valores de Buenos Aires (Merval), with the participation of the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (BCBA). The National Securities Commission (CNV) approved its registration as a market in December 2016.


== History ==


=== Establishment and launch ===
Law No. 26,831 was enacted in 2012. In July 2013, Merval shareholders approved a partial spin-off to create BYMA, with a capital contribution from the BCBA.
On 29 December 2016, the CNV approved BYMA's registration as a market. Merval transferred its trading activities to BYMA in 2017, and trading moved from the SINAC platform to the Millennium system.


=== Market development ===
In December 2024, five new CEDEARs representing ETFs were listed. Two of them, ETHA and IBIT, track Ethereum and Bitcoin. They were the first cryptocurrency ETFs available as CEDEARs in Argentina. The other three were GLD (gold), SH (an inverse S&P 500 fund) and FXI (Chinese equities).
BYMA Clearing went into operation in April 2026. Built on Nasdaq technology, it handles clearing, settlement, collateral and risk management.
From 2018 to 2026, S&P Dow Jones Indices calculated and administered BYMA's equity indices. On 19 October 2026, MSCI assumed responsibility for the indices.
The S&P Merval became the MSCI Merval (MMSCI), while the BYMA General Index was replaced by the MSCI BYMA Argentina General (GMSCI). Both indices started with a base value of 100,000 points and are published in Argentine pesos and US dollars.
The MSCI Merval initially included 19 stocks. Cresud entered the index, replacing Telecom Argentina and Sociedad Comercial del Plata, which were removed from the previous composition. The new methodology limits each stock to 15% of the index's total weight, with quarterly reviews in February, May, August and November.

articles.title: Achilles (Ennius)
articles.text:
Achilles (Ennius)

Achilles or Achilles Aristarchi is a tragedy by Ennius preserved in a select few fragments. It appears that the text described the attempts to convince Achilles to rejoin the Greek army after he had abandoned the fighting.


== Title ==
The alternative title Achilles Aristarchi ("Achilles of Aristarchus") appears in the prologue to Plautus's play Poenulus and also the works of Verrius Flaccus, as quoted by Festus. It is not entirely clear that this alternative title denotes the same play about Achilles by Ennius as the other mentions of Ennius's Achilles. If Plautus was, in fact, trying to describe a different play, then the specifier "of Aristarchus" ("Aristarchi") would perhaps serve to distinguish the work from the other Ennian play Achilles. Alternatively, the classicist H. D. Jocelyn suggests that the original source for this variant title was merely remembering or reading the didascaliae. In any case, whatever play Plautus was describing was itself presumably based on the tragedy Achilles authored by Aristarchus of Tegea. This Plautine reference also implies that this Ennian play was composed before c. 190 BCE. 


== Fragments ==
One passage is possibly preserved in the works of Cicero, who writes "such great floods were being cast ashore" ("ita magni fluctus eiciebantur"), which—according to a later scholiast—was taken from the play Achilles. The stylistic features of this quote are unusual for Cicero, but common in works of Roman tragedy, namely that ita ("thus, so, it this way") is utilized as a causative participle and that the sentence is terminated by a word as long as eiciebantur ("to cast, throw"). The scholiast refers to this line as a hemistich, a detail that is—according to the classicist H. D. Jocelyn—inaccurate. Other scholiasts on Virgil make similar errors, and also mistakenly claim that certain passages are quotes from other authors of dramas, when they were in fact merely authored by Virgil in the style of other poems. Therefore, Jocelyn suggests that this particular scholiast on Cicero may have erroneously wrote that a fragment was quote from Ennius, when it was in fact created by Cicero in imitation of the language of Roman tragedy. It is possible that some storm sent by Apollo was a part of the plot of the Achilles, as Apollo—in the Iliad—causes Agamemnon to insult Achilles. articles.title: Saul and David (film)
articles.text:
Saul and David (film)

Saul and David (Italian: Saul e David) is a 1964 Italian-Spanish biblical epic film directed and co-written by Marcello Baldi. Based on the Books of Samuel, it stars Norman Wooland as King Saul and Gianni Garko as his successor, David.


== Cast ==
Norman Wooland as Saul
Gianni Garko as David
Luz Márquez as Abigail
Virgílio Teixeira as Abner
Elisa Cegani as Ahinoam
Pilar Clemens as Michal
Carlos Casaravilla as Samuel
Marco Paoletti as young David
Paolo Gozlino as Joab
Antonio Mayans as Jonathan (as Antony Mayans)
Giorgio Cerioni
Andrea Sciré as Saul's son
Barta Barri (as Barta Barry)
Dante Maggio
Stefy Lang as Goliath


== Production ==
Saul and David is the second biblical film produced by a priest named Emilio Cordero, the head of San Paolo Film in Rome and San Pablo Film in Madrid. Cordero's first biblical production was The Patriarchs, but he reluctantly sold that film to Italian producer Dino De Laurentiis, who saw The Patriarchs as a competitor to his own film The Bible: In the Beginning... (1966). With the money De Laurentiis paid for the first film, Cordero planned to make other biblical films. Cordero described Saul and David as an effort "to break the ice of the world market."
Produced on a budget of $1,500,000, the film was shot on location in Almería and on the backlot of the Cinecittà studios in Rome. Writing for The New York Times, Robert F. Hawkins said, "An Italian director [Marcello Baldi] is in charge, firing instructions in a garbled but effective blend of languages at a cast principally made up of British, Italian and Spanish actors, all of whom mouth a colorful, if not always intelligible, brand of English, the language in which it is being recorded." 50 technicians worked on the film, and 6,000 extras, 5,000 horses, and 1,000 camels appeared in it.
The film was one of a series of 24 three-hour biblical films (12 for each Testament) planned by San Paolo that would take more than ten years to film and cost between $16 and $20 million.

In August 1965, Reuters reported that Saul and David "received formidable reviews when shown recently at a large cinema in Rome." Segnalazioni cinematografiche (Film Reports) gave the film a positive review: "The film includes the events narrated in the Bible in the first book of Kings. Faithfully following the Sacred Text, it translates with a balanced sense of spectacle the dramatic religious and psychological conflict between the first King of Israel and the man

articles.title: Memrik Colony
articles.text:
Memrik Colony

The Memrik Colony (German: Memriker Ansiedlung or Memrik Kolonie) was a Russian Mennonite daughter settlement of the Molotschna colony, founded in 1885 in the Bakhmut district of Yekaterinoslav Governorate in the Russian Empire, in what is now Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. It lay on the Volchya River, a tributary of the Samara, about 20 miles (32 km) from Yuzovka (now Donetsk). Before the First World War it had about 3,500 inhabitants. Its Mennonite population was largely destroyed by revolution, famine, collectivisation and deportation, and the last Mennonites were deported eastward in 1941.


== History ==


=== Founding ===
In 1884 the Halbstadt and Gnadenfeld districts of the Molotschna settlement bought 32,400 acres (13,100 ha) from the noblemen Kotlyarevsky and Karpov for 600,000 rubles to settle landless families. The Mennonite family-history site chortitza.org gives the same price for about 12,000 desyatinas. A total of 221 families with 1,367 people settled in ten villages. To qualify, the head of a landless family had to lead "a quiet and moral life", be industrious, and own a wagon, plough, harrow, two horses and two cows. Settlers were expected to repay their loans with interest to Molotschna within 15 years.
The ten villages, with their later Russian names, were Alexanderhof (Alexandrovka), Bahndorf (Orlov), Ebental (Nikolayevka), Karpovka, Kotlyarevka, Marienort (Kalinovo), Memrik, Michaelsheim (Michailovka), Nordheim (Marinovka) and Waldeck (Lessowka). Molotschna Mennonites also founded the nearby villages of Alexandropol (1888) and Ossokino (1890s), which were closely linked to Memrik.


=== Administration and economy ===
Memrik was at first administered by Molotschna, more than 100 miles (160 km) away. Its attempt to form its own volost failed, and in 1888 it was incorporated into the neighbouring Russian volost of Golitzynovo against the settlers' wishes. A fire insurance agency was organised in 1901.
The early years were hard, with grasshoppers, gophers and low prices. Farmers rotated wheat, feed crops and summer fallow, switching from spring to winter wheat around 1905, and kept "German Red" and later Holstein cattle. Produce was sold in Yuzovka, Mariupol and Berdyansk. Milling became the main industry, with steam mills in several villages. Julius Legin's agricultural machinery works at Waldeck, founded in 1895, produced about 1,000 reapers, 600 ploughs and 300 fanning mills a year before the First World War.

articles.title: Wurrook
articles.text:
Wurrook

Wurrook is a historic pastoral property and homestead near Rokewood, in the Western District of Victoria, Australia. Established during the 1840s, the estate became a prominent producer of superfine Merino wool under the Russell family, who acquired it in 1857. The property contains a bluestone homestead dating from 1861, together with a nineteenth-century shearing shed and associated agricultural buildings. Since 1954, Wurrook has been owned by the Walton family, who have continued its operation as a merino stud. The estate is also used for visitor accommodation and events.


== History ==
The origins of Wurrook date to 1840, when pastoralist Thomas Bingley and his business partner Compton Ferrers acquired part of the extensive landholdings of the Derwent Company. The property encompassed approximately 30,000 acres (12,000 ha) and was officially known as the Wardy Yallock Chain of Ponds, although it was also referred to as Wurrook. The partnership was subsequently dissolved, and Ferrers became involved in the management of several other pastoral properties in the Western District.

In 1857, the estate was purchased by Philip and Thomas Russell, members of a family with extensive pastoral interests across western Victoria. Thomas Russell, who had previously acquired the nearby Barunah Plains estate, subsequently established Wurrook as his principal residence. A substantial bluestone homestead was constructed in 1861, overlooking a lagoon on the Kuruc-A-Ruc Creek. The residence featured spacious interior rooms and an elevated tower providing views over the surrounding countryside.
During the 1860s, the estate underwent further development, including the construction of a larger bluestone shearing shed. Architect Alexander Davidson, who had established his practice at Rokewood after arriving from Scotland in 1864, undertook architectural work at Wurrook in 1866. Davidson later formed a partnership with George Henderson, and both architects became associated with several major homesteads in the Western District, including Barunah Plains and Barwon Park.
The estate was managed for much of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries by Donald McLaren, who commenced working at Wurrook around 1861. Born in Argyllshire, Scotland, McLaren was entrusted with the day-to-day management of the property by Thomas Russell. He remained at Wurrook for more than five decades, until his death in November 1917.

articles.title: Standard of living in Taiwan
articles.text:
Standard of living in Taiwan

The standard of living in Taiwan refers to the material conditions, income, consumption, housing, health, work, public services, and other factors that shape everyday life in Taiwan. Taiwan is often regarded by international organizations such as the International Monetary Fund as a high-income, developed country with long life expectancy, low crime, extensive public transport, and broad access to consumer goods and services. At the same time, its living standards have been affected by high housing costs in major cities, stagnant wages, an ageing population, regional disparities, and relatively high living costs for some goods and services.
The 1970s witnessed a big rise in living standards, which was characterized by the increased diffusion of various consumer durables. The average national life expectancy rise from around fifty-five years in 1950 to seventy-two years in 1985 and eight-one in 2025. 


== History ==

During Qing rule, the standard of living in Taiwan was  characterized by widespread poverty, extreme income inequalities, and endemic insecurity of livelihood. Malaria and plague were widespread in the towns. The sewage was dumped straight onto the street and soaked into the ground. After Taiwan was ceded to Japan, in July of 1896, a Scottish engineer, W. K. Burton , was brought in to look at the city of Taipei. He proposed the "Taihoku sanitary works plan", which included a separate water supply and sewage system. In 1900, an urban planning official named Yoshio Murakami drew up the plan that set the basic shape of modern Taipei. In 1908, the first public water works opened at the pumping station that is now the Museum of Drinking Water, which supplied about 20,000 tons of water a day to 120,000 residents.
After a period of hyperinflation in the late 1940s when the Kuomintang-led government of the Republic of China military regime of Chen Yi overprinted the Taiwanese dollar against the previous Taiwanese yen in the Japanese era, the government introduced a new and stable currency to address hyperinflation. articles.title: Sommerfeld Colony
articles.text:
Sommerfeld Colony

Sommerfeld Colony (Spanish: Colonia Sommerfeld) is a Mennonite settlement in the district of Doctor Juan Eulogio Estigarribia, Caaguazú Department, in eastern Paraguay. It was founded in 1948 by Sommerfeld Mennonites from Manitoba, Canada, together with the neighbouring Bergthal Colony. With 4,963 inhabitants in 2022 it was the third-largest Mennonite settlement in Paraguay, after Menno and Fernheim. Its cooperative is one of the main industrial employers in the department.


== History ==
The settlers of Sommerfeld and Bergthal were descendants of Mennonites who had moved from Russia to Canada between 1874 and 1918. They left Canada because of what they saw as the inroads of secular society into their congregations. Paraguay offered them closed settlements where they could educate their children in their own German-language schools. In 1948, 740 people from Manitoba's East Reserve, 764 from the West Reserve and 140 from Saskatchewan emigrated. Those from the East Reserve founded Bergthal Colony. The group boarded the Volendam at Quebec City on 25 June 1948, travelled by riverboat from Buenos Aires to Asunción and by train to Villarrica, and arrived there on 23 July 1948.
There was no road to most of the land, so the settlers built one themselves, largely through heavy forest. While they waited, about a third of the emigrants returned to Canada, including 75 families (383 people) from Sommerfeld in the first two years. In 1953 Sommerfeld had 644 inhabitants in 119 families, living in nine villages on about 93,000 acres (38,000 ha). The colony centre was the village of Sommerfeld, home of the elder, Isbrandt Friesen, and of the cooperative. According to the regional broadcaster RCC, 973 people arrived from Canada for the colony in 1948, of whom 624 stayed as its pioneers. ACOMEPA's statistics also give 973 immigrants.
The arrival of the German-Canadian Mennonites from the late 1940s, and the sawmills they set up to work the forest, began the urban growth of what became the town of Campo 9, which was made a district in 1981. The colony celebrated its 75th anniversary on 20 July 2023.


== Geography ==
The colony lies about 210 kilometres (130 mi) east of Asunción along the highway to the Brazilian border. In 1986 it owned 31,428 hectares (77,660 acres). Two of its villages, Neuhoffnung (Campo 9) and Altona (Campo 8), lie directly on the highway. Bergthal Colony is about 20 kilometres (12 mi) away.

articles.title: La Nueva Trinidad
articles.text:
La Nueva Trinidad

La Nueva Trinidad (also La Trinidad or Nueva Trinidad) is a Mennonite colony in Hopelchén Municipality, in the Mexican state of Campeche. It is one of the main Mennonite communities in the municipality, alongside Nuevo Durango, El Temporal and Nuevo Progreso. The colony is made up of several numbered campos (line villages).


== Geography ==
The colony covers about 24.7 square kilometres (9.5 sq mi). It lies in the Chenes region of Campeche, one of the state's main grain-producing areas: in 2020 Hopelchén produced 50,948 tonnes of soybeans, 31,191 tonnes of maize and 10,956 tonnes of sorghum.


== Economy ==
Like the other Mennonite colonies of Campeche, La Nueva Trinidad lives mainly from mechanised grain farming, chiefly maize, sorghum and soybeans. According to Franz Peters Fehr and Abraham Unger Wiebe of the Nueva Trinidad community, Campeche's 18 Mennonite colonies expected to harvest about 164,442 tonnes of grain in the 2021 farm year, 54.4 percent of the state's projected output. In November 2021 the colony hosted a meeting between Mennonite colonies of the region and the federal environment, environmental-enforcement and water agencies (Semarnat, Profepa and Conagua).


== El Progreso and El Porvenir land dispute ==
In 2018 Luis Eduardo Huitz Villareal filed a criminal complaint for alleged dispossession (despojo) against Johan Neufeld Wall, a member of the La Trinidad community, over the El Progreso and El Porvenir tracts, which together cover about 500 hectares (1,200 acres). The complaint led to a dispute over possession of the land that lasted almost a decade. The community lost access to the land when it was put under padlock. According to Eraclio Rodríguez Gómez, leader of the Frente Nacional para el Rescate del Campo Mexicano, which supported the farmers, about 300 hectares (740 acres) of sorghum close to harvest, worth about six million pesos, was on the land at the time. He estimated total losses from missed harvests at up to 20 million pesos. In the days before the ruling the farmers had held a march and sit-in at the Government Palace in the city of Campeche. They paused the protest after state executive and judicial officials offered to review the case file.

articles.title: Augusto Malta
articles.text:
Augusto Malta

Augusto César Malta de Campos (14 May 1864 — 30 June 1957), was a Brazilian photographer who served as the official photographer for the Federal District between 1903 and 1936. During this period, he captured more than eighty thousand photographs; his work now stands as one of the primary visual records of the transformations that took place in the city of Rio de Janeiro in the early 20th century.


== Biography ==


=== Early years and family ===
Malta was born in Mata Grande, in the countryside of Alagoas, in 1864. He lived in the province until the age of 22—in 1886—when he left for Recife, where he served as a cadet sergeant in the Imperial Brazilian Army. During this period, he became a republican and took part in revolutionary meetings with students.
At the end of 1888, he arrived in Rio de Janeiro and began working at the furniture and upholstery firm Casa Leandro Martins, located on Ourives Street (now Miguel Couto Street). He worked as a clerical assistant and, the following year, was promoted to bookkeeper. Also in 1889, he took part in the events surrounding the proclamation of the Republic in Brazil, serving as one of the signatories to the oath read at the Chamber of the Neutral Municipality, which inaugurated the provisional republican government.
In the 1890s, he married a distant cousin, Laura Oliveira Campos, who was from Alagoas. The couple had four daughters—Luthgardes, Arethusa, Callisthene, and Aristocléa—and one son, Aristógiton. All of the couple’s daughters died of tuberculosis, while Aristógiton went on to become a photographer like his father. In 1905, Laura passed away, and Malta began living in a common-law marriage with Celina Augusta Verschueren, a nanny of Belgian origin who had worked for Laura's children since the age of fifteen. With Celina, he had four more children: Dirce, Eglé, Uriel, and Amaltéa.


=== Official photographer ===
In 1900, Malta sold fine fabrics in the center of Rio de Janeiro and used a bicycle to deliver orders. One of his customers, a Navy midshipman, proposed trading his camera for Malta's bicycle. Following this exchange, Malta began to take an interest in photography. In 1903, he was introduced—by contractor Antônio Alves da Silva Júnior, a supplier for the Federal District municipal government who had already seen his photographs—to Mayor Francisco Pereira Passos. articles.title: The Greatest Show on Earth Tour
articles.text:
The Greatest Show on Earth Tour

The Greatest Show on Earth Tour (officially titled Carnaval de Luz Presents: The Greatest Show on Earth) is an upcoming worldwide concert tour by the Irish rock band U2. Staged in support of their forthcoming sixteenth studio album, Carnaval de Luz (2026), the tour is scheduled to begin on 23 February 2027 at Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City, Mexico. Initially announced on 15 October 2026, the tour will feature stadium concerts in Latin America, with further performances planned for Europe and North America.
The tour marks U2's return to stadium touring for the first time since The Joshua Tree Tour 2019, which concluded in Mumbai, India, on 15 December 2019. It will also mark the return of drummer Larry Mullen Jr. to touring with the band following his absence from their 2023–2024 Las Vegas concert residency while recovering from surgery.
The initial announcement confirmed six concerts across three cities: Mexico City, São Paulo, and Buenos Aires. American musician Beck was announced as the opening act for all six performances. The band stated that additional European and North American dates would be announced subsequently, with plans for concerts in their native Ireland also being developed.
The tour takes its name from "The Greatest Show on Earth", the third single from Carnaval de Luz, which was released on the same day as the tour announcement. The band has described the forthcoming production as an attempt to combine the spectacle of a stadium performance with the intimacy and connection of a smaller concert.


== Background ==


=== Previous touring activities ===
U2's previous worldwide stadium tour was The Joshua Tree Tour 2017 and 2019, which began in 2017 to commemorate the 30th anniversary of their fifth studio album, The Joshua Tree (1987). The tour was subsequently revived for concerts in Oceania and Asia in 2019, concluding on 15 December at DY Patil Stadium in Mumbai, India. Across its performances in 2017 and 2019, the tour attracted approximately three million attendees.
Following the conclusion of the tour, the band did not undertake another conventional concert tour for several years. Their next major live project was U2:UV Achtung Baby Live at Sphere, a residency at Sphere in Paradise, Nevada, near Las Vegas, which ran from September 2023 to March 2024. The residency comprised 40 performances and focused primarily on their 1991 album Achtung Baby.
The residency was performed without founding drummer L

articles.title: Paul Geelen
articles.text:
Paul Geelen

Paul Geelen (born March 14, 2003) is a Dutch professional Canadian football placekicker for the Ottawa Redblacks of the Canadian Football League (CFL). He played college football for the Southern Illinois Salukis and William Jewell Cardinals. 


== Early life ==
Geelen was born on March 14, 2003 in Utrecht, Netherlands. He attended Harper Creek High School in Battle Creek, Michigan as an exchange student.


== College career ==
Geelen played college football for the Southern Illinois Salukis from 2022 to 2023 and William Jewell Cardinals from 2024 to 2025. At William Jewell he served as the team's primary kicker and punter for two year. Geelen went 15-of-22 on field goals with a long of 49 yards and had an average of 40.0 yards per punt with a long of 62 and 29 kicks inside the 20-yard line. He earned first-team and second-team All-GLVC honors as a punter and kicker respectively.
Geelen then transferred to Southern Illinois University Carbondale for his final two seasons. As a junior, he converted 10-of-15 field goals with a long of 50 yards and made 24-of-27 PATs while averaging 43.1 yards per punt. Geelen also scored a touchdown on a fake field goal against Missouri State. In 2025, he went 15-of-17 on field goals with a long of 53 and averaged 40.8 yards per punt. Geelen earned second-team All-MVFC honors as a kicker.


== Professional career ==
Geelen was selected in the second round, with the tenth overall selection, by the Ottawa Redblacks in the 2026 CFL global draft. On May 17, he officially signed with the team. On May 31, Geelen was moved to the practice roster. On October 1, he was elevated to the active roster after the Redblacks traded Brett Lauther to the Saskatchewan Roughriders. In a loss to the Hamilton Tiger-Cats, Geelen converted three-of-four field goals and an extra point. On October 16, against the Toronto Argonauts, he kicked the winning PAT to snap a 22-game losing streak.

articles.title: The Greatest Show on Earth (U2 song)
articles.text:
The Greatest Show on Earth (U2 song)

"The Greatest Show on Earth" is a song by the Irish rock band U2. It is the eighth track from their forthcoming sixteenth studio album, Carnaval de Luz, and was released as its third single on 15 October 2026 through Island Records. The song was written by U2 and Brian Eno and produced by Jacknife Lee.
The single's release coincided with the announcement of U2's 2027 concert tour, The Greatest Show on Earth World Tour, which takes its name from the song. An accompanying music video, directed by the band's longtime collaborator Anton Corbijn, was filmed in the Californian desert and depicts the band as members of a fictional religious cult.
The song received positive reviews from several music publications, with critics highlighting its expansive arrangement, the Edge's guitar playing and its resemblance to U2's earlier anthemic material.


== Background ==
U2 announced their sixteenth studio album, Carnaval de Luz, on 24 September 2026, coinciding with the release of its second single, "Silencio". Scheduled for release on 13 November, the album is the band's first studio album of new material since Songs of Experience (2017). The album was recorded during an extended period of creative activity that also produced the six-track EPs Days of Ash and Easter Lily, both released earlier in 2026.
The album's first single, "Street of Dreams", was released on 7 July 2026, followed by "Silencio" on 24 September. "The Greatest Show on Earth" was released as the third single on 15 October, less than a month before the album's scheduled release.
"The Greatest Show on Earth" was co-written by U2 and their longtime collaborator Brian Eno, who contributed synthesizers and keyboards to the recording. Eno also contributed to two other songs on Carnaval de Luz, "Go (Carnaval de Luz)" and "Can't Stop Us Now". The album was produced by Jacknife Lee, who had previously worked with the band on several projects.
In an interview with Rolling Stone preceding the single's release, Bono identified "The Greatest Show on Earth" as his favourite song from Carnaval de Luz, describing it as potentially the band's strongest composition in several years. He stated that the song had been a significant reason for his continued enthusiasm about U2.
Bono also discussed difficulties completing the song's lyrics. According to U2Songs' account of the interview, he found inspiration after watching Baz Luhrmann's concert film about Elvis Presley, which helped hi

articles.title: Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa
articles.text:
Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa

Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa (July 26, 1983 – October 17, 2026) was a Guatemalan prosecutor, anti-corruption activist and politician.  He was best known for his work to stop government corruption and organized crime. He served as the head of the Superintendencia de Administración Tributaria de Guatemala, Guatemala's tax agency, before being removed by the president, and he previously headed criminal investigations at the Attorney General of Guatemala's office. He ran for mayor of Guatemala City in 2023.


== Life and career ==
Foppa was born on July 26, 1983. He was the grandson of poet and activist Alaíde Foppa, who was forcibly disappeared three years prior. His father was a leftist guerilla fighter during the Guatemalan Civil War. His mother was also a guerilla. Foppa, unlike them, decided to study law and attended Rafael Landívar University.
Foppa began as an assistant prosecutor in the Attorney General of Guatemala's office, where among other cases, he prosecuted homicides and organized crimes. He then became head of an office for criminal investigations that had been newly created in 2013. As head, he was responsible for the investigation and arrest of President Otto Pérez Molina for allegedly leading the bribery ring known as La Línea. He also investigated the customs tax department and headed the investigation of steel company Aceros de Guatemala.
In March 2016, he was appointed by President Jimmy Morales to head the Superintendencia de Administración Tributaria de Guatemala as Superintendent, which made him in charge of Guatemala's tax. Conservative think tanks immediately became alarmed, with one stating that he would "commit fiscal terrorism". In this position, he continued with Aceros de Guatemala, alleging they owed US$100 million in taxes, fees, and interest. The company denied this, and as such Foppa tried to seize control of the company's finances. Aceros paid the fees, the largest tax fine in Guatemalan history, but has maintained its innocence. He also investigated and extracted US$5.8 million in back taxes, fines, and interest from a company which owned hotels, partially by arresting its owner.
He investigated many similar cases, and by the end of his term extracted US$280 million. However, he later acknowledged his actions were "too aggressive", and detractors stated he "turned administrative cases into criminal cases". He also restructured the agency, removing individuals he alleged were complicit in h

articles.title: Kuruc-A-Ruc
articles.text:
Kuruc-A-Ruc

Kuruc-A-Ruc is a historic pastoral property and homestead complex near Corindhap and Rokewood, in the Western District of Victoria, Australia. Established in the late 1830s, it was among the earliest pastoral runs in the district and was associated with the Aitchison and Elder families during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The homestead, situated beside Kuruc-A-Ruc Creek, was constructed during the mid-nineteenth century and subsequently extended to designs by architect Alexander Davidson. The property is currently used for agricultural purposes and visitor accommodation.


== History ==
The Kuruc-A-Ruc pastoral run was established in 1838 by the Derwent Company, making it one of the earliest pastoral holdings in the surrounding district. The lease was subsequently acquired by the Aitchison family, with brothers George and David Aitchison taking possession in 1839. An early stone hut was constructed around 1840, followed by the development of additional buildings. By 1852, David Aitchison had become the sole proprietor of the run, and the following year he applied for a 640-acre (260 ha) pre-emptive right over the homestead land.

The original section of the homestead is believed to have been constructed during the early 1850s. Built predominantly from local stone, it formed part of a growing pastoral complex that included stbales, workers' accommodation and other agricultural buildings.
In October 1857, ownership of Kuruc-A-Ruc passed to John Elder and his sons William, John junior and Nairne Guthrie Elder. The family maintained the property as a pastoral station and undertook substantial improvements to its buildings, and in 1866 architect Alexander Davidson designed extensions to both ends of the existing homestead. Davidson, who had arrived in Rokewood from Scotland in 1864, also designed the nearby Rokewood Presbyterian Church.
The homestead was surrounded by an extensive garden, with many of its established trees believed to date from the nineteenth century. Plantings included several varieties of cypress, together with olive and mulberry trees. Two Italian cypresses were named Gog and Magog by the Elder family. The garden was laid out around the homestead and its principal approaches.
