articles.title: Torres Media
articles.text:
Torres Media

Torres Media is a Canadian independent radio broadcasting company that currently own five FM radio stations in Ontario and Quebec.   
The company's division and subsidiary SkyWords Media is the largest radio network in the country.  


== History ==
Its origins began in 1991, when Ed and his brother Frank Torres founded SkyWords Media and was originally an advertising company. It would later branch out into a radio network providing content like weather and traffic reports across three provinces in the country.
On August 26, 2008, an application for a new station at the time CIDG-FM in Ottawa was awarded to Torres Media, and approved by the CRTC the same day. The station would later begin testing its signal on 101.9 FM on June 1, 2010, and officially launched six days later.
On April 3, 2012, Frank Torres received approval from the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) to operate a new station on 105.5 MHz (for CIUX-FM). The station's launch was delayed to 2015 due to several disputes, including Bell Canada briefly opposing the station's co-location on one of its towers, and conflicts with another station owner who objected to the new station. 
On May 8, 2015, it was announced that Torres Media would acquire CKOD-FM from Radio Express, Inc. for $250,000; the sale was completed on November 24.
On July 11, 2018, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) approved an application by Frank Torres on behalf of a corporation to be incorporated (OBCI) to operate a new English language radio station at Georgina on the frequency of 93.7 MHz (for CKOU-FM). The station later began testing on October 19, 2020, and officially signed on and went live with shows on October 26, 2020.
On September 19, 2024, Evanov Communications announced that it had reached eleventh-hour agreements to sell all three stations; CJWL-FM was sold to Torres Media for $1.2 million, along with two other stations to a different company. Both groups filed applications for the purchases with the CRTC on January 24, 2025, and operated the stations under temporary management agreements until they were formally approved.
On April 20, 2026, Torres Media announced its intent to acquire CHSV-FM in Hudson and Saint-Lazare, Quebec from Evanov for $300,000.


== Radio stations ==
Georgina, Ontario: CKOU-FM
Ottawa, Ontario: CIDG-FM, CITM-FM
Uxbridge, Ontario: CIUX-FM

articles.title: Malaxis magniauriculata
articles.text:
Malaxis magniauriculata

Malaxis magniauriculata, with no English name other than adder's mouth, which is applied to all species of Malaxis, is an orchid native only to Mexico. It belongs to the huge orchid Family, the Orchidaceae.


== Description ==
Malaxis magniauriculata is similar to several of the 172 or so species of the genus Malaxis, plus it was recognized as a distinct species only in 2024, so older literature does not include it. Nonetheless, the following combination of key features enables its identification:

It is a terrestrial plant growing up to 33 cm (13 in) tall, including its inflorescence. The visible part of the orchid arises from an underground corm, which is white, egg-shaped, and measuring up to 20 mm × 15 mm (3⁄4 in × 1⁄2 in). When young, the corm is completely covered by the leaf's petiole base, which itself is surrounded by a "corm scale" or cataphyll.
There is only one leaf, the petiole of which is tubular and squarish in cross-section, with each corner bearing a translucent ridge, or keel. The petiole arises from within the cataphyll. The pale green leaf's blade is somewhat fleshy, ascends upward, has 3 veins and grows up to 68 mm × 37 mm (2+1⁄2 in × 1+1⁄2 in). The blade's base varies from rounded to having 2 short, backward directed lobes.
The single corymb-type inflorescence, with the first flowers to open appearing at the edges, has a peduncle up to 15 cm (6 in) long.
Flowers are small for the genus, becoming only about 6.5 mm (1⁄4 in) across, with the flower's "faces" directed upward. The sepals are fused for about ¼ of their length, curved egg-shape, and up to about 3.3 mm (1⁄8 in) long. Slender petals curve backwards and are up to 2.4 mm (3⁄32 in) long. The lip, or labellum, has no stalk, is more or less arrowhead-shaped , and has at its base two conspicuous, backward-directed "ears", or "basal auricles", which in their natural position approach each other and often overlap behind the column (fused male and female parts). Between the ears' bases there are 2 "pollinaria", each composed of 2 fused pollinia and a shiny, wet-looking, sticky "apical droplet", called a "viscidium", which glues the pollinia to visiting pollinators.
The capsular-type fruits are ellipsoid, up to 9 mm × 4 mm (3⁄8 in × 3⁄16 in) in size, and are held on a very slender pedicel up to 7 mm (1⁄4 in) long.


== Distribution ==
Malaxis magniauriculata is endemic just to the three Mexican states of Hidalgo, Puebla and Oaxaca.


== Habitat ==
Malaxis magnia

articles.title: Tân Định Market
articles.text:
Tân Định Market

Tân Định Market is a market in Tân Định, Central Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. This is one of the markets with the longest history in the city.


== Location ==
Tân Định Market is located in a city block surrounded by four roads: Hai Bà Trưng, Nguyễn Hữu Cầu, Mã Lộ, Nguyễn Văn Nghĩa. The main entrance is located at its main address is 314–336 Hai Bà Trưng Street, Tân Định, Ho Chi Minh City. 


== History ==
Initially, the market was named Phú Hòa Market (Vietnamese: Chợ Phú Hòa), As it was located within the territory of the former Phú Hòa village at that time. Later, the authorities incorporated the villages of Tân Định, Phú Hòa, and Nam Chơn from Gia Định province into the administrative boundaries of the Ville de Saigon, designating the area as Tân Định quartier (hộ; an administration existed during French Indochina); consequently, Phú Hòa Market was renamed Tân Định Market.
In 1926, the Council of Ville de Saigon has approved the construction of a new market at a cost of 110,000 piastre. The new Tân Định Market was designed and constructed by the French contractor Société Indochinoise d'Études et de Constructions (SIDEC). According to Les Annales Coloniales, the inauguration ceremony for the market was held on July 26, 1927, and was attended by top-ranking officials of the time, including the Governor of Cochinchina, the President of the Colonial Council, and the Mayor of Saigon.
Tân Định Market at that time was considered a market for the wealthy because the prices were usually higher than other markets. The goods were fresh, high-quality vegetables and meat, produced from Gia Định province. This place is also considered the largest and most affordable hub for trading fabric scraps in Saigon.
The front of the market stands out with its French-style architecture, featuring three bell towers—one in the center and two shorter on either side. During the 1950s and 1960s, there were parking areas for cars on both flanks of the market, while behind is the horse-drawn carriage stand (now is Mã Lộ Road, lit. 'Horse-drawn carriage Road').

=== Fabric & clothes shopping, tailoring ===
The clothing section sells casual garments for men, women and children. Most products are designed for everyday use rather than luxury shopping Shirts and T-shirts, Trousers and shorts, Dresses and skirts, Blouses, Pajamas and homewear, Children’s clothing, Socks, belts and ties, Handbags, purses and backpacks. articles.title: Richard van Kempen
articles.text:
Richard van Kempen

Richard van Kempen (born 23 August 1964) is a Dutch former marathon speed skater. He won the overall classification of the Royal Dutch Skating Federation (Koninklijke Nederlandsche Schaatsenrijders Bond; KNSB) Cup four times (1986, 1987, 1988, and 1992). He triumphed twice at the unofficial World Championships in Kuopio, Finland (1990 and 1991), won the Jaap Eden Trophy three times (1986, 1988, and 1990), secured two national titles, the Dutch championship on artificial ice (1991) and the Open Dutch championship on natural ice (1996), and won the Heineken Six-Day race twice (1986 and 1987).


== Career ==


=== Early years ===
When he was nine years old, Van Kempen moved with his parents to the village of De Hoef in the province of Utrecht. It was in the polder landscape surrounding his family home that he learnt to ice skate. During his youth, he also participated in athletics and cycling, before giving himself over wholly to ice skating from the age of seventeen. He joined the regional squad as a long-track speed skater, but he felt most at home in marathon skating. As a B-category skater, he scored one victory after another, and in 1984 he made the move up to the A-category.


=== Period of success ===
In the years after 1985, Van Kempen was by far the most successful athlete in marathon speed skating. His nickname was "Poeske" ("Little Cat"), a reference to his feline skating style and hunched back. He won the KNSB Cup in 1986, 1987, 1988, and 1992, and secured 47 marathon victories on artificial ice. All together, he achieved 112 victories over both artificial and natural ice. He also won the Heineken Six-Day race twice. In 1991, Van Kempen became the national marathon champion on artificial ice, and in 1996, he won the Open Dutch Marathon Championship on natural ice, held in Austria on the Plansee, near Reutte.
Between 1987 and 1990, Van Kempen competed four times in the Dutch national single-distance championships in the 10,000-metre event. On each occasion, he finished near the back of the field. His personal best for this long-distance event, set in December 1987 at the Thialf arena in Heerenveen, was 14:40.67.
Van Kempen achieved his victories mainly on artificial ice. He participated in only one edition of the Elfstedentocht (the thirteenth, in 1985), finishing in 92nd place. He also took part seven times in the Alternative Elfstedentocht in Finland. His last appearance there, on 2 March 1996, resulted in his greatest victory

articles.title: 2026 Shabwah missile attack
articles.text:
2026 Shabwah missile attack

On 19 October 2026, a training center within a military camp in Shabwah Governorate controlled by the internationally recognized government of Yemen was struck by Houthi missiles. The attacks killed 73 soldiers and injured over 200, most of them young recruits.


== Background ==
The attack occurred in the government-controlled Shabwah Governorate amidst the resumption of the Yemeni civil war after a four-year lull in fighting. The target of the attack was the al-Alam camp in Jardan district and, north of the provincial capital Ataq. Previously operated by a United Arab Emirates-aligned militia prior to their withdrawal from Yemen, the camp is strategically valuable to the government for operating supply lines to other areas, including Marib Governorate. Just prior to the attack, the Houthis blocked a road connecting Shabwah to the Houthi-controlled al-Bayda Governorate.


== Attack ==
On 19 October 2026, the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, a facility within the al-Alam camp, was struck by three ballistic missiles. The targeted site was hosting a training drill for recruits joining Rapid Intervention, a newly-formed group involved in local defense. A government spokesperson said it was not involved in the current fighting and was providing "training and qualification programmes" for local forces in Shabwah.
The missile impacts occurred as the recruits were lining up to commence a training drill. Footage at the site published on social media and verified by The New York Times displayed bodies strewn across paved ground. The attacks killed 73 soldiers and wounded over 200 according to the government, the majority of them young recruits. It was the deadliest single incident since the resumption of the civil war. A Houthi spokesperson claimed they targeted a Saudi-led coalition military site ran by Saudi officers, and that it inflicted casualties on them. He did not provide any evidence in the statement.


== Aftermath ==
The victims were transported for treatment in Ataq, where hospitals urged locals to donate blood. They were visited by Shabwah governor Awad bin al-Wazir. Deputy governor Fahad al-Khalifi said those with critical injuries were transferred to Aden and Mukalla, Hadhramaut, to lighten the strain on local hospitals.
Presidential Leadership Council head Rashad al-Alimi said the Houthis resorted a terrorist attack as "their Iranian-backed sabotage plots falter", vowing a response. The same day he spoke to Uni

articles.title: Fairvest
articles.text:
Fairvest

Fairvest is a South African real estate investment trust (REIT), headquartered in Cape Town. Founded in 1998, the company is listed on both the JSE and A2X.
As of 2025, Fairvest has a portfolio of 130 properties, including retail, commercial, and industrial real estate. Its investment assets span a gross leasable area (GLA) of over 1.05 million m², and are worth a combined R13.4 billion.


== History ==
Fairvest was incorporated on 17 March 1998 as Basfour 429 Pty Limited.
In December 2001, Basfour was converted to a public company and renamed Fairvest Property Holdings. The company developed a strategy focused on retail properties in non-metropolitan areas, particularly convenience, community, and regional shopping centers serving lower-income consumers.
In 2013, Fairvest expanded this strategy through acquisitions including Nyanga Junction in Cape Town and Matsulu Centre in Mpumalanga.
That same year, Fairvest received approval from the JSE to become a real estate investment trust (REIT).
In January 2014, it completed the acquisition of a portfolio of four retail properties from Vukile Property Fund, issuing R235 million of new equity as part of the transaction. Vukile subsequently became a significant shareholder in Fairvest.
In 2019, Fairvest entered into discussions with Safari Investments regarding a potential merger. Safari subsequently became the subject of a competing offer from Community Property Company, and Fairvest's proposed transaction did not proceed.
In 2021, Fairvest and Arrowhead Properties announced plans to merge. The proposed transaction would create a larger JSE-listed REIT with a portfolio spanning retail, office, and industrial properties.
The merger was implemented on in January 2022. Arrowhead was the legal acquiring entity and was subsequently renamed Fairvest Limited, while the former Fairvest Property Holdings business was incorporated into the enlarged group. The combined portfolio was valued at approximately R12.1 billion, and comprised 141 properties across South Africa.
Following the merger, Fairvest began restructuring the enlarged portfolio around a more focused retail strategy. It sought to dispose of non-core office and industrial properties, reduce vacancies, and concentrate investment on convenience-oriented retail properties in underserved communities.

articles.title: Jalen Bell
articles.text:
Jalen Bell

Jalen Bell (born November 1, 2001) is an American professional football defensive lineman for the Toronto Argonauts of the Canadian Football League (CFL). He played college football for the Mississippi Valley State Delta Devils, Tennessee State Tigers and Memphis Tigers.


== Early life ==
Bell was born on November 1, 2001. He attended Martin Luther King Jr. Senior High School in Detroit, Michigan. Bell committed to play college football at University of Akron but flipped to Mississippi Valley State University after a coaching change.


== College career ==
Bell played college football for the Mississippi Valley State Delta Devils from 2019 to 2022, Tennessee State Tigers from 2023 to 2024 and Memphis Tigers in 2025. In 30 games at Mississippi Valley State, he had 113 tackles, including 26.5 for loss, 12 sacks, forced forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries. 
On January 16, 2023, Bell transferred to Tennessee State University. In his first season, he suffered an injury in the opener and missed the rest of the year. In 2024, Bell played in four games, recording 24 tackles, with seven for loss and 2.5 sacks.
Bell transferred again to University of Memphis for the 2025 season where he played in all 13 games with 12 starts. He had 36 tackles, including 5.5 for loss, two sacks and one interception. 


== Professional career ==
After not being selected in the 2026 NFL draft, Toomer signed with the Toronto Argonauts of the Canadian Football League (CFL). He made his CFL debut in the opener against the Montreal Alouettes but made his first tackle the following week against the Ottawa Redblacks. On July 21, Bell was signed to the practice roster. On August 28, he was elevated to the active roster against the Saskatchewan Roughriders and had two tackles. Bell reverted to the practice roster the following week. On October 15, he was promoted to the active roster. Against the 0–16 Redblacks, Bell rushed for a two-point conversion for the go-ahead score but the Argonauts ended up losing, 39–40.

articles.title: Corryocactus volcanicus
articles.text:
Corryocactus volcanicus

Corryocactus volcanicus is a species of succulent flowering plant in the genus Corryocactus, within the family Cactaceae. It is endemic to the department of Arequipa in southern Peru. 


== Description ==
Corryocactus volcanicus is a species of large, shrubby cactus that may also develop a columnar growth form. It can grow to 3 m in height. It branches from the base and forms erect stems measuring 10-12 cm in diameter. The epidermis is light green in color. 
The stems have 7-10 ribs, which are raised by 2.2-2.8 cm. The circular areoles, which measure 0.9-1.9 cm in diameter and are separated by 2.1-3 cm, are found on top of the ribs. The older areoles have a grayish felt-like covering, while the younger areoles have a black felt-like covering with a small brown tuft pointing towards the rib, as well as small, yellow-green, deltoid scales.

This species has 12-17 spines per areole, although the basal areoles of the trunk may produce up to 50. The central and radial spines are practically indistinguishable. Their surfaces are smooth, and they are generally straight, although they occasionally may appear slightly curved. They reach 0.6-10.5 cm in length. The new spines are yellow, with a yellowish base and a brownish apex throughout development, even as the rest of the spine turns gray with age.
The flowers open during the day, and are radially symmetrical and funnel-shaped. They often develop in a subapical position and are an almost-white shade of light yellow in color. They grow to 7.2-7.7 in length and 5-5.3 in diameter when open. The pericarpel is greenish and measures 1.6-2.4 cm in length and 2.1-2.7 cm in diameter. They are covered in dark green deltoid scales measuring 0.7-2.9 mm in length. On these are rounded areoles measuring 1.6-2.4 mm in diameter, with a brownish-black felt-like covering and a few off-white curly trichomes. Each areole has 3 straight spines that are yellowish and 3-4 mm in length.
The ovary is off-white in color and measures 9-10 mm in width. The style is off-white, cylindrical, glabrous, short, and thick, measuring 1.3-1.4 cm in length and 4-5 mm in diameter. The stigma has 20-24 yellowish lobes, which measure 1-1.3 cm in length and are papillose on the surface. The nectary is situated at the base of the style. The stamens are numerous and grow from near the base of the style. Their filaments are glabrous and light yellow in color, growing to 0.9-1.4 cm in length. The anthers are yellowish, basifixed, and

articles.title: Margarette Ball Dickson
articles.text:
Margarette Ball Dickson

Margarette Ball Dickson (June 4, 1879 - July 21, 1963) was an American poet and educator who served as the first poet laureate for the state of Minnesota.


== Early life ==
Margarette Adell Ball was born in Little Rock, Iowa to Leroy Augustus Ball and Mary Adell Mansfield. She graduated Rock Rapids High School, and earned her B.A. from Iowa State Teachers College in 1925 and M.A. at the University of South Dakota in 1926. She studied at the University of Iowa, earning a Ph.D. She headed the English department at Valparaiso University in Indiana, taught creative writing at California State Teacher's College in Chico, and was a correspondence course instructor for the Stapes School of Writing. She married George Robert Dickson on June 1, 1904, who worked for the Chicago and North Western Railway. The couple had two sons and one daughter.  She remarried fellow poet John Allison Haining in 1930. She remarried to Andrew Christian Jensen on June 5, 1945, but retained Margarette Ball Dickson as her pen name. She was also a member of the Daughters of the American Revolution, the Order of the Eastern Star, the American Association of University Women, and General Federation of Women's Clubs.


== Poetry ==
Dickson was appointed state poet laureate by Minnesota Governor Floyd B. Olson on April 25, 1934. By 1936 she had been published in 53 anthologies. She co-founded the Minnesota Poetry League and was its second president, and was president of the Minnesota Poetry Society. She was national vice president of the League of American Pen Women and president of the American Poetry Circle. She was also member of the National Country Bard Association, American Lit Association, and American Literary League. 
Dickson was a founder of the Midwest Federation of Chaparral Poets, serving as its regional director from 1939 to 1951, and national director until her death in 1963. She also helped organize the East Coast Canadian Chaparral Poets and European Chaparral Poets.

articles.title: Roger S. Wieck
articles.text:
Roger S. Wieck

Roger S. Wieck (January 30, 1952 – March 13, 2026) was an American art historian, curator, author, and collector. He served as head of the Morgan Library and Museum's Department of Medieval and Renaissance Manuscripts from 2015 through 2025. 


== Early life and education ==
Wieck was born January 30, 1952. He was educated at the University of Cincinnati, where he received a masters degree in art history and did further graduate work at the Institute of Fine Arts of New York University. As a graduate student, he did an internship at the Morgan Library and his initial stay there lasted two years.


== Career ==
After appointments at Baltimore's Walters Art Museum and the Houghton Library of Harvard University, he returned to the Morgan Library in 1989. In 2015, he was appointed Melvin R. Seiden Curator and Department Head of Medieval and Renaissance Manuscripts.
Wieck retired from the Morgan Library effective January 1, 2026 and died of cancer March 13, 2026.


== Books ==
Wieck was the author or editor of a number of books including

——— (1988). Time sanctified: the Book of hours in medieval art and life (1st ed.). New York: G. Braziller in association with the Walters Art Gallery, Baltimore. ISBN 0807611891.
Kren, Thomas; ——— (1990). The Visions of Tondal from the library of Margaret of York. Malibu, Calif: J. Paul Getty Museum. ISBN 0-89236-169-7.
with William M. Voelkle, The Bernard H. Breslauer Collection of Manuscript Illuminations (1992)
Mathews, Thomas F.; ———, eds. (1994). Treasures in Heaven: Armenian illuminated manuscripts. New York : Princeton, N.J: Pierpont Morgan Library ; Distributed by Princeton University Press. ISBN 978-0691037516.
Painted Prayers: The Book of Hours in Medieval and Renaissance Art (1997)
The Prayer Book of Anne de Bretagne (1999)
The Prayer Book of Claude de France (2010)


== Personal Life ==
Raised Catholic, Wieck stated that he "became a nonbeliever gradually when [he] was in [his] 20s" and did not believe in God.
Wieck was married to Jean-François Vilain (1942 – 2025) and they lived in New York City's Kips Bay neighborhood. Property from their personal art collection was sold at auction in 2026 by Stair Galleries to benefit the Morgan Library.

articles.title: Emily Nahon
articles.text:
Emily Nahon

Emily Julia Frederica Nahon (born 17 May 2007) is a professional footballer who plays as a centre-back for the NCAA Division I club Little Rock Trojans. Born in the Netherlands, she plays for the Indonesia national team.


== Early life ==
Nahon was born in Oegstgeest, Netherlands, on 17 May 2007. She is of Indonesian descent through her father, Vincent Rudolf Nahon. Her paternal grandmother, Julie Margot Rancuret, was born in Bogor, West Java, on 29 April 1949.


== Club career ==


=== ADO Den Haag ===
Nahon began playing football in the youth system of ADO Den Haag at the age of 14. She initially played for the club's under-16 team between 2021 and 2023 before progressing to its under-19 side in the 2023–24 season. She also made appearances for the club's senior team.


=== Little Rock Trojans ===
In 2025, Nahon joined the Little Rock Trojans women's soccer programme at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock in the United States. She competed in NCAA Division I women's soccer during the 2025 season.
She remained on the Little Rock Trojans roster for the 2026 season, listed as a sophomore defender wearing number 8.


== International career ==
Nahon was called up to the Indonesia national team in preparation for the 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup qualification. She made her senior international debut against the Kyrgyztan, helping Indonesia secure a 1–0 victory.
On 10 June 2025, Nahon obtained Indonesian citizenship alongside fellow Dutch-born footballers Felicia de Zeeuw, Iris de Rouw and Isa Warps. The four players were naturalised to strengthen Indonesia's women's national team for upcoming international competitions.
Nahon represented Indonesia at the 2025 SEA Games women's football tournament, where Indonesia finished in fourth place.
In July 2026, Nahon was part of the Indonesian squad that won the 2026 AFF Women's Cup. She scored in Indonesia's 2–0 group-stage victory over Timor-Leste on 10 July 2026.
She also scored in the final against the Laos on 22 July 2026, when Indonesia won 5–0 to secure the title. Nahon scored Indonesia's fifth goal in the match, contributing to the team's championship victory.


== Personal life ==
Nahon is the daughter of Vincent Rudolf Nahon and Martine Alexandra Fluitsma. Her Indonesian ancestry comes from her paternal grandmother, who was born in Bogor, Indonesia.
While playing for Little Rock, Nahon pursued studies in business and marketing at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock.

articles.title: Kitsanga massacre
articles.text:
Kitsanga massacre

Between November 12 and 13, 2023, militants from the Islamic State – Central Africa Province (ISCAP), also called the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), killed 42 people in the village of Kitsanga, Watalinga Chiefdom, Beni Territory, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.


== Background ==
The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) was founded in Uganda in the 1990s, gaining prominence as an Islamist rebel group and conducting deadly attacks on civilians in the early 2010s. The group pledged bay'ah to the Islamic State in 2019 and began carrying out its first attacks under the ISCAP moniker months later. Beginning in 2021, the ADF carried out dozens of deadly massacres against villages in North Kivu, attacking villagers along ethnic and religious lines.
In late 2023, the ADF carried out a series of massacres in North Kivu, beginning with the killing of dozens of civilians in Oicha in October 2023. This was partially instigated by the start of phase 4 of Operation Shujaa, a joint Ugandan-Congolese anti-ISCAP operation in North Kivu.


== Massacre ==
At about 11:30pm on November 12, ISCAP militants ended the village of Kitsanga, close to the Ugandan-Congolese border, going door-to-door and massacreing civilians. Several civilians were tied up with ropes before being executed. The ISCAP militants had entered Kitsanga from Ituri Province to the north, where they were losing territory as a result of Operation Shujaa. The fighters were led by a white man named Guraba. Another source in the Congolese army said that the fighters were from Beni, and led by a man named Sebangala or Mzee Mea. Shops in the Kitsanga market were looted, with the fighters seeking to resupply on pharmaceuticals.
Although no military presence was reported in the village during the massacre, a Congolese army captain in Kitsanga was killed by ISCAP and the Congolese army said six ISCAP militants were killed that night. Many civilians who fled tried to cross the Lamia river, with several drowning. One group of civilians was kidnapped and forced to loot for ISCAP before being executed; another group was repotedly freed by the Congolese army. Initial reports by Congolese media said that 19 civilians were killed, excluding two children who drowned crossing the Lamia. Reuters, citing humanitarian sources, said that 33 people were killed in the massacre. By November 17, Actualite.cd reported that 42 people had been killed, including 12 women, and 5,000 people were displaced to Buto

articles.title: Too Cute to Be Lonely
articles.text:
Too Cute to Be Lonely

"Too Cute to Be Lonely" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter Holly Humberstone. It was released by Polydor Records on 30 September 2026 as a single from the deluxe edition of her second studio album, Cruel World (2026). Humberstone wrote the track with long-term collaborators Rob Milton and Benjamin Francis Leftwich, as well as JT Daly.
An alt synth-pop song, the lyrical content involves Humberstone wanting to find a romantic and physical connection. Although thematically connecting to Cruel World, it was seen as a lyrical departure from the contents of the original album, instead seen as a more positive outlook on relationships. It was accompanied by a music video directed by Silken Weinberg.


== Background and release ==
Humberstone released "Die Happy" in November 2025 as the lead single from her second studio album, Cruel World (2026). It was followed by "To Love Somebody", "Cruel World" and "Beauty Pageant", with the album eventually released on 10 April 2026. In June, a reimagined version of four songs from the album was released as an extended play, It's a Real Cruel World.
Following the release of Cruel World, Humberstone embarked on various tours and festival appearances, including sets at Reading and Leeds, Summer Sonic, Mad Cool, All Things Go and Governors Ball, as well as a headline concert tour across North America and supporting the War on Drugs at British Summer Time. Her set at Reading and Leeds included the first live performances of "Too Cute to Be Lonely" prior to its release. On 30 September, she announced a deluxe edition of Cruel World, titled Cruel World... So It Ends, releasing "Too Cute to Be Lonely" as a single from the project.


== Composition and lyrics ==
Humberstone co-wrote "Too Cute to Be Lonely" with long-term collaborators Rob Milton and Benjamin Francis Leftwich, as well as JT Daly. Milton also handled the production of the track. It has been described as an alt pop and synth-pop song with subtle nods to disco and opera. Inspired by ABBA, Madonna and Robyn, the song was billed as having a "more dancefloor-oriented sound" to Humberstone's typical releases. Speaking about the song and its accompanying deluxe tracks, Humberstone explained that it was a continuation of the original album's story. She explained: "To me the fairytale doesn't end, it just turns a page to a new chapter. Cruel World was a journey of self discovery and finding my confidence in my voice, the songs within So It En

articles.title: Copiapoa megarhiza
articles.text:
Copiapoa megarhiza

Copiapoa megarhiza is a species of succulent flowering plant in the genus Copiapoa, within the family Cactaceae. It is endemic to the Atacama Desert in northern Chile.


== Description ==
Copiapoa megarhiza is a very spiny species of cactus with a solitary or somewhat-branched stem. Its growth form is globose to somewhat elongated, and it is gray-green in color. It measures 10-25 cm in length and 7-10 cm in diameter. Its apex is covered in gray woolly trichomes, and its taproot is large and tuberous. 

This species has 13-17 ribs which are divided into tubercles and slightly widened around the areoles. The areoles are rounded to oval in shape and measure 0.4-0.7 cm in diameter. These have thick spines that are yellow to black in color but turn gray with age. Among these, there are up to 4 especially thick central spines which range from straight to curved and measure up to 4 cm in length. There are also 8-10 somewhat-curved radial spines, which measure up to 3 cm in length.

The flowers are funnel-shaped and yellow in color, measuring up to 3 cm in length. The fruits are olive green in color and egg-shaped, measuring up to 1.5 cm in diameter. They have many wide, fleshy scales near their margins, and some on their lower parts. Inside, the seeds are black and shiny.


== Distribution and habitat ==
Copiapoa megarhiza is native to the Atacama Desert in northern  Chile, where it is found in desert or dry scrubland biomes at altitudes of 0 to 800 m above sea level. It grows in alluvial soils and on rocky, north-facing slopes.


== Taxonomy ==
Copiapoa megarhiza was described by the American botanists Nathaniel Lord Britton and Joseph Nelson Rose, who published this name in their book The Cactaceae; descriptions and illustrations of plants of the cactus family 3: 89 in 1922.

Etymology
Copiapoa: the genus name references the Chilean province of Copiapó in the Atacama Desert, to which most of the species in this genus are native.
megarhiza: the specific epithet is derived from the Greek words mega (meaning "large") and rhiza (meaning "root"), in reference to this species' large taproot.


== Conservation status ==
On the IUCN Red List, Copiapoa megarhiza is classified as being Endangered (EN).

articles.title: Vahe R. Engibaryan
articles.text:
Vahe R. Engibaryan

Vahe Engibaryan (born 1 June 1976) is an Armenian entrepreneur and former diplomat. He founded PrimeConcept, a private membership club, and is a co-founder of Armenian Assembly, where he has served as chairman of the presidium of the public council. Since 2017, he has served as chairman of the Board of the public organisation "Armenian Assembly".


== Early and personal life ==
Engibaryan was born in Yerevan and graduated from the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO). His father, Robert Engibaryan, is a legal scholar and MGIMO professor who received the title of Honoured Scientist of the Russian Federation.
His 2000 dissertation for the Candidate of Legal Sciences degree was titled Federalism in the Modern World: Legal Status and Key Features.
Vahe Engibaryan graduated from MGIMO and received a Candidate of Legal Sciences degree in 2000. His dissertation was titled Federalism in the Modern World: Legal Status and Key Features.


== Diplomatic career ==
Engibaryan joined the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in 1996, working in its Department of North America. He later served as vice-consul in New York. The US Department of State's directory of foreign consular officers lists him as “Vage R. Yengibaryan”, with a recognition date of 10 December 2001. His biography in the Hayazg Foundation's encyclopedia also records subsequent service as a consul in New York and an adviser to the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.


== Business ==
Engibaryan founded PrimeConcept, a private membership club. 
In June 2009, Vedomosti reported that Spain's Zed Group had bought Engibaryan's stake in Temafon, a mobile content aggregator working with VimpelCom.
He was also a shareholder in RURU, a mobile payment service whose other shareholders included Alfa-Bank and VimpelCom. VimpelCom acquired full ownership of the business in 2019.
His business interests also include construction and investment, according to Armenian Assembly.  


== Exhibitions with Gagosian ==
PrimeConcept collaborated with Gagosian on two exhibitions in Moscow. According to a 2007 NEWSru.com report, Ulyana Tseitlina credited Engibaryan with persuading Larry Gagosian to visit Russia.

The first exhibition, Insight?, ran from 19 to 28 October 2007 at Barvikha Luxury Village. Gagosian's first exhibition in the city, it included works by Cy Twombly, Richard Serra and Ed Ruscha.
The second, For What You Are About to Receive, was held at the former Red October chocolate

articles.title: Romodan Osman Awliya
articles.text:
Romodan Osman Awliya

Romodan Osman Awliya (also spelled Ramadan Osman Awliya, Romedan Osman Aweliay or Romodan Osman Awelyay) is an Eritrean military officer with the rank of major general in the Eritrean Defence Forces (EDF). He has served as Commissioner of Sports, as Governor (administrator) of the Central Region, and as Commander of the EDF's Central Command. As of September 2026, he was Commander of the Eritrean Defence Forces Training Center.


== Early life ==
Awliya was born in Hirgigo, a town near Massawa in what is now the Northern Red Sea Region of Eritrea.


== Career ==


=== Commissioner of Sports ===
Awliya succeeded Alamin Siraj, a veteran of the armed struggle, as head of Eritrea's sports commission. He was later succeeded in the post by former ambassador to Italy Zemede Tekle Woldetatios, who was reported as Commissioner of Sports in 2015.


=== Governor of the Central Region ===
After leaving the sports commission, Awliya became administrator of the Central Region (Zoba Maekel), which includes the capital, Asmara. Eritrean state media referred to him as Governor of the Central Region in October 2018, when he attended a workshop on strengthening community magistrates, and in June 2019, when he attended a Martyrs' Day cultural event in the region.


=== Central Command and military delegations ===
By July 2020, Awliya was Commander of the EDF's Central Command. In that capacity he was part of a high-level EDF delegation led by Chief of Staff General Filipos Woldeyohannes that visited Sudan on 20–21 July 2020, delivering a message from President Isaias Afwerki to Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, chairman of the Transitional Sovereignty Council. The delegation also held talks with Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo and Sudanese military leaders on defence and security cooperation.
In April 2023, he was a member of a senior Eritrean military delegation, led by Brigadier General Abraha Kasa, head of Eritrea's National Security Agency, that made an official visit to Ethiopia at the invitation of the Ethiopian National Defense Force. The delegation visited Asosa and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam in the Benishangul-Gumuz Region.


=== EDF Training Center ===
On 26 September 2026, as Commander of the Eritrean Defence Forces Training Center, Awliya inaugurated a new dam in the Adi-Hawosha administrative area of the Gala-Nefhi sub-zone of the Central Region. The dam was built jointly by residents, the government and an EDF unit, at a reported cost of about 11 mill

articles.title: Penguin Colony
articles.text:
Penguin Colony

Penguin Colony is a 2026 walking simulator video game developed by Origame Digital and published by Fellow Traveller Games, featuring the voice of Lenval Brown. The game is an anti-colonial retelling of At the Mountains of Madness, and places the player as a penguin, who is free to explore and observe the remains of a doomed Nazi scientific expedition to Antarctica. The game draws extensively on its developers' own Māori culture. It received generally positive reviews upon release, with critics praising its unusual perspective and its cultural/political critique, but also noting its short runtime, awkward controls and sparse, sometimes monotonous presentation. 


== Gameplay and plot ==
Penguin Colony places the player in control of a penguin in an Antarctic setting inspired by At the Mountains of Madness, and tasks them with exploring the surrounding area, instructing the player to "follow the wind" to progress. The game incorporates some puzzle and platformer elements, as well as penguin-centric belly-sliding and swimming mechanics, and the ability to switch between control of different penguins, but the game has been described as a walking simulator overall.
While the player controls a penguin, the game's story is told through voice-over narration, primarily from Howard Blakely, an English scientist accompanying a Nazi German expedition to the Antarctic wilderness (voiced by Lenval Brown of Disco Elysium fame). By the time of the player's arrival, the expedition has already fallen into disarray, with most of its members dead, mutilated, or consumed by madness. Interspersed between the penguin-exploration components, cutscenes highlight the struggles of a group of Māori warriors, who are revealed to be racing to contain and defeat the Nazis and their discoveries. In a final series of cutscenes at the end of the game, the Māori warriors find Howard in the throes of delusions of grandeur, kill him, and then reckon with the destruction already unleashed and the future, similar evils to come.
Towards the end of the game, gameplay sequences are increasingly interrupted by fourth-wall breaking images of Māori art and music, and mixed-media footage denouncing the genocides committed by the British Empire, as well as the general silence of the video games industry in response to the Gaza genocide.

articles.title: Bryan Lovell
articles.text:
Bryan Lovell

Julian Patrick Bryan Lovell OBE (10 February 1942 – 20 September 2024) was a geologist who spent much of his working life with BP. After retirement he was elected President of the Geological Society of London. He promoted the recognition of man-made climate change and was a prominent advocate for carbon capture and storage.


== Early life and education ==
Lovell was born on 10 February 1942 in Bath, England, he was the second of five children, their father was the astronomer Sir Bernard Lovell who was the first director of Jodrell Bank Observatory. He grew up in Swettenham, Cheshire, was educated at King's School, Macclesfield and went on to study geology at New College, Oxford, graduating with a BA in 1963. He then studied the sandstones of the Carboniferous Bude Formation, North Cornwall under the supervision of Harold Reading and in 1964 he was awarded an MSc by Oxford for that work. He carried out research under the supervision of Raymond Siever at Harvard University, graduating in 1968 with a PhD on the "Eocene Tyee Formation of the Oregon Coast Range".


== Scotland ==
After graduating from Harvard he spent ten years as a lecturer in the Department of Geology at the  University of Edinburgh (1970-1981). Whilst at Edinburgh he worked on sandstones which had been deposited in deep-water by turbidites (like the sediments he had studied in Cornwall and Oregon) and by contourites. His work on developing criteria for distinguishing between sediments deposited by these different mechanisms attracted the attention of people involved in hydrocarbon exploration and in 1979 he set up the consultancy firm 'Petrological Services Edinburgh Ltd' to advise oil industry clients.
During his time in Scotland he became active in politics with the Scottish Liberal Party and in 1978 he became their energy spokesman. He unsuccessfully stood as the Liberal's Parliamentary candidate for Edinburgh South in the General Election of May 1979, being beaten to third place by Michael Ancram and Gordon Brown.


== Oil industry ==
Lovell joined BP as a geologist in 1981 and over the next fifteen years he was the company's Chief Sedimentologist, Exploration Manager for Ireland and later for the Middle East, and finally the overall Head of Recruitment at BP Exploration. 
Whilst based in Dublin he was awarded an OBE in the Diplomatic Service and Overseas List of the 1989 Birthday Honours for 'Services to British Commercial interests and to Anglo-Irish relations'.

articles.title: Carlos Aured
articles.text:
Carlos Aured

Carlos Aured Alonso (22 January 1937 – 3 February 2008) was a Spanish film director and screenwriter associated with the Spanish horror cinema of the 1970s, commonly known as fantaterror. He is particularly known for his collaborations with actor and screenwriter Paul Naschy, including Horror Rises from the Tomb (1973), El Retorno de Walpurgis (1973), Blue Eyes of the Broken Doll (1974) and The Mummy's Revenge. Following the decline of Spain's horror film cycle, Aured increasingly worked in erotic cinema during the country's transition to democracy.


== Career ==


=== Early work and horror films ===
Aured was born in Los Alcázares, in the province of Murcia. He initially pursued studies in civil engineering before entering the Spanish film industry, where he began in junior production positions and subsequently became an assistant director.
He worked with filmmakers including Luis García Berlanga on ¡Vivan los novios! (1970), Rafael Moreno Alba on Las melancólicas (1971), and León Klimovsky on several productions, including La Noche de Walpurgis (1971), starring Paul Naschy. Aured later acknowledged Klimovsky as an important influence on his development as a filmmaker.
Aured made his directorial debut with El espanto surge de la tumba (Horror Rises from the Tomb), a supernatural horror film starring Naschy. Produced in 1972 and commonly dated to 1973 in international filmographies, the film initiated a series of collaborations between the two filmmakers.
The collaboration with Naschy continued with El retorno de Walpurgis (Curse of the Devil, 1973), featuring Naschy's recurring werewolf character Waldemar Daninsky, and La venganza de la momia (The Mummy's Revenge, 1973). Their work together also included Los ojos azules de la muñeca rota (Blue Eyes of the Broken Doll), a horror thriller starring Naschy alongside Diana Lorys and Maria Perschy. The films formed part of the commercially oriented Spanish horror cycle that attracted international audiences during the 1970s.
Aured also directed crime and suspense films without Naschy, including Los fríos senderos del crimen (1974) and La noche de la furia (1974). His professional relationship with Naschy ended in the mid-1970s following a disagreement surrounding the production of the latter film. The two later reconciled.

articles.title: Consolea testudinis-crus
articles.text:
Consolea testudinis-crus

Consolea testudinis-crus, commonly known in the Dominican Republic as alpargata, is a species of succulent flowering plant in the genus Consolea, within the family Cactaceae. It is endemic to the island of Hispaniola.


== Description ==
Consolea testudinis-crus is a species of cactus with a treelike growth form and a highly-branched crown. It may grow to 3-4 m in height. It forms an erect, non-articulated trunk, which is very spiny and grows to more than 2 m in height. It is cylindrical in cross-section and woody inside, and is covered in thick white and blackish wool. From the trunk grow flattened, segmented branches that grow up to 30 cm in length and 15 cm in width. Their surfaces are covered in small protuberances which form a reticulate pattern, giving the branches a rough appearance.
On the stems are areoles with glochids and short bristly spines; these are often lost with age.
The flowers are bright yellow in color, and may turn reddish over time. They open during the day and have curved bracts. The flowers develop on the upper parts of the uppermost stems. They measure up to 5 cm in length and 2.5 cm in diameter. In the center of the flower, there are many yellow stamens with anthers of the same color.
The fruits are egg-shaped with small spines that are green at first and turn yellowish with age. They have a bitter flavor and contain rough seeds. Although this species is very similar to Consolea moniliformis, it does not fruit as prolifically, and the fruits do not grow roots when they fall to the ground.


== Distribution and habitat ==
This species is native to the lowland dry forests of Hispaniola.
It is often found together with Consolea moniliformis. The flowers and fruits of both species provide an important food source for the rhinoceros and Ricord's iguanas that are endemic to the island (the latter of which is only found in the southern part of the island).


== Taxonomy ==
Consolea testudinis-crus was first described as Opuntia testudinis-crus, a name published in 1904 by the French botanist Frédéric Albert Constantin Weber in the scientific journal Bulletin du Muséum d'Histoire Naturelle 10: 389.
Later, the British botanists Roy Mottram and Paul Hoxey transferred the species to the genus Consolea, renaming it Consolea testudinis-crus. They registered these changes in the scientific journal Cactician 13: 73, published in 2020.

Etymology
Consolea: the genus name honors the Italian botanist Michelangelo Console

articles.title: Sharky (internet personality)
articles.text:
Sharky (internet personality)

Sharmarke Mohamud (born 31 December 1995), better known as Sharky, is a Dutch-British social media personality. After launching his YouTube account in 2015, with videos consisting mainly of vlog, football and gaming videos, he joined the YouTube group the Beta Squad alongside five other creators on the platform, amassing over 12 million subscribers.


== Life and career ==
Sharky was born Shamarke Mohamud in Utrecht, Netherlands, on 31 December 1995 to Somali parents and is the oldest of seven siblings. He later relocated to England and attended Oasis Academy Enfield and Harrow High School, before studying BTEC Level 3 Sport Science at Barnet and Southgate College and took part in a development squad for Tottenham Hotspur F.C.. He previously worked as a steward at Emirates Stadium, the home of the football club Arsenal F.C. which he supports, and in 2015, launched his YouTube channel under the name "Afcsharky", in reference to the club. He went on to upload various videos relating to football, as well as gaming and challenge videos.
In 2019, Sharky joined the Beta Squad, a British YouTube collective group, along with fellow YouTubers Chunkz, Niko Omilana, AJ Shabeel and King Kenny. In February of that year, the group lived together in a mansion in London, where they created daily content across social media platforms. The group operate a shared channel titled "Beta Squad" where they upload collaborative content and have amassed over 12 million subscribers. In 2020, he launched a podcast SDS, an acronym of "Sharky Does Sports", in which he chats with various guests about primarily football topics.
In 2023, Sharky appeared on an episode of the online series Get in the Van on Channel 4's online digital channel, Channel 4.0. The series follows teams of influencers using social media to scout the most suitable person to "get in the van" in an array of categories going head to head against hosts Spuddz and America Foster. Sharky, alongside Madame Joyce had to find someone with the hairiest chest. He also plays and manages a team SDS FC in the Baller League, with his team winning the inaugural UK league in June 2025.

articles.title: Matiur Rahman (tax official)
articles.text:
Matiur Rahman (tax official)

Matiur Rahman is a Bangladeshi civil servant who served as a member of the National Board of Revenue (NBR). In June 2024 he became the subject of media scrutiny and an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) inquiry into his wealth after his son purchased a 1.2 million taka goat. NBR officials have also said that he used his connections to prevent or reverse official transfers.


== Career ==
Rahman joined government service in the trade cadre in 1994 and was moved to the customs service on deputation in 1998. He served at several National Board of Revenue postings that many tax officials regard as lucrative. These included the Chittagong Custom House, the Benapole Custom House, the Large Taxpayer Unit, and the Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerates in Dhaka and Chattogram.
During the 2007 caretaker government, NBR chairman Badiur Rahman ordered Rahman's transfer from the Chittagong Customs House to the VAT Commissionerate in Rajshahi. In a television talk show in 2024, Badiur said that Rahman approached him at his office and at his home after the order was issued, and that he declined to meet him. Badiur also said that Bangladesh Army chief Moeen U Ahmed and three other army officers contacted him asking that the transfer be stopped. He said he refused to withdraw the order and told the army chief that he could be transferred himself instead. Badiur was subsequently moved to another post, and Rahman was back at the Chittagong Customs House within a month.
In February 2022, the government appointed Rahman to the board of directors of Sonali Bank. NBR officials said this was done without the consent of the NBR chairman or clearance from the tax authority. The officials said Rahman was one of 13 officials included in a routine round of transfers that year. The other 12 took up their new posts, but Rahman did not.
In July 2022, NBR chairman Abu Hena Md. Rahmatul Muneem ordered Rahman transferred from the Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal to the Rajshahi VAT Commissionerate. Rahman did not take up the post, and a new order cancelling the transfer was issued within 15 days. Several senior NBR officials, speaking anonymously, said Rahman had friends in influential positions, whom he hosted at resorts owned by him or his family. They attributed the cancellation of at least two transfer orders to these connections.

articles.title: Coleocephalocereus fluminensis
articles.text:
Coleocephalocereus fluminensis

Coleocephalocereus fluminensis is a species of succulent flowering plant in the genus Coleocephalocereus, within the family Cactaceae. It is endemic to southeastern Brazil.


== Description ==
Coleocephalocereus fluminensis is a species of cactus whose stems initially grow in a prostrate manner, but then turn upwards. The stems are dark green in color, branch at the base, and may reach 3 m in height and 10 cm in diameter.

This species has 5-17 straight ribs which are slightly divided into tubercles; the areoles are situated on top of the tubercles. The areoles have one central spine that is initially yellow-brown in color, but then changes to gray over time. There are 4-14 yellowish radial spines which also turn gray with age; these may measure up to 3 cm in length.
The flowers are off-white to light pink in color. They open at night and measure up to 7 cm in length. They develop from a woolly structure on the sides of the vertical stems called the pseudocephalium; this may measure up to 5 cm in width and 1 m in length. The pseudocephalium is made up of thick white wool and bristles, as well as many fine spines.
The fruits are thin and club-shaped. They are bright purple in color and measure 2-3 cm in length.


== Distribution and habitat ==
This species is native to southeastern Brazil, where it is found in eastern and southern Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, and northeastern São Paulo. It grows primarily in the seasonally-dry tropical biome.


== Taxonomy ==
Coleocephalocereus fluminensis was first described as Cereus fluminensis, a name published in 1838 by the Dutch botanist Friedrich Anton Wilhelm Miquel in the scientific journal Bulletin des Sciences Physiques et Naturelles en Neerlande 1: 48.
Later, the German botanist Curt Backeberg transferred this species to the genus Coleocephalocereus, renaming it Coleocephalocereus fluminensis. He registered these changes in the scientific journal Cactaceae. Jahrbücher der Deutschen Kakteen-Gesellschaft 1941 (2): 53, published in 1942.

Etymology
Coleocephalocereus: the genus name is derived from the Greek words koleon (meaning "veil" or "cover") and cephalé (meaning "head", in reference to the pseudocephalium from which the flowers develop), as well as from the Latin word cereus (meaning "candle"), in reference to the elongated straight growth form of this genus' stems.
fluminensis: the specific epithet is derived from the Latin name of Rio de Janeiro (Flumen Jan

articles.title: LulzSecPeru
articles.text:
LulzSecPeru

LulzSecPeru was a Peruvian hacker group active during the 2010s by @Cyber-Rat and @Desh501. Despite the name, the group has no ties to LulzSec, being much more related to  Anonymous. Known for their cyberactivism, it was considered "the region's most skillful and accomplished hacktivist team".
They were responsible for the 2014 e-mail leak known as "CornejoLeaks", that revealed several scandals from René Cornejo's government, ranging from environmental disregard in concessions to irregular use of police force for private purposes. Cornejo's government suffered a motion of no confidence and survived by one vote. Shortly after, the group ceased operations to avoid being prosecuted.


== Description ==
LulzSecPeru was created in the 2010s by @Cyber-Rat and @Desh501. The first was 17 years old, while the latter appeared to be between 19 and 21 years old and also to be a college student. They affirm to be autodidacts, learning how to program at 8 and 6 years old, respectively. Rat was more outgoing and responsible for most of the group's relationship with other cyberactivists and making their achievements public on social media, while Desh was more discreet and focused on the technical aspects of hacking.
Despite the name, the hacker group is not a branch of LulzSec. According to the creators, the name was chosen as "lulz is a way of laughing instead of crying. It's a laugh of shame and separation. It's schadenfreude".
The group is dedicated to hacking for mocking purposes against political targets and cyberactivism in Latin America, exposing the relations of the governments with corruption and illegal drug trade. They openly advocated for freedom of speech and government transparency. They have hacked the governments of Peru, Chile, Colombia, Argentina and Venezuela, and had the help of the hacker group Anonymous to publicize their actions. They've said to avoid hacking the United States government to escape being investigated by the FBI.


== Activities ==


=== Main attacks ===
In 2011, the group hacked the Ministry of the Interior of Peru, their first hacking in big proportions.
On 6 March 2012, the group hacked and defaced the Peru Police Information website. They've also intercepted e-mails from the Police to Facebook and discovered Evans Daniel Velásquez was the one responsible for neutralizing Anonymous profiles on the social media. According to the group, on this hack, they discovered they knew more about the police than the police knew ab

articles.title: Cussen Memorial
articles.text:
Cussen Memorial

The Cussen Memorial, sometimes called the Leo Cussen Memorial, is a memorial monument and family mausoleum located in the Roman Catholic section of the Boroondara General Cemetery, at 430–440 High Street in Kew, in the City of Boroondara, in the inner eastern suburbs of Melbourne, in Victoria, Australia. Built initially as a memorial to one family member, as of 1998, the mausoleum held the remains of ten members of the Cussen family.
Built during 1912 and 1913 on the traditional lands of the Wurundjeri people, the mausoleum was added to the Victorian Heritage Register on 11 March 2004 in recognition of its architectural and historical significance; and the cemetery was also added to a non-statutory list by the Victorian branch of the National Trust on 1 September 1997. 


== History ==
The Cussen Memorial is a mausoleum located within the Roman Catholic section of the Boroondara General Cemetery. The sandstone memorial is built in the Federation Gothic Revival style in the form of a small chapel with carvings, diamond shaped roof tiles and decorated ridge capping embellishing the exterior. The memorial occupies a landmark position within the cemetery. The Cussen Memorial was constructed in 1912–1913 by Sir Leo Cussen in memory of his son Hubert who died on 3 May 1911, aged 14 years. 
Sir Leo was appointed to the bench of the Supreme Court of Victoria in 1906, where he displayed the qualities which were to mark him, in the words of Sir Owen Dixon, as the 'greatest of all judges', combining legal expertise with great humanity and practicality. Sir Leo was considered by Sir Robert Menzies as 'one of the great judges of the English speaking world'. In addition to his duties as a judge, Cussen accepted responsibility for the consolidations of the Victorian Acts of Parliament, which took place in 1915, and again in 1929. In 1922, after four years of labour over centuries of English legislation, he presented to the Victorian Parliament the Bill for the Imperial Acts Application Act, which was passed without amendment. Cussen was elected president of the Melbourne Cricket Club in 1907, a position he would hold until his death in 1933. In 1916, Cussen was appointed as a trustee of the State Library of Victoria, the Victoria Museum, and the National Gallery of Victoria, including serving as president of the trustees from 1928.

articles.title: Contract labour system in Namibia
articles.text:
Contract labour system in Namibia

The contract labour system in Namibia was a system where black migrant workers from the north went to work in white areas under a contract. Until 1971/1972, workers could not leave without a reasonable reason as it was a criminal offence to do so. Several other work acts were also barred by criminal law, such as attempting to avoid work, doing it carelessly or having a second place of employment. They lived in poor conditions and were poorly paid. Women could not participate in the contract labour system.


== History ==
Contract labour existed during German rule, although Owambo, the region from which these migrant laborers came, was then independent. There were between 6000 to 12000 Ovambo workers present in German South West Africa each year between 1910 and 1914. Ovambo men notably went into contract to pay the taxes imposed by Europeans and to buy European goods, and because they could no longer collect minerals from regions that were now under white control.
Contract labour continued under South African rule, specifically in the north of Namibia. The homelands were unproductive areas, and thus almost all African workers in Namibia were migrant workers under the contract system migrating to white areas to find work. Africans in the north were only allowed to leave the bantustans to be workers under this system until 1979.
Before 1971, all employers except farmers had to obtain a permit from a local official to participate in the contract system. They then had to send the permit alongside a requisition for labor to the South West African Native Labour Associations (SWANLA), a semi-governmental association responsible for the recruitment of contract labourers. Future workers were classified in four different grades (A, B, C, "piccanins") depending on their physical condition, and had different minimum wages depending on their category, ranging from 3,75 rands/month ("piccanins"; juveniles under 15) to 8,69 rands/month (category A). Women were barred from the contract labour system.
The contract system led to a major strike in 1971/1972. As a result of the strike, the contract system changed completely. SWANLA was abolished and replaced by employment bureaux run by tribal authority. Normal working hours were instituted, and excess work was regarded as overtime. articles.title: Amy Israel
articles.text:
Amy Israel

Amy Israel is an American film and television executive and producer. She is currently the President of Television at Peter Chernin's North Road Company.


== Career ==
Before joining the North Road Company, she was the Executive Vice President of Original Programming for Showtime Networks.
Prior to joining Showtime Networks, Israel held leadership roles at New Regency Productions, Paramount Vantage, The Orphanage and Miramax Films. Israel founded Blum Israel Productions with producer Jason Blum.
She is a member of the Producers Guild of America. Israel is also an ambassador for ReFrame, an organization whose mission is to create a more gender-representative film and television industry on all levels. She is a member of Studio Advisory Board for Reboot Studios, an organization that provides seed investments to develop Jewish content.  Israel is also a member of Lunch Partners, a venture capital fund that invests in early stage companies.
As of 2026, Israel was named to the Peabody Awards board.


== Personal life ==
Israel was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. She is the daughter of Robert Israel and Ellen Israel, who ran the Kentshire Galleries in New York City, founded by her grandfather, dealing in period jewelry, vintage costume jewelry, and fine antique English furniture.
Her sister is Laurie Israel who is a three-time Daytime Emmy Award nominee for her work on children's television programming.
Israel graduated from Oberlin College with a major in Art History.
She lives in Los Angeles with her husband, RD Robb, and her two children.


== Recognition ==
The Hollywood Reporter named Israel to their Women in Entertainment Power 100 list first in 2007 during her tenure at Paramount Vantage and again in 2022 while at the helm of Showtime Networks.
CableFax named her one of the Most Powerful Women in 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022.
She was named one of Multichannel News Wonder Women in 2022.

articles.title: Movement on the Road '96
articles.text:
Movement on the Road '96

Movement on the Road '96 (Amazigh: Amussu xf Ubrid n 96; abbreviated MOR96) was a protest movement in the rural commune of Imider, in Tinghir Province, southeastern Morocco. Its participants campaigned over access to water, collective land rights, employment and the distribution of benefits from silver mining near their villages. 
The movement became known for a protest camp on Mount Alebban that lasted from August 2011 to September 2019. Protesters shut a valve on a pipeline serving the nearby Imiter silver mine and maintained a presence near the mine's water infrastructure.
The name referred to earlier protests in 1996, although local disputes over water extraction had begun during the 1980s. 
Researchers have studied the camp as a form of rural political mobilization, a site of community self-organization and a space for documenting the history of the dispute.


== Background ==


=== Silver mining and water use ===
The commune of Imider lies in a semi-arid part of southeastern Morocco along the N10 road between Ouarzazate and Errachidia. It includes seven villages whose residents include members of the Amazigh Ait Atta confederation. Agriculture and pastoralism have historically formed part of local livelihoods.
The nearby Imiter silver mine is operated by Société Métallurgique d'Imiter (SMI), part of the Managem mining group. The enterprise was established as a state-owned company and was privatized in the 1990s. Local farming has depended in part on a traditional underground water-collection and distribution system known as a khettara.
Residents accused SMI of excessive groundwater extraction, damage to agricultural land, pollution and a lack of local employment opportunities. Academic accounts have cited an estimate from the World Amazigh Congress that the mine used 1,555 cubic metres of water per day; the figure should be understood as an attributed estimate rather than an independently verified measurement. SMI disputed residents' allegations of environmental harm.


=== Earlier protests, 1986–2010 ===
In 1986, the drilling of the Targuit well near village farmland prompted protests and arrests. According to sociologist Zakia Salime, six men were sentenced to two months in prison.
In early 1996, residents held a sit-in by the N10 road near the Targuit well for approximately 45 days. Security forces dispersed the protest on 10 March 1996, and 23 people were arrested, according to Koenraad Bogaert and Soraya El Kahlaoui. Th

articles.title: Now TV (New Zealand)
articles.text:
Now TV (New Zealand)

Now TV (formerly Christchurch Television or CHTV) was a television station in Christchurch. It opened in 1997 by initiative of former Canterbury Television staff, and closed in 2002, merging with the aforementioned station.


== History ==


=== CHTV ===
CHTV was due to begin transmission in October 1997. Channel Seven Ltd., owner of Nelson's Mainland Television, which sought to bring back local television to Wellington, set up a joint-venture with the operating company, It inherited most of CTV's team, as the station joined the Family Television Network following the closure of TVNZ's Horizon Pacific Television, to which it was an affiliate.
CHTV started broadcasting on 3 November 1997, employing 15 staff. The weekday programmes would begin at 5:30pm with the news. It also aired programmes on sports, motoring and gardening. Among the station's non-news programmes was On Q, a youth magazine, and a three-hour programme on William Shakespeare, An Evening with Shakespeare, in April 1998. In December, it inked an agreement with the Canterbury Rugby Football Union to transmit Saturday matches from April 1998.
Sue Wells returned to host Canterbury Today on 24 April 1998 after two months of sick leave, replacing George Balani. The station was temporarily off air for three hours starting from 1pm on 20 May 1998, when a contractor cut the cable on Marleys Hill at the Port Hills. Overnight and during the morning, the channel aired Welcome to Canterbury (formerly on CTV), which in July 1998 was set to be screened all day as a closed-circuit channel on city hotels. The station broadcast the opening of the RDH Steel Technology Centre on 24 July. At the end of 1998, the station ran The Press Debate over a seven-week period.
The channel carried both the Canterbury Tennis Championships and the ASB Bank Trans-Tasman Challenge at Wilding Park on 18-19 January 1999. On 19-23 April, it aired Newsnight at 7:30pm, a pilot service produced by students of Christchurch Polytechnic's Broadcasting School. On 29 August, it aired St Andrew's performance of Romeo and Juliet.
The station had lost its profitability in 2000, as it had invested on a radio station on 1017 AM. By December of that year, it was airing Community Access Television on Sundays from 10am to 12pm.

articles.title: Adolph "Doc" M. Ferguson
articles.text:
Adolph "Doc" M. Ferguson

Adolphus Mallory "Doc" Ferguson (c. 1850s – April 1925) was an American entrepreneur, contractor, photographer, and civic figure in Key West, Florida. A native "Conch" born to a prominent local family whose wealth stemmed from the California Gold Rush, Ferguson engaged in a wide variety of island trades, including photography, dentistry, horse carriage operations, and concrete block manufacturing.
Ferguson owned and lived at 907 Whitehead Street from 1903 until his death in 1925. He lived there for 22 years between Asa Tift's ownership and its 1931 acquisition by author Ernest Hemingway.


== Early life and the Naval station expansion ==
Adolphus Ferguson was the youngest son of the Ferguson family of Key West, an influential merchant family that held extensive real estate along the island's harbor and inner residential streets. The main waterfront Ferguson family mansion on Front Street was acquired and condemned by the United States Navy in the early 1900s during the federal expansion of the Key West Naval Station, coal depot, and submarine base (now part of the Truman Annex).
Adolphus Ferguson resided at 218 Caroline Street, a property inherited through his mother, Rosalinda Ferguson. As the naval perimeter expanded around the waterfront and a wire wireless communications station was built toward Caroline Street, Ferguson sought a new primary residence, leading to his acquisition of the Tift estate.


== 907 Whitehead Street estate (1903–1925) ==
After original builder Asa Tift died in 1889, the estate at 907 Whitehead Street became entangled in 14 years of chancery litigation and probate disputes among out-of-state heirs. In 1898, the Monroe County Circuit Court appointed Ferguson as the legal custodian and caretaker to maintain the estate during the ongoing court proceedings.
When the court ordered a public partition auction in 1903 to settle the Tift estate, Ferguson purchased the property on the courthouse steps as the highest bidder. Relocating his household from Caroline Street, Ferguson maintained the native coral rock home and upkept the carriage house for his horses.
Locally known as "Doc," he worked as a photographer, artist, itinerant dentist, and horse-drawn carriage operator. He later co-founded Ferguson & Ward (with W. W. Ward), a local structural engineering and contracting firm located on Duval Street that manufactured structural concrete blocks for island construction projects.

articles.title: Heaven on Earth (workshop)
articles.text:
Heaven on Earth (workshop)

The Familial Iconography Workshop "HEAVEN ON EARTH" (Ukrainian: сімейна іконописна майстерня «НЕБО НА ЗЕМЛІ») is a religious art workshop based in Ukraine. It was founded by Priest Sergii Pavelko in 2004 in Mykolaiv. The workshop works in the field of contemporary icon painting, combining traditional icon-making techniques with the artists' own interpretations of Christian iconography and seeking new ways of presenting sacred imagery. In 2016, the workshop moved from Mykolaiv to Kyiv. Thus its works and exhibitions became known as Kyivan. The Ukrainian-language names "NEBO NA ZEMLI" and "IKONA" are trademarked by the workshop.


== History ==

The workshop was founded in Mykolaiv, Ukraine in 2004 with the initiative of Priest Sergii Pavelko. In its first years, its work was linked to the updating of traditional iconography and usage of ancient icon-making techniques. Publications regarding the workshop's activities noted that traditional materials and techniques were employed, and that icon painting was viewed not merely as an artistic craft but also as a form of spiritual contemplation of Christian images.
In 2007, the workshop presented the exhibition "May They All Be One" in Lviv, organized jointly with Ivanka Krypiakevych-Dymyd. The exhibition was held at the Andrey Sheptytsky National Museum of Lviv.
From 2008 to 2010, the workshop held exhibitions in Kyiv, including the Ivan Honchar Museum. In 2010, the "PER ASPERA AD ASTRUM" exhibition project was held in the museum. There, modern icons were shown in a dark environment. In 2011, the "Light in the Dark" exhibiton was hosted by the Lviv ICONART gallery. It tackles the concepts of dark and light with the works placed in a dark environment, and visitors viewed them using flashlights. The centerpiece of the project was "Christ – The Angel of the Great Counsel".

In 2013, the exhibition "Eternal Symbols" was held in Kyiv, featuring 54 icons from the workshop's collection. The exhibition included works created using various techniques, including original interpretations of the traditions of Ukrainian and international icon-painting schools. In 2014, the exhibition "Pokrov" (transl. The Protection of the Holy Virgin), dedicated to images of the Theotokos, was held at the Ivan Honchar Museum. The exhibition featured approximately 40 icons.

articles.title: Bus No. 53 (Bangkok)
articles.text:
Bus No. 53 (Bangkok)

Bus No. 53, currently designated Bus No. 2-9 (53) under the post-reform bus numbering system, is a bus route in Bangkok operated directly by the Bangkok Mass Transit Authority (BMTA). It is under the jurisdiction of Bus Operations District 6. The route is currently served by cream-and-red, non-air-conditioned Isuzu MT111QB buses, which entered service in 1991.
The route has a unique feature: it is the only bus route that operates in a circular loop around Phra Nakhon District and its neighboring districts, encompassing Rattanakosin Island, Bangkok's historic old city. The area is home to numerous important landmarks and historical sites, making Bus No. 53 a sightseeing route of sorts in Bangkok.


== Route ==
Bus No. 53 is divided into two services: a clockwise route and a counterclockwise route. Both services pass through each other's starting points, allowing passengers to travel on either route using a single ticket. As of 2026, the flat fare is 8 baht for the entire journey. The buses operate daily from 5:00 a.m. to 10:30 p.m.


=== Clockwise Route ===
The clockwise service begins at the bus terminal near Thewet Bridge. At each junction, the bus turns right, following a clockwise loop. Along the way, it passes several important landmarks, including Nang Loeng, Bobae and Mahanak markets, Debsirin School, 22 July Circle, Hua Lamphong railway station, Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park, Wat Traimit, Odeon Circle, Yaowarat Road (Bangkok's Chinatown), Sampheng Market, Phahurat, Pak Khlong Talat flower market, Maha Rat Road, Tha Tien, Wat Pho, the Grand Palace, Tha Chang, Tha Phra Chan, Thammasat University, Sanam Luang, the National Theatre, Phra Athit Road, Bang Lamphu, Wan Chat Bridge, Wisut Kasat Road, and the Bank of Thailand. The route then returns to its terminus at Thewet Bridge,  covering a total distance of 15.2 km (9.4 mi).


=== Counterclockwise Route ===
The counterclockwise service begins at Sanam Luang, near the Volunteer Soldiers Monument in front of the National Theatre. At each junction, the bus turns left, following a counterclockwise loop. The route passes Thammasat University, Tha Phra Chan, Maha Rat Road, Tha Chang, Wat Pho, the Grand Palace, Tha Tien, Wat Rajabopit School, the Territorial Defense Department's shooting range, Ban Mo, Wang Burapha, Saphan Lek, Woeng Nakhon Khasem, Khlong Thom, Chinatown along Charoen Krung Road, 22 July Circle, Phlapphla Chai Road, Wat Thep Sirin, Bobae, Mahanak and Nang Loeng

articles.title: 2026 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships – Women's 100 metre backstroke
articles.text:
2026 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships – Women's 100 metre backstroke

The women's 100 metre backstroke event at the 2026 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships was held on August 12 at the William Woollett Jr. Aquatics Center in Irvine, California. The event was won by reigning 50 metre backstroke world champion Katharine Berkoff of the United States in a time of 57.93, ahead of her compatriot and world record holder Regan Smith, who claimed the silver medal in 58.11. Canada's Taylor Ruck won the bronze medal in 58.40, while Australia's Iona Anderson finished fourth in 59.53.
Earlier in the morning heats, the United States recorded six of the eight fastest times, although only two swimmers from each nation were permitted to advance to the A final. Claire Curzan initially broke the championship record held by Canada's Kylie Masse with a personal best time of 58.21, improving on the previous mark of 58.29 set in 2018. Berkoff subsequently lowered the record to 58.09 before Smith established a new championship record of 57.86 in the following heat. Smith's time remained the championship record despite Berkoff winning the final. Curzan, who was unable to qualify for the A final due to the two-swimmers-per-nation restriction, subsequently won the B final in 58.24, a time that would have placed third in the A final.
